issue_title: Postgres node: a comma in a query-parameter value is split into several bind values
issue_description:
> **⚠️ Severity corrected after further testing.** An earlier version of this report
> claimed *silent data corruption*. That was wrong: I had verified n8n's value
> **collection** but not the value **binding**. Supplying the surplus value to
> PostgreSQL produces a hard error, not a wrong write. See the
> [correction comment](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/40022#issuecomment-5919564259).
> The code path and the fix suggestion are unchanged.

**Affected version:** 2.41.3 — and current `master`. The code is byte-identical in both
(verified against `n8n@2.41.3` and `master`: same statements, same line numbers).
**Node version:** `typeVersion` 2.5 and above, i.e. the current branch.
**Impact:** the query fails with a parameter-count error that does not point at the real
cause. No incorrect data is written.

## Summary

The Postgres node tells users to use `$1, $2, …` with **Query Parameters** to avoid SQL
injection. When a parameter's evaluated value is a **string containing a comma that is not
itself valid JSON**, the node splits that one value into several bind values. The
resulting parameter count no longer matches the statement, and execution fails with an
error that blames the *count* rather than the comma in the user's data.

## Affected code

`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Postgres/v2/actions/database/executeQuery.operation.ts`,
inside the `nodeVersion >= 2.5` branch (lines 106–108 in both 2.41.3 and `master`):

```ts
const evaluatedExpression = evaluateExpression(rawEvaluated);
const evaluatedValues = isJSON(evaluatedExpression)
    ? [evaluatedExpression]
    : stringToArray(evaluatedExpression);

if (evaluatedValues.length) values.push(...evaluatedValues);
```

`stringToArray` (`helpers/utils.ts`) is a comma split with empty filtering and trimming:

```ts
export function stringToArray(str: NodeParameterValueType | undefined) {
	if (str === undefined) return [];
	return String(str)
		.split(',')
		.filter((entry) => entry)
		.map((entry) => entry.trim());
}
```

So a single parameter whose evaluated value is `O'Brien, Test` contributes **two** bind
values instead of one.

## Why `isJSON()` does not save you

`evaluateExpression` (`helpers/utils.ts`) returns plain strings via `toString()` — it does
**not** JSON-encode them:

```ts
return typeof expression === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(expression) : expression.toString();
```

So `isJSON()` returns `true` only when the *data itself* happens to parse as JSON:

| evaluated value | `isJSON` | bind values produced | correct? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `123` | true | 1 | yes |
| `true` | true | 1 | yes |
| `Doe, John` | **false** | **2** | **no** |
| `O'Brien, Test` | **false** | **2** | **no** |
| `hello, world, again` | **false** | **3** | **no** |

This is why casual testing tends to pass: a numeric or boolean-looking value behaves
correctly, while ordinary free text does not. It is **data-dependent**, which is the most
dangerous shape for a bug in a form/webhook ingestion path.

## Reproduction

1. Add a **Postgres** node, operation **Execute Query**, with **Query Parameters** on.
2. Query: `SELECT $1::text AS a, $2::text AS b` — two placeholders.
3. Query parameters, in the node's `options.queryReplacement`:
   - `={{ $json.name }}`
   - `={{ $json.note }}`
4. Feed webhook/Code-node data: `{ "name": "Doe, John", "note": "hello" }`
5. Execute.

### Verified — value collection, using the node's own logic

`isJSON`, `evaluateExpression` and `stringToArray` copied verbatim from `helpers/utils.ts`,
plus the `nodeVersion >= 2.5` branch copied verbatim, mocking only `getResolvables()` and
the expression evaluator. Observed bind values:

```
no commas   {name:"Smith",      note:"hello"}                 -> ["Smith","hello"]           correct
comma in $1 {name:"Doe, John", note:"hello"}                 -> ["Doe","John","hello"]       3 values, 2 placeholders
3 params    {name:"Doe, John", note:"hello", city:"Galena"}   -> ["Doe","John","hello","Galena"]  4 values, 3
legacy <2.5 {name:"Doe, John", note:"hello"}                 -> ["Doe, John","hello"]         SAFE
array       {tags:["a","b","c"]}                             -> ["a","b","c"]                 #31704 fix present
```

### Verified — what the database then does

```
BEGIN;
CREATE TEMP TABLE reprobind (a text, b text);
PREPARE two (text, text) AS INSERT INTO reprobind VALUES ($1, $2) RETURNING a, b;
EXECUTE two('Doe', 'John', 'hello');
```
```
ERROR:  wrong number of parameters for prepared statement "two"
DETAIL:  Expected 2 parameters but got 3.
```

The driver rejects the surplus value; it does not drop it and does not shift the remaining
bindings.

**This can never be silent.** `stringToArray` splits on commas and filters empties, so a
value containing a comma can only ever *add* to the parameter count, never reduce it.
`values.length` is therefore always `>=` the number of expressions supplied, so the count
either overshoots the placeholders (*"Expected N but got M"*) or undershoots them (the
mirror error). It can never accidentally re-align.

## Note on the `nodeVersion < 2.5` branch

The older branch splits the **raw** parameter string (`rawReplacements.replace(/^=+/, '').split(',')`)
and then pushes each *evaluated* result **whole**:

```ts
for (const rawValue of rawValues) {
    const resolvables = getResolvables(rawValue);
    if (resolvables.length) {
        for (const resolvable of resolvables) {
            values.push(this.evaluateExpression(`${resolvable}`, index) as IDataObject);
        }
    } else {
        values.push(rawValue);
    }
}
```

Because the split is applied *before* evaluation, commas inside the **data** are safe
there. The hazard is in the newer branch, where the split is applied *after* evaluation.

## Relationship to #30978 / #31704

#30978 reported that a JS **array** was wrapped as a single bind value because of the same
`isJSON()` mismatch, and #31704 (merged 2026-06-04) fixed it by spreading arrays. That fix
handles `Array.isArray(rawEvaluated)` and does not change the `isJSON() ? … : stringToArray(…)`
path for **strings**, so the comma case described here remains. This looks like the
remaining half of the same underlying problem: the node cannot reliably distinguish "a
string that is one value" from "a comma-separated list of values".

## Suggested fix

Keep the ability to pass several literal parameters, but never split a value that came
from an expression. Concretely, in the `nodeVersion >= 2.5` branch, when the raw parameter
contained a resolvable, push the evaluated result as exactly one value, and reserve
`stringToArray` for parameters that are literal text with no `{{ }}`:

```ts
if (resolvables.length) {
    for (const resolvable of resolvables) {
        const rawEvaluated = this.evaluateExpression(`${resolvable}`, index);
        if (Array.isArray(rawEvaluated)) {
            for (const item of rawEvaluated) { /* unchanged */ }
            continue;
        }
        // an expression evaluates to exactly one value
        values.push(evaluateExpression(rawEvaluated));
    }
} else {
    values.push(...stringToArray(rawValues));
}
```

If comma-splitting of *literal* parameters must be preserved for backwards compatibility,
that is the branch to keep it in. The current behaviour appears to be unintentional: a
single expression is expected to yield a single bind value everywhere else in the node.

Happy to open a PR with tests if that is useful.

## Environment

- n8n 2.41.3, self-hosted
- Postgres node `typeVersion` 2.5
- Observed on a form/webhook ingestion workflow storing free-text customer input

issue_title: Agent Airspace: clear and resolution-advisory colours are indistinguishable for red-green colour blindness (1.01:1 luminance)
issue_description:
## Summary

In the Agent Airspace view, risk level is conveyed by colour alone, and the "clear" and "resolution advisory" colours have almost identical relative luminance. For an operator with red-green colour blindness, *all clear* and *collision imminent, steer now* are the same grey dot.

## The measurement

`scripts/lib/control-pane/proximity-viz.js:84-88`

```js
function riskColor(risk) {
  if (risk >= 0.7)  return '#ff7b72';   // resolution advisory (steer)
  if (risk >= 0.35) return '#e3b341';   // traffic advisory (transmit)
  return '#3fb950';                     // clear
}
```

WCAG relative luminance:

```
clear       #3fb950   L = 0.3633
traffic     #e3b341   L = 0.4895
resolution  #ff7b72   L = 0.3664

clear vs resolution  ->  contrast ratio 1.01:1
```

1.00:1 means indistinguishable by luminance. With deuteranopia or protanopia the hue channel is already unavailable, and here luminance offers no fallback. The amber "traffic" level is separable (L = 0.49), so the two that collapse into each other are precisely the two that matter most: the safe state and the urgent one.

Each colour passes contrast **against the background** individually (7.5:1 and 7.7:1 on `#0b0e14`), so a standard contrast check does not catch this. The problem is contrast *between the categories*.

## No textual alternative for the majority case

`proximity-viz.js:135-156` does render advisories as text in the side panel, including the level and risk percentage — good. But that only covers pairs already above the warning threshold. Agents in the **clear** state — normally most of them — appear nowhere as text: no table, no list, no per-point `aria-label`. For those, the canvas is the only source of information.

The canvas itself (`proximity-viz.js:56`) is `<canvas id="c"></canvas>` — no `role`, no `aria-label`, no fallback content between the tags. Verified in the browser: `role` and `aria-label` are both `null`.

## What the codebase already does better

`control-plane-view-ui.js:180-207` (`renderLanes()`) is the model: it lists every task with harness, state, file count and **risk as a text percentage**, for all tasks rather than only those over a threshold. The same approach in the proximity view would resolve the non-text-content gap.

## Suggested fix

1. Add a second visual channel so the three levels differ by more than hue — shape (circle / triangle / square), a ring, or a fill pattern per level.
2. Separate the palette by luminance as well as hue. Darkening the clear green or lightening the resolution red would give the two states distinct luminance.
3. Add a text list of agents with their risk percentage, matching `renderLanes()` in the 2D view.
4. Give the canvas `role="img"` and an `aria-label` summarizing the current state, with the list from (3) as the accessible alternative.

Items 1 and 2 help every operator on a dim screen or a projector, not only colour-blind users.

## Environment

- ECC 2.2.1, commit 07756cee
- Verified in browser at `/proximity` against a running `control-pane` server

issue_title: [Bug]: network failure (UND_ERR_SOCKET) — 'failing over' logged after run already terminated; fallback chain never executes, user gets error
issue_description:
## Bug type

Bug (something is broken)

## Beta release blocker

No

## Summary

Under a **network** failure (`Connection error` / `UND_ERR_SOCKET`) on the primary provider, the model fallback chain does **not** actually run, and the user sees `run failed before producing a reply` — even though the log line `transient retry window elapsed … failing over` appears. The failover decision is emitted **after** the embedded run has already been terminated with `isError=true`, so there is no run left to attach the fallback to.

In short: the failover arrives ~76ms too late; the run is already dead, the fallback candidates are never attempted, and the message fails with `outcome=error`.

## Timing evidence (single run, ms-level ordering)

```
.453  [provider-transport-fetch] error provider=opencode-go causeName=SocketError causeCode=UND_ERR_SOCKET fetch failed
.463  [agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: isError=true rawError="Connection error."
.539  [agent/embedded] transient retry window elapsed for opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash after 2/8 retries; failing over
.998  [diagnostic] message dispatch completed: source=replyResolver outcome=error
```

Note the order: the run is marked `isError=true` at `.463`, and only **76ms later** (`.539`) does the transient-retry observe the window is exhausted and emit `failing over`. The network error escapes as a terminal assistant message (empty content, `stopReason=error`) **before** the failover decision is produced, so laguna/deepseek/etc. are never called.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an HTTP/S provider whose streaming SSE occasionally drops mid-request (observed with `opencode-go`, baseUrl `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`).
2. Send any message that triggers a model call during such a drop.
3. Observe the log ordering above and a user-visible `run failed before producing a reply` / `network connection error`, with no fallback attempt logged between the failure and the terminal error.

## Expected

When the primary provider fails with a transient **network** error, the model fallback chain should be consulted and a fallback provider/model attempted before the run is surfaced as failed. The `failing over` decision should precede — or re-open — the run's terminal error state, not follow it.

## Actual

The network error is surfaced as a terminal assistant error immediately; `failing over` is logged afterward but has nothing to act on, so the fallback chain is effectively bypassed and the user receives the error.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.3 (also present in 2026.9.4)
- WSL2 (Ubuntu), gateway embedded run (`agent:main` dashboard session)
- provider `opencode-go` / `deepseek-v4.1-flash`

## Related issues (different trigger, same "fallback never/too-late engages" family)

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/145690 — runtime-level error burns through fallback chain, message dropped (non-network root cause)
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/142319 — content-class failure never engages fallback
- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141115 — 429 terminates session without consulting fallback

This report is distinct in that the trigger is a **network/transport error** and the failure mode is a **race**: the terminal-error state is emitted before the failover decision, independent of any single provider's error class.

issue_title: [FEATURE REQUEST]  Add Digit Dynamic Programming Template
issue_description:
### What would you like to Propose?

Add a generalized, production-grade template implementation of the **Digit Dynamic Programming** (Digit DP) technique along with a complete unit test suite under the `dynamicprogramming` package.

### Issue details

### Description
Digit Dynamic Programming (Digit DP) is an advanced algorithmic technique used to efficiently count or evaluate numbers within a range $[L, R]$ that satisfy specific digit-based constraints. 

Instead of an iterative brute force lookup, the approach evaluates numbers digit-by-digit from left to right (most significant to least significant) using a compressed search tree with memoization. This template tracks three critical architectural dimensions:
1. **Index (Position):** The specific digit placement currently being evaluated.
2. **Accumulated Property State:** The specific criteria tracking array (e.g., sum of digits, digit frequencies, parity matching).
3. **Tight Flag Matrix Constraint:** A binary state (`1` or `0`) specifying whether the current prefixes are bounded by the maximum prefix of the upper range parameter limit or are completely free to iterate from `0` to `9`.

Adding a clean, reusable boilerplate/template for Digit DP in the `dynamicprogramming` section will serve as a foundational study layout for students looking to learn state-transition constraints, state-compression arrays, branch pruning optimizations, and range query adjustments.

* **Core Logic:** `src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/dynamicprogramming/DigitDP.java`
* **Unit Testing Suite:** `src/test/java/com/thealgorithms/dynamicprogramming/DigitDPTest.java`

### Time & Space Complexity
* **Time Complexity:** $O(\text{Number of Digits} \times \text{State Array Size} \times 10)$ — Processing a $10^{18}$ boundary ceiling executes instantly within a fraction of a millisecond.
* **Space Complexity:** $O(\text{Number of Digits} \times \text{State Array Size} \times 2)$ — Bounded by the static allocation bounds of the memoization table grid.

The implementation will explicitly comply with the repository's build requirements:

3. **Checkstyle Compliance:** Variables, constants, and matrix definitions are completely isolated without loose magic constants or check violations.

#### Expected Calculation Yield:
* **Output Quantifier:** `6`
* **Valid Value Set:** `5`, `14`, `23`, `32`, `41`, `50`

### Additional Information

This feature bridges a major gap between standard dynamic programming problems (like knapsack or longest common subsequence) and digit state-compression techniques. It provides a generalized structure that developers and learners can study to understand advanced combinatorial enumeration and branch-pruning methods.

issue_title: boundImages recomputes the strip set per request — stripped images flip back to live and invalidate the prompt cache
issue_description:
## Summary

`boundImages()` (`packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts`, since v2.0.x) recomputes which inline images to strip **from scratch on every request**. When the history changes (a new image arrives, compaction prunes, tool output is truncated), the total image bytes move around the 25 MiB trigger and previously-stripped images **flip back to live**. That rewrites the prompt prefix at the oldest image's position, so every provider-side prompt cache behind it is discarded — in our case a ~300k-token conversation re-prefilled on every turn after a few screenshots were read, including plain-text turns.

## Evidence

With a local inference server that logs cache reuse, the divergence is exactly at the position of the first stripped image: consecutive requests alternate between the image payload and the `IMAGE_REMOVED` placeholder at the same token offset (`image_pad` vs placeholder text), and cache reuse collapses from ~99.9% to the system-prompt root each time. On our backend (strata, a custom llama.cpp-derived server with a conversation KV cache) this forces a **full re-prefill of the entire KV cache** — every turn after a few screenshots, including plain-text turns, pays ~300k tokens of prefill (~30–40 s) that the cache should have served.

## Why it's a bug, not a policy question

The strip policy (25 MiB trigger → 15 MiB target) is untouched. The issue is that the *decision* is non-monotonic: the same message renders differently across requests, which silently breaks prefix caching for every provider. A one-way decision fixes it without changing when stripping happens.

## Proposed fix

Make the strip decision sticky per image (content hash + occurrence index, so identical-but-distinct attachments stay distinct): once an image is replaced by the placeholder, it stays replaced for the process lifetime. Stripping still only starts above the trigger and winds down to the target.

```diff
commit 76a65c3b009c71d5d88e0819414ab8f78b787666
Author: hermes <hermes@local>
Date:   Mon Oct 5 15:09:49 2026 +0800

    fix(session): make boundImages stripping sticky per image
    
    Recomputing the strip set per request let a stripped image flip back to
    live whenever the history changed, rewriting the prompt prefix at the
    image position and discarding the provider prompt cache behind it. The
    decision is now one-way, keyed by content hash + occurrence.

index 26cecde..e5c8542 100644
--- a/packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts
+++ b/packages/core/src/session/model-request.ts
@@ -158,6 +158,32 @@ export const unsupportedParts = (messages: LLMRequest["messages"], capabilities:
     }),

+// Images already replaced by the placeholder in this process. Recomputing the strip set per request
+// let a stripped image flip back to live whenever the history changed (a new image, compaction, or
+// pruning moved the total back under the trigger), rewriting the prompt prefix at the image's position
+// and discarding the provider's prompt cache for the whole conversation behind it. The decision is
+// one-way: once stripped, an image stays stripped for the life of the process.
+const strippedImages = new Set<string>()
+
+// A stable identity for an image payload: mime, length, and sampled bytes. Identical bytes across
+// requests hash identically, so the sticky decision survives every rebuild of the request.
+const imageKey = (mime: string, sample: string, length: number) => {
+  let h = 0xcbf29ce484222325n
+  const s = `${mime}:${length}:${sample}`
+  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
+    h ^= BigInt(s.charCodeAt(i))
+    h = (h * 0x100000001b3n) & 0xffffffffffffffffn
+  }
+  return h.toString(16)
+}

+  if (media.source.type === "base64") return imageKey(media.mediaType, media.source.data.slice(0, 4096), media.source.data.length)
+  if (media.source.type === "bytes")
+    return imageKey(media.mediaType, media.source.data.subarray(0, 4096).toString("base64"), media.source.data.byteLength)
+  return imageKey(media.mediaType, media.source.type, 0)
+}
+

   const isImage = (mime: string) => mime.toLowerCase().startsWith("image/")
   // Remote and provider-referenced media carry no local payload and never count toward the inline budget.
@@ -166,33 +192,58 @@ export const boundImages = (messages: LLMRequest["messages"]) => {
     if (media.source.type === "bytes") return Math.ceil(media.source.data.byteLength / 3) * 4
     return 0
   }
-  const imageBytes = messages.reduce(
-    (total, message) =>
-      total +
-      message.content.reduce((sum, part) => {
-        if (part.type === "media" && isImage(part.media.mediaType)) return sum + size(part.media)
-        if (part.type !== "tool-result" || part.result.type !== "content") return sum
-        return (
-          sum +
-          part.result.value.reduce(
-            (bytes: number, item: Content) =>
-              bytes + (item.type === "file" && isImage(item.mime) ? Buffer.byteLength(item.uri) : 0),
-            0,
-          )
-        )
-      }, 0),
-    0,
-  )
-  if (imageBytes <= IMAGE_BYTES_TRIGGER) return messages
+  const uriSize = (uri: string) => Buffer.byteLength(uri)
+
+  // Identical payloads are distinct attachments, so each occurrence of a hash gets its own key.
+  const occurrence = () => {
+    const seen = new Map<string, number>()
+    return (base: string) => {
+      const n = seen.get(base) ?? 0
+      seen.set(base, n + 1)
+      return `${base}#${n}`
+    }
+  }
+
+  // Pass 1: bytes of the images still live - sticky-stripped ones no longer count.
+  let live = 0
+  const counted = occurrence()
+  for (const message of messages)
+    for (const part of message.content) {
+      if (part.type === "media" && isImage(part.media.mediaType)) {
+        if (!strippedImages.has(counted(mediaSample(part.media)))) live += size(part.media)
+      } else if (part.type === "tool-result" && part.result.type === "content") {
+        for (const item of part.result.value) {

+            live += uriSize(item.uri)
+        }
+      }
+    }
 
-  let removed = 0
-  return messages.map((message) =>
+  // Pass 2: rebuild. Sticky images stay placeholders; if still over the trigger, strip oldest-first
+  // down to the target and remember the decision.
+  if (live <= IMAGE_BYTES_TRIGGER && strippedImages.size === 0) return messages
+  let budget = live
+  let changed = false
+  const overTrigger = live > IMAGE_BYTES_TRIGGER
+  const shouldStrip = () => overTrigger && budget > IMAGE_BYTES_TARGET
+  const placed = occurrence()
+  const out = messages.map((message) =>
     Message.make({
       ...message,
       content: message.content.map((part) => {
-        if (part.type === "media" && isImage(part.media.mediaType) && imageBytes - removed > IMAGE_BYTES_TARGET) {
-          removed += size(part.media)
-          return Message.text(IMAGE_REMOVED)
+        if (part.type === "media" && isImage(part.media.mediaType)) {
+          const key = placed(mediaSample(part.media))
+          if (strippedImages.has(key)) {
+            changed = true
+            return Message.text(IMAGE_REMOVED)
+          }
+          if (shouldStrip()) {
+            strippedImages.add(key)
+            budget -= size(part.media)
+            changed = true
+            return Message.text(IMAGE_REMOVED)
+          }
+          return part
         }
         if (part.type !== "tool-result" || part.result.type !== "content") return part
         return {
@@ -200,15 +251,27 @@ export const boundImages = (messages: LLMRequest["messages"]) => {
           result: {
             ...part.result,
             value: part.result.value.map((item: Content) => {
-              if (item.type !== "file" || !isImage(item.mime) || imageBytes - removed <= IMAGE_BYTES_TARGET) return item
-              removed += Buffer.byteLength(item.uri)
-              return { type: "text" as const, text: IMAGE_REMOVED }
+              if (item.type !== "file" || !isImage(item.mime)) return item
+              const key = placed(imageKey(item.mime, item.uri.slice(0, 4096), item.uri.length))
+              if (strippedImages.has(key)) {

issue_title: npm 12 upgrade leaves the Windows executable stub
issue_description:
### Description

`opencode upgrade` can report success with npm 12 while leaving the published text stub in `bin/opencode.exe`. The next invocation fails on Windows because the file is not a valid executable.

The updater runs `npm install --global --force` without allowing the target package's lifecycle scripts. npm 12 can block postinstall and still exit 0, even with `ignore-scripts=false`. Adding `--allow-scripts=@opencode/cli` lets postinstall replace the stub.

I reproduced that policy behavior with a synthetic package in an isolated Windows install prefix using npm 12.0.2 and Node 24.21.0. The flag also preserved explicit `ignore-scripts=true`. This report covers the updater command; #48884 covers the broader packaging behavior when scripts are disabled.

### OpenCode version

issue_description:
### Description

GitLab Duo workflow models do not work correctly with a self-managed GitLab instance.

I found two issues while testing this:

1. Duo workflow models need the current working directory and GitLab project/namespace context.
2. If the stored GitLab OAuth token is expired and the refresh fails, provider initialization throws and can prevent OpenCode from starting.

I reproduced the OAuth failure with an expired credential where the refresh endpoint returned `invalid_grant`.

### Plugins

None

### OpenCode version

0.0.0-dev-202609112115

### Steps to reproduce

   ```powershell
   $env:GITLAB_INSTANCE_URL = "https://gitlab.example.com"
   $env:GITLAB_HOST = "https://gitlab.example.com"

2. Authenticate OpenCode with GitLab OAuth and configure GitLab Duo.

3. Start OpenCode using the GitLab Duo workflow model:
   ```powershell
   opencode -m gitlab/duo-workflow`

4. On a self-managed GitLab instance, start a GitLab Duo workflow and observe that the workflow does not receive the working directory and project/namespace context required for the current repository.

5. Let the stored GitLab OAuth credentials expire or make the refresh token invalid/revoked, then start OpenCode again.

6. OpenCode attempts to refresh the expired GitLab OAuth token. If GitLab returns `invalid_grant`, provider initialization throws and OpenCode can fail to start.

notFound() serves an empty `__next_error__` document instead of not-found.tsx
issue_description:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/franknoel/next-notfound-ssr

### To Reproduce

1. Clone the reproduction and run `npm install`.
2. Run `npm run build && npm run start` (`npm run dev` shows the same thing).
3. Run `./check.sh`, or fetch the pages by hand:

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:3000/missing        # page that calls notFound()
curl -s http://localhost:3000/no/such/route  # URL that matches no route
```

The app has three files: a root layout with `<html lang="en">`, an `app/not-found.tsx` that renders `NOT FOUND BOUNDARY`, and `app/[slug]/page.tsx`, which calls `notFound()` unless the slug is `known`.

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** `/missing` answers 404, but its HTML is `<html id="__next_error__"><head></head><body>` plus scripts. The root layout does not render, so there is no `lang` and none of the `not-found.tsx` markup. That markup exists only in the RSC payload, so the page is blank until it hydrates, and stays blank without JavaScript.

An unmatched URL (`/no/such/route`) is fine: it renders `not-found.tsx` inside the root layout.

`check.sh` output, the same on 16.3.6 and 16.4.0-canary.48, in `next dev` and in `next build && next start`:

```
/known           200  <html lang="en">             boundary/page text in HTML: yes
/missing         404  <html id="__next_error__">   boundary/page text in HTML: no
/no/such/route   404  <html lang="en">             boundary/page text in HTML: yes
```

**Expected:** `/missing` renders like `/no/such/route`: the root layout with `NOT FOUND BOUNDARY` in the server HTML, and the same 404 status.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: darwin
  Arch: arm64
  Version: Darwin Kernel Version 25.6.0: Tue Aug 18 17:49:13 PDT 2026; root:xnu-12377.161.15.700.19~2/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000
  Available memory (MB): 32768
  Available CPU cores: 10
Binaries:
  Node: 24.21.0
  npm: 11.19.0
  Yarn: 1.22.22
  pnpm: 9.15.9
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.3.6 // Latest available version is detected (16.3.6).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.2.8
  react-dom: 19.2.8
  typescript: 5.9.3
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Not Found, Error Handling

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next build (local), next start (local), Vercel (Deployed)

### Additional context

Also reproduces on `next@16.4.0-canary.48`, dev and prod.

Same bug as #98295 and #98954, which were closed automatically for lacking a reproduction link.

Where it seems to happen: `HTTPAccessFallbackBoundary` is a client error boundary, and React does not run error boundaries during server rendering, so the `notFound()` throw escapes the Fizz shell. The catch in `app-render` (`renderToStream`, and `prerenderToStream` for ISR) sets the 404 status and renders `getErrorRSCPayload`, whose seed is the hardcoded `__next_error__` document. Because the status and the empty document come from the same catch, an app cannot get a 404 with real HTML from `notFound()`.

We hit it on a site with locale-prefixed routes: every unknown page and event URL is served without `lang` or any text.

issue_description:

```

### Subsystem

http

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

Repository with reproduction - https://github.com/SuperOleg39/node-js-perf-problem-reproduction

About repo:

`server.js` - a http server with:
- `/`, `/test/` and `/unknown/` endpoinds with cpu-heavy work emulation
- 5 parallel request processing limit for this endpoints for event loop overload protection
- `/readyz` health check endpoint
- `/metrics` metrics endpoint
- `/`, `/test/` and `/unknown/` handlers wrapped in `setImmediate` to split heavy tasks by different event loop tasks

`server.test.js` - performance test case for this server:
- `autocannon` make a 1000 concurrent requests for 1 minute to server endpoints `/`, `/test/` and `/unknown/`
- in parallel run 5 seconds interval with request to `/readyz`

For reproduction, need to run `server.js` with different node.js versions, and run `server.test.js` for every try (more in repository README.md)

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

It works correctly at 16, 18 and 19 Node.js versions, but not works at 20 and 22 versions.

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

Event loop lag is small, incoming health check requests is processed fast, <500ms

### What do you see instead?

Event loop lag is small, but incoming health check requests is processed slowly, >10s

### Additional information

Hello!

We have a integration test for custom requests limiter, working on the principle of awesome [under-pressure](https://github.com/fastify/under-pressure) library - in summary with this requests limiter Node.js application can be responsive even under high load.

This test emulates a high load and endpoints with CPU-heavy work, and expects that fast requests to health checks or metrics will be processed almost immediately.

After update Node.js to v20 in our CI, we saw a failed test with very slow healthcheck responses.

I spend a few days to debug, and main results is:
- event loop is not overloaded, lag is less than 500ms (okay for this test)
- in CPU profile I can see microtasks between `setImmediate` calls
- but incoming `/readyz` requests start to be processed after 10-20 seconds
- problem somewere in core modules, because this lag starts from the request handler - `http.createServer(handler)` - and also deeper, event before internal `server.emit('request')` call.
- if we split healthchecks and metrics endpoints to different http server in the same Node.js process, it respond fast in all Node.js versions - one more confirmation that there is some queue at the level of a particular http server

issue_title: compress/zstd: add new package
issue_description:
Zstandard ([RFC 8878](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8878)) is well-positioned to replaced GZIP ([RFC 1952](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1952)) as the de-facto compression format.

Zstandard:
* is [faster to compress/decompress](https://facebook.github.io/zstd/#benchmarks) than GZIP,
* has [much better compression ratios](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/62446#issue-1880889127),
* is [well-specified](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8878), 
* is [backed by a prominent company](https://github.com/facebook/zstd), and 
* is seeing increased adoption in use with archives and as a [browser content encoding](https://chromestatus.com/feature/6186023867908096).
 
Given the likely ubiquitous place Zstandard is going have in the future, I propose first-class adoption of Zstandard in the stdlib.

Existing Go implementations:
* @klauspost has an excellent Zstandard implementation at [github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd), but the API is a somewhat complex and it makes use of native assembly.
* @ianlancetaylor implemented a Zstandard decompressor in [internal/zstd](https://github.com/golang/go/tree/master/src/internal/zstd) without any use of `unsafe` or assembly.

Some goals for this package:
* The API be simple and similar to existing packages like `compress/gzip`.
* It does not use `unsafe` or assembly similar to the existing compress package.
  * Performance is always nice, but Go community surveys consistently shows security as more important than performance.
  * Users who just need a decently fast enough Zstandard implementation can use `compress/zstd`, while those want the best performance and/or advanced features of Zstandard can use @klauspost's package. Any stdlib packages (e.g., `net/http` that make use of `compress/zstd` should make it possible to swap over to a different `zstd` implementation).
  * Note that the same is already true of `compress/gzip`, which is generally good enough (although there is still room for performance optimizations), but power users can use [github.com/klauspost/compress/gzip](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/klauspost/compress/gzip), which is much faster (as it makes use of assembly).

We could:
* adopt @klauspost's pure-Go (i.e., no assembly) implementation with a cleaned-up API
* extend @ianlancetaylor's work to support compressing
* do a combination of both

```

### What did you do?

- Check the [Add modules to workspace file](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Add_modules_to_workspace_file) section in the Go command documentation page (generated from [`src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L32-L34)):

  The documentation currently states:
  > A use directive will be added to the go.work file for each argument
  > directory listed on the command line go.work file, if it exists,
  > or removed from the go.work file if it does not exist.

- Verify the documented behavior with a sample workspace:

  ```shell
  # create workspace with three modules
  mkdir workspace && cd workspace
  mkdir a && cd a && go mod init a && cd ..
  mkdir b && cd b && go mod init b && cd ..
  mkdir c && cd c && go mod init c && cd ..
  go work init a b c

  # Case A: Argument directory exists and contains go.mod
  go work use a

  # Case B: Argument directory exists but does not contain go.mod
  rm b/go.mod
  go work use b

  # Case C: Argument directory does not exist on disk
  rm -r c   # in powershell: rm -Recurse c
  go work use c
  ```

### What did you see happen?

#### Case A (`go work use a`)

The `use a` directive is retained in `go.work` (exit code 0).

#### Case B (`go work use b`)

Even though the directory exists, the `use b` directive is **removed** from `go.work` (exit code 0) because removal is governed by the absence of `go.mod`, which is not mentioned in the documentation.

#### Case C (`go work use c`)

The documentation states that the directive will be removed from `go.work` if the argument directory does not exist. But the command fails with an error:

```shell
$ go work use c
go: directory c does not exist
go: open U:\workspace\c\go.mod: The system cannot find the path specified.
```

The command exits with exit code 1 without modifying `go.work`. The `use c` directive is **not** removed:

```text
go 1.22
use (
    a
    c
)
```

#### Summary

- **Documented behavior:** A `use` directive is added if the argument directory exists and removed if it does not exist.
- **Actual behavior:** A `use` directive is only removed when the argument directory exists on disk but does not contain a `go.mod` file (Case B). When an argument directory does not exist on disk (Case C), the command errors out and leaves `go.work` completely unmodified.
- **Typo:** [`"directory listed on the command line go.work file, if it exists"`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L33) has an extra `"go.work file"` after `"command line"`.

### What did you expect to see?

Expected either the documentation to accurately reflect the actual implementation (along with fixing the typo), or the implementation to match the documented behavior:

#### Proposed Solution

1. Fix the typo in [`src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L33) by removing the extra `"go.work file"` after `"command line"`.   

2. For the behavior discrepancy, either:

   - **Option A (Update documentation to match implementation):**
     Clarify that directives are added if the argument directory contains a `go.mod` file, or removed if it does not:

     ```diff
       A use directive will be added to the go.work file for each argument
     - directory listed on the command line go.work file, if it exists,
     - or removed from the go.work file if it does not exist.
     + directory listed on the command line, if it contains a go.mod file,
     + or removed from the go.work file if it does not.
     ```

     Regenerate `alldocs.go` via `go generate cmd/go`.

   - **Option B (Update implementation to match documentation):**
     Change `go work use` to drop the directive from `go.work` when the argument directory does not exist, rather than failing with `directory ... does not exist`.
     
     *(Note: `go work edit -dropuse=<dir>` is already available for removing directives without requiring the directory to exist on disk).*

3. The following related documentation pages in `golang/website` will also need to be updated with the revised description:
   - [Go Modules Reference: go work use](https://go.dev/ref/mod#go-work-use) (source: [`_content/ref/mod.md#L2846-L2848`](https://github.com/golang/website/blob/f2661d967b28530da480f0a1da9a4279026d34ca/_content/ref/mod.md?plain=1#L2846-L2848))
   - [Workspaces Tutorial: Learn more about workspaces](https://go.dev/doc/tutorial/workspaces#learn-more-about-workspaces) (source: [`_content/doc/tutorial/workspaces.md#L272-L274`](https://github.com/golang/website/blob/f2661d967b28530da480f0a1da9a4279026d34ca/_content/doc/tutorial/workspaces.md?plain=1#L272-L274), related issue: [#81779](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/81779))


### Analysis

Inspecting [`src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go`](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go) (function `workUse`) and verifying with runtime tests shows how each case is handled:

| Scenario | Command Behavior | Effect on `go.work` | Exit Code |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :---: |
| **Case A: Directory exists with valid `go.mod`** (`go work use a`) | `lookDir` finds `go.mod`, checks that it is regular, and records it in `keepDirs` ([L128](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L128)). | **Adds or keeps** the `use` directive via `wf.AddUse`. | `0` |
| **Case B: Directory exists, but has no `go.mod`** (`go work use b`) | `lookDir` encounters `os.IsNotExist` for `go.mod` and sets `keepDirs[absDir] = ""` ([L113](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L113)). | **Removes directive**. If `b` was in `go.work`, `wf.DropUse` removes it. | `0` |
| **Case C: Directory does not exist on disk** (`go work use c`) | Fails with `go: directory c does not exist` ([L138-L140](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L138-L140), [L227](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L227)). | **None**. Even if `c` was previously in `go.work`, the command exits before saving the file. | `1` |
| **Recursive flag** (`go work use -r <dir>`) | `<dir>` must exist. Subdirectories are walked recursively via `fsys.WalkDir`. | Adds directories containing `go.mod`. Drops directories without `go.mod`. Also **removes subdirectories under `<dir>` that previously existed in `go.work` but were deleted from disk** ([L178-L184](https://github.com/golang/go/blob/2ff5743d9fd52fac166225e75df0c2c1edf82abb/src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go#L178-L184)). | `0` |

### History

<details>
<summary>Click to expand related commit history</summary>

Tracing the history of `src/cmd/go/internal/workcmd/use.go`:

1. **Commit [`fdee1b297438`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/fdee1b297438a64c553ecc7468a7647f5a070404) (Oct 2021) — Initial implementation:**
   Originally, `lookDir` only checked `os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod"))` and did not validate whether `dir` itself existed on disk. If `dir` did not exist, `os.IsNotExist` matched and any matching directive in `go.work` was dropped without an error.

2. **Commit [`0c24038d22a8`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/0c24038d22a83c0da5feb3d700b13445f47b24c9) (Dec 2021) — Initial documentation:**
   The command documentation was added to reflect the initial behavior:
   > *"A use directive will be added to the go.work file for each argument directory listed on the command line go.work file, if it exists on disk, or removed from the go.work file if it does not exist on disk."*
   
   This commit also introduced the repeated phrase `"command line go.work file"`.

3. **Commit [`a84ef500213e`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/a84ef500213ef6c2a0e4bfd82253e9fcd28f1f62) (Mar 2022, fixes [#51749](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/51749)):**
   Added a check for regular files (`if target, err := fsys.Stat(useDir); err == nil && !target.IsDir()`). If `useDir` did not exist at all, `err != nil`, so execution still fell through to `lookDir(useDir)` (preserving silent removal for non-existent directories).

4. **Commit [`492c85ab84dc`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/492c85ab84dc1d4d19be0466d2d73f4a6174f07e) (Apr 2022, fixes [#51841](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/51841)):**
   Addressed an issue where `go work use -r does_not_exist` panicked with a nil pointer dereference inside `fsys.Walk`. `fsys.Stat(absArg)` was moved up front for all arguments:
   ```go
   info, err := fsys.Stat(absArg)
   if err != nil {
       if os.IsNotExist(err) {
           base.Errorf("go: directory %v does not exist", absArg)
       } else {
           base.Errorf("go: %v", err)
       }
       continue
   }
   ```
   Passing a non-existent directory argument became an error that halts execution via `base.ExitIfErrors()`. The command documentation was not updated at the time to reflect this change.

5. **Commit [`ce8146ed3361`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/ce8146ed3361f584ba79427ac6c6d6fe9c297bea) (Jun 2023):**
   Added toolchain switching and updated the documentation for Go versions and *"fails if any remaining use directives refer to modules that do not exist"*. The phrase `"if it exists on disk"` was shortened to `"if it exists"`, but the first sentence and the `"command line go.work file"` wording remained.

6. **Commit [`94982a07825a`](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/94982a07825aec711f11c97283e99e467838d616) (Jul 2024, fixes [#68245](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/68245)):**
   Clarified the `-r` flag description by removing the second clause (`"namely, use directives will be added for directories that exist, and removed for directories that do not exist"`). The first paragraph remained unchanged.

</details>

issue_description:
I would like to contribute a new design pattern to the repository:
**Generic Lazy-Holder Singleton Registry Pattern** — a hybrid design combining:

**1. Initialization-on-demand holder idiom** (best-practice JVM lazy-loading singleton)

**2. Generic Singleton Factory / Multiton Registry** (one singleton instance per class)

**3. Reflection-safe instance creation**

**4. Concurrent, thread-safe instance registry using computeIfAbsent**

This pattern provides a type-safe, lazy-loaded, per-class singleton registry that does not require external frameworks (like Spring) and works purely through Java language mechanisms.

issue_title: [Bug]: Hardcoded 1 GiB package-integrity limit blocks npm update to 2026.9.8
issue_description:
## Description

The OpenClaw updater refuses to activate a valid staged npm package when the package tree exceeds a hardcoded 1 GiB rollback-verification limit.

On a macOS arm64 npm-global installation, upgrading:

```text
2026.9.7 -> 2026.9.8
```

repeatedly failed with:

```text
Package rollback verification byte limit exceeded
```

The staged OpenClaw 2026.9.8 package is approximately 1.117 GiB by logical file size, while the integrity reader is hard-limited to exactly 1 GiB.

Temporarily changing that limit from 1 GiB to 2 GiB allowed the exact same update to complete successfully, including package activation, Gateway restart, version verification, channels-ready verification, and HTTP readiness.

## Environment

- Source OpenClaw: `2026.9.7 (c074824)`
- Target OpenClaw: `2026.9.8`
- Successful target build after workaround: `2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)`
- Installation method: npm global
- OS: macOS 27.0.1
- Architecture: arm64
- Node: Node 24 via Homebrew

## Relevant code

In the installed 2026.9.7 package:

```text
dist/package-update-integrity-BuKkfsLg.mjs
```

contains:

```js
const MAX_TREE_BYTES = 1073741824;
const MAX_TREE_ENTRIES = 5e4;
const MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES = 1048576;
const MAX_LAUNCHER_BYTES = 1048576;
```

The tree scanner uses `MAX_TREE_BYTES` while hashing package contents and throws:

```text
Package rollback verification byte limit exceeded
```

when the budget is exhausted.

## Reproduction

Run:

```bash
openclaw update --yes --accept-capabilities --timeout 1200
```

while upgrading npm-global OpenClaw 2026.9.7 to 2026.9.8.

## First failure before pruning the current installation

The original 2026.9.7 package itself was over 1 GiB because it contained native packages for unrelated architectures.

The updater failed with:

```text
Failed: validating
Failed: package-swap — Exit code: 1;
Baseline package scan failed |
Package rollback verification byte limit exceeded

Failing check package-swap (baseline-scan-failed)
```

## After pruning incompatible architecture packages

The current 2026.9.7 live tree was reduced to:

```text
files: 41,484
bytes: 737,667,175
MiB: 703.49
GiB: 0.687
```

After that change, the previous `baseline-scan-failed` condition disappeared.

However the update still failed later in `package-swap`:

```text
Failed: package-swap
Exit code: 1
Package rollback verification byte limit exceeded
```

This showed that the baseline package was now within the limit, but the new candidate/rollback verification was not.

## Candidate package size

A clean isolated global npm installation of OpenClaw 2026.9.8 was measured with the same global package layout:

```bash
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"

npm install -g \
  --prefix "$TMP" \
  --ignore-scripts \
  --no-audit \
  --no-fund \
  openclaw@2026.9.8
```

Result:

```text
files: 41,631
bytes: 1,199,336,837
MiB: 1,143.78
GiB: 1.117
```

Current integrity limit:

```text
1,073,741,824 bytes
1,024 MiB
1 GiB
```

The candidate therefore exceeds the integrity budget by:

```text
125,595,013 bytes
~119.78 MiB
```

## Update-run evidence

The recorded update run showed:

```text
updater-runtime-retention:
entries: 106,416
estimatedBytes: 1,664,008,192
linked: 92,984
copied: 3,221
```

The update successfully completed all of these stages before `package-swap` failed:

```text
package-install                    ✓
updater-runtime-retention          ✓
candidate-state-snapshot           ✓
candidate-doctor                   ✓
candidate-doctor-lint              ✓
candidate-config                   ✓
candidate-plugins                  ✓
candidate-recovery                 ✓
candidate-gateway-startup          ✓
candidate-state-cleanup            ✓
global update                      ✓
package-swap                       ✗
```

The recorded failure was:

```text
Package rollback verification byte limit exceeded
```

Recovery correctly restored/verified the original 2026.9.7 Gateway.

## Confirmed workaround

As a diagnostic test, only the integrity limit in the installed 2026.9.7 updater was changed:

```diff
- const MAX_TREE_BYTES = 1073741824;
+ const MAX_TREE_BYTES = 2147483648;
```

No other update logic was modified.

Then the same update command was executed again.

Result:

```text
OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)

update_rc=0
result=success
```

OpenClaw reported:

```text
✅ OpenClaw updated to 2026.9.8 (from 2026.9.7).

Package recovery: complete
Update: npm · up to date · npm latest 2026.9.8
```

Verification also completed successfully:

```text
service running
version verified
channels ready
HTTP ready
```

The update phases completed:

```text
requested
→ staging
→ validating
→ activating
→ restarting
→ verifying
→ finished
```

This strongly indicates that the 1 GiB integrity budget itself was the blocker.

## Expected behavior

The updater should be able to safely fingerprint and verify package trees produced by the supported OpenClaw npm-global installation mechanism.

A valid package generated by OpenClaw's supported installation/update path should not exceed a hardcoded integrity limit that causes the updater to reject its own candidate.

## Actual behavior

OpenClaw 2026.9.8 can produce a package tree larger than:

```text
MAX_TREE_BYTES = 1 GiB
```

and OpenClaw 2026.9.7's updater then refuses to activate it.

## Impact

The failure is deterministic and prevents a normal in-place update.

Because package install, candidate validation, Doctor checks, state snapshotting, Gateway candidate startup, and recovery all succeed before this check, the user spends several minutes in the update process before encountering an unavoidable package-swap failure.

## Possible fixes

A few possible approaches:

1. Increase `MAX_TREE_BYTES` to a value with reasonable headroom, e.g. 2 GiB or higher.
2. Make the limit configurable while retaining a safe default.
3. Derive the allowed fingerprint budget from the size of the staged package plus bounded headroom.
4. Stream/hash the tree without treating aggregate bytes as a fixed 1 GiB safety threshold.
5. Fix the separate packaging issue causing unrelated OS/architecture binaries to be installed, which would currently bring the package below the limit.

Even if the packaging issue is fixed, the updater should ideally not have a package-size ceiling lower than what supported OpenClaw installations can legitimately produce.

## Related issue

See #165602 for the separate npm-global packaging issue that installs native optional dependencies for unrelated OS/architectures and inflates the package by roughly 440–450 MiB.

issue_title: [utils] devalue: BigInt/RegExp/Map/null branches raise unhandled exceptions on malformed payloads, crash extractors
issue_description:
## Description

In `yt_dlp/utils/jslib/devalue.py`, the `BigInt`, `RegExp`, `Map` and `null` branches of `parse_iter` raise **unhandled exceptions** when their payloads are malformed, while every other type branch (`Date`, `ArrayBuffer`, typed arrays, `DataView`) catches errors and yields a `ValueError`/`IndexError`/`TypeError` for graceful handling.

Because `_resolve_nuxt_array` (`yt_dlp/extractor/common.py`) consumes `parse_iter` via `gen.send(None)` inside a loop that only catches `StopIteration`, these unhandled exceptions escape the error-handling path entirely and crash the extractor — instead of being turned into an `ExtractorError`/warning like other malformed devalue payloads.

## Reproduction

```python
from yt_dlp.utils.jslib import devalue

# These crash with unhandled exceptions:
devalue.parse([['BigInt', 'abc']])   # ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'abc'
devalue.parse([['BigInt', None]])    # TypeError: int() argument must be ...
devalue.parse([['RegExp', '[']])     # re.error: unterminated character set
devalue.parse([['RegExp', None]])    # TypeError: first argument must be string or compiled pattern
devalue.parse([['Map', 1, 2, 3]])    # ValueError: zip() argument 2 is shorter than argument 1
devalue.parse([['null', 'a', 1, 'b']])  # ValueError: zip() argument 2 is shorter than argument 1
```

The same class of malformed input in other branches is handled gracefully:

```python
devalue.parse([['Date', 'not-a-date']])              # ValueError: invalid date: 'not-a-date'
devalue.parse([['ArrayBuffer', 123]])                # ValueError: Invalid ArrayBuffer ...
devalue.parse([['Uint8Array', 99]])                  # ValueError: Invalid Uint8Array ... Invalid ArrayBuffer index
devalue.parse([['Uint8Array', 'AQID', 'x']])         # ValueError: Invalid Uint8Array ... Invalid byte offset
```

These yield errors are consumed by `_resolve_nuxt_array`'s loop (`yt_dlp/extractor/common.py`):

```python
gen = devalue.parse_iter(array, revivers={...})
while True:
    try:
        error_msg = f'Error resolving Nuxt JSON: {gen.send(None)}'
        ...  # graceful ExtractorError / warning path
    except StopIteration as error:
        return error.value
```

For the `BigInt`/`Map` cases above, `gen.send(None)` raises directly — the exception escapes the loop (only `StopIteration` is caught) and propagates out of the extractor, so a website returning malformed Nuxt devalue data crashes extraction instead of producing a graceful error.

## Root cause

`yt_dlp/utils/jslib/devalue.py`:

- `BigInt` branch: `result = int(value[1])` (no try/except)
- `RegExp` branch: `result = re.compile(value[1])` (no try/except)
- `Map` / `null` branches: `zip(*(iter(value[1:]),) * 2, strict=True)` raises on odd-length payloads (no try/except)

All other branches (`Date`, `ArrayBuffer`, typed arrays, `DataView`) wrap their work in `try/except` and `yield` the error, which is the established convention in this file.

`test/test_devalue.py`'s `TEST_CASES_INVALID` only covers malformed *top-level* input (empty string, ints, `None`, `{}`, `[]`, negative index) — no case feeds malformed arguments *inside* a typed branch, which is why this isn't caught.

## Impact

- Any extractor using `_resolve_nuxt_array`/`_search_nuxt_json` (Nuxt-based sites) crashes with an unhandled traceback on malformed devalue data instead of failing gracefully.
- Affects the latest release (2026.08.19) and master.

## Suggested fix

Wrap the `BigInt`, `RegExp`, `Map` and `null` branches in try/except and yield `ValueError(...)` with `result = None`, consistent with the `Date`/`ArrayBuffer`/typed-array branches — or catch in `parse_iter` uniformly.

issue_description:
### Checklist

- [x] I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
- [x] I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
- [x] I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
- [x] I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
- [x] I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates

### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

@echo off
chcp 65001 >nul 2>&1
setlocal EnableDelayedExpansion
title yt-dlp 视频下载器

:: ==========================================
::  配置区域
:: ==========================================
set "OUTPUT_DIR=.\Downloads"
set "FORMAT_ALL=bv*+ba/b"
set "FORMAT_AUDIO=ba"
set "QUAL_BEST=bv*+ba/b"
set "QUAL_1080=bv*[height<=1080]+ba/b[height<=1080]"
set "QUAL_720=bv*[height<=720]+ba/b[height<=720]"
set "QUAL_480=bv*[height<=480]+ba/b[height<=480]"
set "DEFAULT_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:3067"
set "CONF_FILE=%~dp0yt-dlp_proxy.conf"
:: ==========================================

:: 读取代理配置(首次运行自动写入默认值)
if exist "%CONF_FILE%" (
    for /f "usebackq delims=" %%A in ("%CONF_FILE%") do (
        set "PROXY=%%A"
        goto :EOF_FOUND
    )
    :EOF_FOUND
    if /i "!PROXY!"=="off" set "PROXY="
) else (
    set "PROXY=!DEFAULT_PROXY!"
    echo !PROXY!> "%CONF_FILE%"
)

:: 检查 yt-dlp.exe
if not exist "%~dp0yt-dlp.exe" (
    echo [错误] 未找到 yt-dlp.exe！请放在同一目录。
    pause & exit /b 1
)

:: 检查 ffmpeg
set "FFMPEG_FOUND=1"
where ffmpeg >nul 2>&1 || (
    if exist "%~dp0ffmpeg.exe" (set "FFMPEG_FOUND=1") else (set "FFMPEG_FOUND=0")
)

:: 创建输出目录
if not exist "%OUTPUT_DIR%" mkdir "%OUTPUT_DIR%"

:INPUT
cls
echo ============================================
echo          yt-dlp 视频下载器
echo ============================================
echo.
echo 输出目录: %OUTPUT_DIR%
if "!PROXY!"=="" (
    echo 代理: [未启用-直连]
) else (
    echo 代理: !PROXY!
)
if "!FFMPEG_FOUND!"=="0" (
    echo [!] 未检测到 ffmpeg，合并/转码功能不可用
) else (
    echo [✔] ffmpeg 已就绪，支持音视频合并/转码
)
echo.
echo [0] 设置/修改代理
echo 提示: 直接按回车退出 ^| 输入 q 也可退出
echo --------------------------------------------
set "URL="
set /p "URL=请输入视频网址 (输入0设置代理): "

if "!URL!"=="" goto EXIT
if /i "!URL!"=="q" goto EXIT
if "!URL!"=="0" goto SET_PROXY

:: 输入自定义文件名
echo.
set "CUSTOM_NAME="
set /p "CUSTOM_NAME=请输入文件名称 (如 快乐崇拜): "

if "!CUSTOM_NAME!"=="" (
    echo [错误] 文件名不能为空！
    pause >nul
    goto INPUT
)

:: 选择画质
echo.
echo 请选择画质:
echo   [1/回车] 最高画质(自动)
echo   [2]      1080p
echo   [3]      720p
echo   [4]      480p
echo   [5]      仅音频(直接下载)
echo --------------------------------------------
set "QUAL_CHOICE="
set /p "QUAL_CHOICE=请输入选项 (1-5, 默认1): "

if "!QUAL_CHOICE!"=="" set "QUAL_CHOICE=1"

set "FMT="
set "SORT_ARG="
set "QUAL_LABEL="
set "SKIP_MODE=0"

if "!QUAL_CHOICE!"=="1" (
    set "FMT=!QUAL_BEST!"
    set "QUAL_LABEL=最高画质"
) else if "!QUAL_CHOICE!"=="2" (
    set "FMT=!QUAL_1080!"
    set "SORT_ARG=-S res:1080"
    set "QUAL_LABEL=1080p"
) else if "!QUAL_CHOICE!"=="3" (
    set "FMT=!QUAL_720!"
    set "SORT_ARG=-S res:720"
    set "QUAL_LABEL=720p"
) else if "!QUAL_CHOICE!"=="4" (
    set "FMT=!QUAL_480!"
    set "SORT_ARG=-S res:480"
    set "QUAL_LABEL=480p"
) else if "!QUAL_CHOICE!"=="5" (
    set "FMT=!FORMAT_AUDIO!"
    set "QUAL_LABEL=仅音频"
    set "SKIP_MODE=1"
) else (
    echo [警告] 无效选项，已自动使用最高画质
    set "FMT=!QUAL_BEST!"
    set "QUAL_LABEL=最高画质"
)

if "!SKIP_MODE!"=="1" (
    set "EXTRA_ARGS=-x --audio-format mp3"
    set "MODE_NAME=仅音频"
    set "OUT_TEMPLATE=%OUTPUT_DIR%\!CUSTOM_NAME!.DJ.%%(ext)s"
    goto START_DOWNLOAD
)

:: 选择下载模式
echo.
echo 请选择下载模式:
echo   [1/回车] 仅下载音频 → !CUSTOM_NAME!.DJ.mp3
echo   [2]      合并音视频 → !CUSTOM_NAME!.!QUAL_LABEL!.MV.mp4
echo --------------------------------------------
set "CHOICE="
set /p "CHOICE=请输入选项 (1=音频, 2=合并, 回车默认音频): "

if "!CHOICE!"=="" set "CHOICE=1"

set "EXTRA_ARGS="
set "MODE_NAME="
set "OUT_TEMPLATE="

if "!CHOICE!"=="2" (
    if "!FFMPEG_FOUND!"=="0" (
        echo.
        echo [错误] 未安装 ffmpeg，无法合并！请先安装 ffmpeg 或选择其他选项。
        pause >nul
        goto INPUT
    )
    set "EXTRA_ARGS=--merge-output-format mp4"
    set "MODE_NAME=合并音视频"
    set "OUT_TEMPLATE=%OUTPUT_DIR%\!CUSTOM_NAME!.!QUAL_LABEL!.MV.%%(ext)s"
) else if "!CHOICE!"=="1" (
    set "FMT=!FORMAT_AUDIO!"
    set "SORT_ARG="
    set "EXTRA_ARGS=-x --audio-format mp3"
    set "MODE_NAME=仅音频"
    set "OUT_TEMPLATE=%OUTPUT_DIR%\!CUSTOM_NAME!.DJ.%%(ext)s"
) else (
    echo [警告] 无效选项，已自动使用默认值[仅音频]
    set "FMT=!FORMAT_AUDIO!"
    set "SORT_ARG="
    set "EXTRA_ARGS=-x --audio-format mp3"
    set "MODE_NAME=仅音频(默认)"
    set "OUT_TEMPLATE=%OUTPUT_DIR%\!CUSTOM_NAME!.DJ.%%(ext)s"
)

:START_DOWNLOAD
echo.
echo [信息] 画质: !QUAL_LABEL!
echo [信息] 模式: !MODE_NAME!
if "!PROXY!"=="" (
    echo [信息] 代理: 未启用(直连)
) else (
    echo [信息] 代理: !PROXY!
)
echo [信息] 开始解析并下载...
echo --------------------------------------------

if "!PROXY!"=="" (
    "%~dp0yt-dlp.exe" ^
        -f "!FMT!" ^
        !SORT_ARG! ^
        !EXTRA_ARGS! ^
        -o "!OUT_TEMPLATE!" ^
        --no-playlist ^
        --windows-filenames ^
        --restrict-filenames ^
        --console-title ^
        --newline ^
        --progress ^
        "!URL!"
) else (
    "%~dp0yt-dlp.exe" ^
        -f "!FMT!" ^
        !SORT_ARG! ^
        !EXTRA_ARGS! ^
        --proxy "!PROXY!" ^
        -o "!OUT_TEMPLATE!" ^
        --no-playlist ^
        --windows-filenames ^
        --restrict-filenames ^
        --console-title ^
        --newline ^
        --progress ^
        "!URL!"
)

echo.
if !errorlevel! equ 0 (
    echo [✔ 成功] !MODE_NAME! 下载完成！
) else (
    echo [✘ 失败] 出错代码: !errorlevel!
)

echo --------------------------------------------
echo 按任意键继续下载下一个...
pause >nul
goto INPUT

:: 代理设置
:SET_PROXY
cls
echo ============================================
echo              代理设置
echo ============================================
echo.
echo 当前代理: !PROXY!
echo 配置文件: %CD%\yt-dlp_proxy.conf
echo.
echo 说明:
echo   - 直接回车: 保持当前设置不变
echo   - 输入新地址: 如 http://127.0.0.1:7890
echo   - 输入 socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 可改用SOCKS5
echo   - 输入 off: 关闭代理(直连下载)
echo --------------------------------------------
set "NEW_PROXY="
set /p "NEW_PROXY=请输入代理地址: "

if "!NEW_PROXY!"=="" (
    echo [信息] 保持原设置: !PROXY!
) else if /i "!NEW_PROXY!"=="off" (
    set "PROXY="
    echo off> "%CONF_FILE%"
    echo [✔] 已关闭代理(直连模式)
) else (
    set "PROXY=!NEW_PROXY!"
    echo !PROXY!> "%CONF_FILE%"
    echo [✔] 代理已更新为: !PROXY!
)

echo.
pause
goto INPUT

:EXIT

echo 已退出下载器。

issue_title: DOCX math: a boxed formula (`<m:borderBox>`) and everything inside it are dropped
issue_description:
When a Word equation contains a border box (`<m:borderBox>`), MarkItDown drops the element and all of its content without any warning. An equation that is boxed as a whole converts to an empty `$$$$`.

Word writes `<m:borderBox>` for its "Boxed Formula" equation structure.

## Repro

```python
from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET
from markitdown.converter_utils.docx.math.omml import OMML_NS, oMath2Latex

M = f'xmlns:m="{OMML_NS[1:-1]}"'

def latex(xml):
    return oMath2Latex(ET.fromstring(f"<m:oMath {M}>{xml}</m:oMath>")).latex

e_mc2 = ("<m:r><m:t>E=m</m:t></m:r><m:sSup><m:e><m:r><m:t>c</m:t></m:r></m:e>"
         "<m:sup><m:r><m:t>2</m:t></m:r></m:sup></m:sSup>")

print(repr(latex(f"<m:borderBox><m:borderBoxPr><m:ctrlPr/></m:borderBoxPr>"
                 f"<m:e>{e_mc2}</m:e></m:borderBox>")))
# -> ''

print(repr(latex("<m:r><m:t>a+</m:t></m:r>"
                 "<m:borderBox><m:e><m:r><m:t>b</m:t></m:r></m:e></m:borderBox>"
                 "<m:r><m:t>=c</m:t></m:r>")))
# -> 'a+=c'
```

End to end: I added a paragraph with a boxed `E=mc^2` to a copy of `tests/test_files/equations.docx`, placed between the paragraphs `BEFORE` and `AFTER`. `MarkItDown().convert()` returns `BEFORE\n\n$$$$\n\nAFTER`.

## Expected vs actual

| Input | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `<m:borderBox>` around `E=mc^2` | `\boxed{E=mc^{2}}` | `''` |
| `a+` `<m:borderBox>b</m:borderBox>` `=c` | `a+\boxed{b}=c` | `a+=c` |

ISO/IEC 29500-1 says `borderBox` (Border-Box Object) "specifies the Border Box object, consisting of a border drawn around an instance of mathematical text (such as a formula or equation)". Its children are an optional `borderBoxPr` and one `e` that holds ordinary math content. When `borderBoxPr` is omitted, the default is a full rectangular border. The [Open XML SDK `BorderBox` reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.math.borderbox) reproduces this text. Dropping the `e` content loses document text silently. At minimum the content should be kept, and `\boxed{...}` is the direct LaTeX equivalent of a full border.

## Cause

In `packages/markitdown/src/markitdown/converter_utils/docx/math/omml.py`, `oMath2Latex.tag2meth` has no entry for `borderBox`, and `__direct_tags` lists `box` but not `borderBox`. `process_unknow` returns `None` for the tag, so `process_children_list` skips the element together with its children.

## Suggested fix

Add a `do_borderbox` handler that renders `process_children_dict(elm).get("e", "")` as `\boxed{...}`, with the template in `latex_dict.py`. It must not require `<m:borderBoxPr>`. The `hide*` and `strike*` flags in `borderBoxPr` (partial borders, strike lines) have no direct LaTeX equivalent, so ignoring them and emitting `\boxed{}` covers Word's default "Boxed Formula".

## Environment

- markitdown `main` at 1f9530a (0.1.8)
- Python 3.13, macOS

I have a fix and a regression test ready on a branch and will open the PR for this myself.

issue_title: PDF: one form-like page makes the rest of the document interleave two-column text
issue_description:
### Summary

When `PdfConverter` finds at least one page that looks like a form or table, it extracts **every other page** with pdfplumber's `page.extract_text()`. That call reads straight across both columns of a two-column layout, so the prose pages come out interleaved. If no page looks like a form, the whole document goes through pdfminer, which reads each column top to bottom.

So the reading order of page 1 depends on whether page 11 has a table.

### Reproduction

A synthetic PDF, generated with reportlab: two pages of two-column prose ("Article 1." … "Article 24.") plus, in the second file, one extra page with a 4-column grid.

| File | Article order from `markitdown` | Order inversions |
|---|---|---:|
| two-column pages only | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, … 24 | 0 |
| same pages + one form-like page | 1, 7, 2, 8, 3, 9, 4, 10, … | 10 |

`pdftotext` reads both files in order.

On a real document (an 11-page, two-column law in Spanish, 40 articles; only its last page is detected as form-like), `markitdown` 0.1.8 gives 8 order inversions; pdfminer on the same pages gives 1.

### Where

`packages/markitdown/src/markitdown/converters/_pdf_converter.py`, around lines 552-574 (commit `1f9530a`):

- if `form_page_count == 0`: `pdfminer.high_level.extract_text(pdf_bytes)` for the whole document;
- otherwise: plain pages use `page.extract_text()` (pdfplumber), joined with `"\n\n"`.

`plain_page_indices` is filled in that loop but never used, which suggests the plain pages were meant to be handled separately.

### A fix, and its trade-off

I have a small patch ready: keep the form pages as they are, and re-extract the plain pages with one pdfminer pass (`extract_text(..., page_numbers=plain_page_indices)`, split on `\f`), keeping the pdfplumber text if that pass fails. It fixes the reproduction (10 → 0 inversions) and the real document (8 → 1), passes the existing PDF tests, and adds a regression test.

It is not free, which is why I'm asking before opening a PR:

- Mixed documents get pdfminer's known weaknesses on their plain pages, the same ones pure-prose documents already get today: unexpanded ligatures (`ﬁ`), rotated watermarks one letter per line, and some table-like pages collapsing into long lines.
- On a 208-page mixed PDF, conversion time goes from ~16 s to ~25 s (the same cost as the prose path); memory is unchanged.
- It touches the same block as several open PRs (#2576, #2556, #1902, #2491, #2562).

Two options I can see:

1. Plain pages always through pdfminer (the patch above), i.e. the same policy the prose path already has.
2. Keep pdfplumber for plain pages, but pass layout-aware options or detect multi-column pages before choosing.

Happy to open the PR for whichever you prefer. The reproduction script (reportlab) is below.

Related but separate: page markers (#1304, #2272).

### Environment

markitdown 0.1.8 (main @ `1f9530a`), pdfminer.six 20251230+, pdfplumber 0.11.10, Python 3.14, macOS.

<details><summary>Reproduction script</summary>

```python
"""Minimal repro: a two-column PDF reads in order, until one form-like page is added."""
import re, sys
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
from markitdown import MarkItDown

W, H = A4
FILLER = "This paragraph is long enough to wrap across several lines of its column so that the two columns run side by side on the page."

def column(c, x, y, first, last):
    for n in range(first, last + 1):
        c.setFont("Helvetica-Bold", 10); c.drawString(x, y, f"Article {n}."); y -= 14
        c.setFont("Helvetica", 9)
        words, line = FILLER.split(), ""
        for w in words:
            if c.stringWidth(line + " " + w, "Helvetica", 9) > 200:
                c.drawString(x, y, line.strip()); y -= 12; line = ""
            line += " " + w
        c.drawString(x, y, line.strip()); y -= 22

def build(path, with_form_page):
    c = canvas.Canvas(path, pagesize=A4)
    art = 1
    for _ in range(2):  # two pages, two columns, 6 articles per column
        column(c, 50, H - 60, art, art + 5); column(c, 320, H - 67, art + 6, art + 11)
        art += 12; c.showPage()
    if with_form_page:  # one page that looks like a form/table to the heuristic
        c.setFont("Helvetica", 10)
        for r in range(12):
            for k, x in enumerate((50, 200, 350, 470)):
                c.drawString(x, H - 80 - r * 18, f"{'Field' if k == 0 else 'Value'}{r}-{k}")
        c.showPage()
    c.save()

def order(md):
    seen = []
    for n in map(int, re.findall(r"Article (\d+)\.", md)):
        if n not in seen: seen.append(n)
    return seen

for flag in (False, True):
    p = f"repro_{'with' if flag else 'without'}_form_page.pdf"
    build(p, flag)
    s = order(MarkItDown().convert(p).markdown)
    print(f"{p}: {s}  -> {sum(b < a for a, b in zip(s, s[1:]))} order inversions")
```
</details>

issue_title: PPTX: one unrecognized shape type aborts the whole presentation
issue_description:
A single shape whose type `python-pptx` can't identify makes MarkItDown fail the entire PPTX, losing every slide.

### Repro

Convert a deck containing an unrecognized shape (docling ships one: [`powerpoint_unrecognized_shape.pptx`](https://github.com/docling-project/docling/blob/main/tests/data/pptx/sources/powerpoint_unrecognized_shape.pptx), slide 2 has a shape named `BadShape`). It raises and returns nothing, though the other two slides are ordinary:

```
PptxConverter threw NotImplementedError with message: Shape instance of unrecognized shape type
```

`PptxConverter` reads `shape.shape_type` (in `_is_picture`, `_is_table`, and the group-shape check); for an unmapped shape that access raises and propagates out of `convert()`.

### Expected

One unreadable shape should be skipped and the rest of the deck converted, in the same spirit as the tolerance fixes already merged for `PptxConverter`: #2059 (tolerate `None` shape/notes text), #2194 (chart title without a text frame), and #2408 (top-zero sort).

The PR is written and tested; it adds a small `_shape_type_or_none()` helper that returns the type or `None` on `NotImplementedError`, so the shape falls through as "none of the handled types" and its own text is still recovered.

issue_title: markitdown-ocr: OCR text is matched to DOCX images by position instead of identity
issue_description:
# markitdown-ocr: OCR text is matched to DOCX images by position instead of identity markitdown-ocr 0.1.0, `packages/markitdown-ocr/src/markitdown_ocr/_docx_converter_with_ocr.py`, checked against `main` @ `b752951`. `DocxConverterWithOCR` decides which OCR result belongs to which image by counting, not by looking at the image. That works only when `doc.part.rels` yields the image relationships in the same order the body uses them. In documents that have been edited over time it often doesn't, and then the descriptions end up under the wrong pictures. The markdown is still well formed, so nothing errors out and the problem is easy to miss. ## The code `_inject_placeholders`, line 206: ```python def replace_img(match: re.Match) -> str: # type: ignore[type-arg] for i in range(len(ocr_texts)): if i not in used: used.append(i) return f"

{_PLACEHOLDER.format(i)}

" return "" # remove image if all OCR texts already used result = re.sub(r"]*>", replace_img, html) ``` `replace_img` receives the matched `` tag and never reads it. For every image in the body it hands out the next OCR text that hasn't been used yet. Those texts come from `_extract_and_ocr_images`, line 172: ```python for rel in doc.part.rels.values(): if "image" in rel.target_ref.lower(): ... ocr_map[rel.rId] = ocr_result.text.strip() ``` ## Reproduction [repro_markitdown_ocr.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31824993/repro_markitdown_ocr.py) builds its own documents and calls no external service. The OCR service is a stub that returns a marker derived from the image bytes, so you can see which text ended up under which image. ``` pip install markitdown markitdown-ocr python-docx pillow python repro_markitdown_ocr.py ``` Case B makes a document with 12 distinct images, then rewrites `word/document.xml` so the body walks them in reverse while the relationships keep their original order. It's a shortcut to what happens on its own in a document whose images have been moved, inserted or deleted. ``` === B. same 12 images, body order != relationship order === images in the document body : 12 OCR blocks produced : 12 blocks in the right place : 1/12 ``` I also hit this on a real business document, an internal SAP manual I can't attach: 19 distinct images, referenced 20 times in the body since one is reused. Every one of the 20 positions was wrong. The relationships came out as `rId13, rId18, rId26, rId21, ...` while the body used them as `rId11, rId12, rId13, ...`. ## Why the current tests don't catch it The fixtures in `packages/markitdown-ocr/tests/ocr_test_data/` have at most three images: | fixture | images | | --- | --- | | `docx_image_start/middle/end.docx` | 1 | | `docx_complex_layout.docx` | 1 | | `docx_multiple_images.docx` | 2 | | `docx_multipage.docx` | 3 | With a few images added in sequence, relationship order and body order are the same, so the positional matching happens to give the right answer. [check_fixtures.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31824991/check_fixtures.py) runs the check over a directory of `.docx` files and they all pass. Case C of the repro script recreates those conditions and passes too. ## Possible fix Match on image content rather than position. mammoth inlines images as base64 data URIs without re-encoding them, so the digest of the decoded bytes identifies each image. On the document above, all 20 `` tags resolved to the right relationship by SHA-256, including both occurrences of the reused image. Roughly: ```python # _extract_and_ocr_images: key the map by content digest instead of rId digest = hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest() # _inject_placeholders: resolve each through its own data URI def replace_img(match): data_uri = re.search(r'src="data:[^;]+;base64,([^"]+)"', match.group(0)) if not data_uri: return "" digest = hashlib.sha256(base64.b64decode(data_uri.group(1))).hexdigest() text = ocr_map.get(digest) ... ``` This also handles an image used more than once in a document. Right now each occurrence consumes a different OCR text; with a content lookup they all get the same one. I can send a PR if this looks like the right direction. There's a second, unrelated bug in the same converter that shows up on documents with eleven or more images. I've filed it separately.
