issue_title: Refresh under an intercepted modal falls back to an MPA navigation when the background page is itself interceptable (Next-Url sent on the reused route's refresh request)
issue_description:
### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

https://github.com/scheinkman-roberto/next-interception-refresh-repro

### To Reproduce

1. `npm install`, then `npm run dev` (or `npm run build && npm start`).
2. Open `http://localhost:3000/photo` directly, so the Photo **page** is rendered by a document load.
3. Click **Settings (interceptable)** in the nav. The Settings **modal** (`@modal/(.)settings`) opens over the Photo page.
4. Inside the modal, click **router.refresh()** — or **Server Action with revalidatePath**.

Control: repeat with `http://localhost:3000/plain` in step 2 (a page with no intercepting twin).

### Current vs. Expected behavior

**Current:** after step 4 the browser loads a new document at `/settings`: the "Document loaded at" stamp (`performance.timeOrigin`) changes, the modal is gone, and the Settings *page* is shown. Any client state on the background page and in the modal is lost.

**Expected:** the background page and the modal are refreshed in place, without replacing the document. That is what happens in the control: over `/plain`, both buttons re-render the background and the modal and the stamp does not change.

Requests in the failing case:

```
GET /photo                 document
GET /settings?_rsc=…       opens the modal (intercepted)
GET /settings?_rsc=…       refresh, primary request
GET /photo?_rsc=…          refresh, separate request for the reused background route
GET /settings              document  <- MPA fallback
```

The separate refresh request is sent with `Next-Url: /photo`. `/photo` has an interception rewrite whose only condition is `next-url` matching `/.*`, so the server answers with the **intercepted** tree instead of the page tree:

| `GET /photo` with `RSC: 1` | Response |
|---|---|
| no `Next-Url` | page tree ("Photo PAGE"), `Vary` without `next-url` |
| `Next-Url: /photo` | `@modal/(.)photo` tree ("Photo MODAL"), `Vary` with `next-url` |

The client then finds a mismatch inside an inactive parallel route and falls back to an MPA navigation.

### Provide environment information

```bash
Operating System:
  Platform: win32
  Arch: x64
  Version: Windows 11 Pro
  Available memory (MB): 16123
  Available CPU cores: 8
Binaries:
  Node: 24.18.0
  npm: 11.16.0
  Yarn: N/A
  pnpm: N/A
Relevant Packages:
  next: 16.4.0-canary.59 // Latest available version is detected (16.4.0-canary.59).
  eslint-config-next: N/A
  react: 19.3.0
  react-dom: 19.3.0
  typescript: 7.0.2
Next.js Config:
  output: N/A
```

### Which area(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

Parallel & Intercepting Routes

### Which stage(s) are affected? (Select all that apply)

next dev (local), next start (local)

### Additional context

- Reproduced with this repository on **16.4.0-canary.59**, in `next dev` (Turbopack) and in `next build && next start`. First seen in a real app on **16.3.5** (dev and production build); 16.3.8 ships the same code path, but I did not run it.
- The trigger is the background page being *itself* an interceptable route that was rendered as a page — which only happens after a document load (reloading while a modal is open, opening a link directly, an OAuth return). It does not depend on shared segments or route groups.
- Any revalidation triggers it: `router.refresh()`, or a Server Action that calls `revalidatePath` (for any path), since both refresh all dynamic data.
- It is self-perpetuating in an app where most detail screens are intercepted modals: after the fallback the user is on another interceptable page, and the next modal over it fails the same way.

**Suspected cause.** The refresh request for a reused "default" slot is sent with the *current* `Next-Url`, and the code already has a TODO about it. In canary this is `packages/next/src/client/components/render-tree.ts` (in 16.3.x, `router-reducer/ppr-navigations.ts`):

```js
refreshRequestPromises.push(fetchMissingDynamicData(…, new URL(refreshUrl, location.origin),
  // TODO: Just noticed that this should actually the Next-Url at the
  // time the refresh URL was set, not the current Next-Url. Need to
  // start tracking this alongside the refresh URL. In the meantime,
  // if a refresh fails due to a mismatch, it will trigger a
  // hard refresh.
  nextUrl, …))
```

Here the background page was rendered by a document load, so the `Next-Url` "at the time the refresh URL was set" is none — and without the header the server would return the page tree.

Things that do not work around it from application code (tried on 16.3.5):

- Stripping `Next-Url` in `proxy.ts` for that request: the `_rsc` cache-busting param no longer matches the headers, the server answers 307, and the client goes into a retry loop.
- Revalidating a narrower path, or calling `router.refresh()` instead of `revalidatePath`: same refresh, same header.

Our workaround is to never keep an intercepted modal open over an interceptable page (we detect it with `useSelectedLayoutSegments()` for both slots in the layout and load the requested route as a page instead).

Possibly related, but with a different cause (a stale refresh URL, plain parallel routes): #99444 / #99460.

issue_title: /v1/chat/completions ignores max_tokens AND overrides the Modelfile num_predict default, leaving generation unbounded
issue_description:
## Summary

Ollama's OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint does not bound generation. It ignores
`max_tokens` in the request **and** overrides a model's own `num_predict` default from its
Modelfile, so there is no way to bound a response through that endpoint. Since the server
processes one request at a time by default, a single unbounded generation blocks every
subsequent request indefinitely.

Version: ollama 0.34.0 (Homebrew, arm64, macOS 26.6). Model: llama3.1:8b.

## Reproduction

Identical prompt, no cap in either request, against a model with a Modelfile ceiling:

```
FROM llama3.1:8b
PARAMETER num_predict 4096
PARAMETER temperature 0.0
```

Native endpoint — ceiling honored:

```
curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate \
  -d '{"model":"capped-llama","prompt":"Count from 1 to 400, one number per line.","stream":false}'
→ eval_count 804, done_reason "stop"
```

OpenAI-compatible endpoint — ceiling overridden, no response:

```
curl -s --max-time 300 http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"capped-llama","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count from 1 to 400, one number per line."}]}'
→ no response in 300s; server log shows n_gen = 30,576 and still climbing
```

Sending an explicit cap does not help either:

```
-d '{"model":"llama3.1:8b","max_tokens":20,"messages":[...]}'
→ no response in 60s; n_gen past 3,150
```

while the native equivalent (`options.num_predict: 20`) returns `eval_count 8-20` every time.

## Impact

Any client that speaks the OpenAI protocol to Ollama inherits an unbounded generation it cannot
cap from either side — not by request parameter, not by model default. With single-slot serving,
one runaway wedges the queue and the symptom presents as "the server is slow" rather than as an
error. In our case a knowledge-extraction pipeline appeared to hang for two hours; the actual
state was one request at 160,000+ tokens with everything else queued behind it.

## Expected

`/v1/chat/completions` should honor `max_tokens`, and in its absence should fall back to the
model's `num_predict` rather than overriding it with unlimited.

## Related

#2723 (max_tokens via the OpenAI library appears non-functional) and #12779 (native API should
accept max_tokens as an alias for num_predict) both touch this area; neither covers the Modelfile
default being overridden, which is what removes the last available workaround.

Happy to test a fix or provide server logs.

issue_title: An operand placed before the mnemonic in a display section is printed as its table name
issue_description:
**Describe the bug**

If a constructor's display section puts an operand ahead of the mnemonic, the
operand is not resolved. It is printed literally as the name of its sub-table, and
it becomes the instruction's mnemonic as far as `getMnemonicString()` is concerned.

Both of these compile without complaint:

```
:"ADD" guard  is opc=1 & guard { ... }     # renders  ADD r2     — correct
:guard "ADD"  is opc=2 & guard { ... }     # renders  guard ADD  — wrong
```

The second one should render `r2 ADD`. Instead the text `guard` is emitted, and
`getMnemonicString()` returns `"guard"` rather than `"ADD"`.

This matters for ISAs where an operand genuinely precedes the mnemonic in the
vendor's syntax. The case I ran into is predicated execution in NVIDIA SASS, where
the vendor disassembler prints

```
@!P0  LDG  R4, [R6]
```

The `@!P0` guard leads the mnemonic on roughly 12% of instructions in the corpus I
measure against. There is no way to render that in SLEIGH: put the guard first and
you get the sub-table's name, put it anywhere else and the operand order no longer
matches the vendor's. The only remaining option is to not display it at all and
model predication purely in p-code, which is what the module does now — but it
means the disassembly is missing information that is present in the encoding.

ARM's condition codes and Hexagon's predicates are handled by folding the
condition into the mnemonic (`ADDEQ`), which works when the set of conditions is
small and known. It does not generalise to a guard that names one of N predicate
registers plus a negation bit.

I could not find a way to do this with `^` concatenation either, since the problem
is the position of the operand rather than the spacing around it.

**To Reproduce**

1. `leadop.slaspec`:

   ```
   define endian=little;
   define alignment=1;
   define space ram      type=ram_space       size=4 default;
   define space register type=register_space  size=4;

   define register offset=0 size=4 [ r0 r1 r2 r3 ];

   define token instr(8)
     opc  = (0,3)
     psel = (4,5)
   ;

   attach variables [ psel ] [ r0 r1 r2 r3 ];

   guard: psel is psel { export psel; }

   # (A) operand after the mnemonic
   :"ADD" guard  is opc=1 & guard { r0 = r0 + guard; }

   # (B) same operand before the mnemonic
   :guard "ADD"  is opc=2 & guard { r0 = r0 + guard; }
   ```

2. `sleigh -e leadop.slaspec` — compiles clean, no warning about (B).

3. Disassemble the two bytes `21 22` (opc=1 then opc=2, both with psel=2, so the
   operand is `r2` in each case):

   ```
   21    mnemonic='ADD'      full='ADD r2'
   22    mnemonic='guard'    full='guard ADD'
   ```

**Expected behavior**

`22` should render as `r2 ADD`, with `getMnemonicString()` returning `"ADD"`.

Failing that, I would settle for the compiler rejecting the construct. Compiling
a display section into text that names an internal symbol is worse than refusing
it, because the spec looks correct and the problem only shows up in the listing.

**Screenshots**

N/A, headless.

**Attachments**

The spec above is complete and self-contained; it needs only a minimal
`.ldefs`/`.pspec`/`.cspec` to load.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (kernel 5.15.0-190)
 - Java Version: OpenJDK 21.0.12
 - Ghidra Version: 12.1.3 (build 2026-Aug-17)
 - Ghidra Origin: official GitHub distro

**Additional context**

If this is a documented restriction I could not find it — the SLEIGH documentation
describes the display section as a mnemonic followed by operands, but does not say
what happens if you write it the other way, and the compiler accepts it. Saying so
explicitly in the docs, and rejecting it in the compiler, would be a smaller change
than supporting it and would still have saved me the investigation.

issue_title: Decompiler: equates on constant arguments of user-defined p-code ops (CALLOTHER: `swi`, `out`, etc) are not displayed
issue_description: **Describe the bug** Equates applied to constants that are passed to user-defined p-code ops (CALLOTHER) are not shown in the decompiler output; the raw value is printed instead. This happens both when the equate is set in the Listing and when it is set from the decompiler (right-click → Set Equate). This looks like a remaining case of [#336](https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/issues/336). That issue was closed in 9.0.4, but its own example (`INT INT_DISP` still decompiling as `swi(0x12)`) still reproduces with a DOS `INT 21h`. **To Reproduce** 1. Import the attached `poc.exe` (MS-DOS EXE, language `x86:LE:16:Real Mode`) and run auto-analysis. Alternatively, open the attached `.gzf`, which already has the equates applied. 2. Go to `FUN_1000_0170`. 3. In the Listing, set equates: - `1000:0171 MOV AL,0x20`: operand `0x20` → `PIC_EOI` - `1000:0173 OUT 0x20,AL`: operand `0x20` → `PIC_MASTER_CMD` - `1000:017a INT 0x21`: operand `0x21` → `DOS_INT` 4. Look at the decompiler output. 5. In the decompiler, right-click the `0x21` in `swi(0x21)` → Set Equate → `DOS_INT`. The output does not change. Listing: ``` ************************************************************** * FUNCTION * ************************************************************** undefined __cdecl16near FUN_1000_0170() assume CS = 0x1000 assume DS = 0x1040 undefined FUN_1000_0170 XREF[1]: entry:1000:0100(c) 1000:0170 90 NOP 1000:0171 b0 20 MOV AL,PIC_EOI AL = COPY 32:1 1000:0173 e6 20 OUT PIC_MASTER_CMD,AL CALLOTHER "out", 32:1, AL 1000:0175 90 NOP 1000:0176 b0 00 MOV AL,0x0 AL = COPY 0:1 1000:0178 b4 4c MOV AH,0x4c AH = COPY 0x4c:1 1000:017a cd 21 INT INT_DOS $U78e00:4 = CALLOTHER "swi", 33:1 CALLIND $U78e00:4 ``` Decompiler output: ```c void __cdecl16near FUN_1000_0170(void) { code *pcVar1; out(0x20,0x20); pcVar1 = (code *)swi(0x21); (*pcVar1)(); return; } ``` **Expected behavior** ```c out(PIC_MASTER_CMD,PIC_EOI); pcVar1 = (code *)swi(DOS_INT); ``` **Screenshots** **Attachments** - [poc.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32623330/poc.zip): contains `poc.exe`, a minimal POC with no third-party code - [poc.gzf.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32623457/poc.gzf.zip): contains `poc.gzf` exported program with the equates applied - [FUN_1000_0170.xml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32623329/FUN_1000_0170.xml): decompiler debug output (Decompiler window → Debug Function Decompilation) **Environment** - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 - Java Version: 21.0.10 - Ghidra Version: 12.1.3 **Additional context** The `swi` case is the simplest one. In the p-code, the constant `33:1` is a direct input of the CALLOTHER op in the same instruction that carries the `DOS_INT` equate, so no propagation is involved. The equate is still not displayed. For `out`, the port constant is on the `OUT` instruction itself, while the value comes from `AL`, loaded by the preceding `MOV AL,PIC_EOI`. Neither equate is displayed, and setting either one from the decompiler (right-click → Set Equate) has no visible effect. The problem seems specific to CALLOTHER arguments. Related: #336

issue_title: Reorganize the catch-all `others/` and `misc/` packages into thematic packages
issue_description:
### Description

The [`others/`](https://github.com/TheAlgorithms/Java/tree/master/src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/others) (35 files) and [`misc/`](https://github.com/TheAlgorithms/Java/tree/master/src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/misc) (15 files) packages have grown into dumping grounds: they hold unrelated algorithms that already have a natural home elsewhere in the project. This makes algorithms hard to discover and encourages duplicates (e.g. a graph algorithm landing in `others/` instead of next to the other graph algorithms).

### Examples of misplaced files

| File | Better home |
| --- | --- |
| [`others/Dijkstra.java`](https://github.com/TheAlgorithms/Java/blob/master/src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/others/Dijkstra.java), [`others/PageRank.java`](https://github.com/TheAlgorithms/Java/blob/master/src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/others/PageRank.java) | `datastructures/graphs/` |
| [`others/Huffman.java`](https://github.com/TheAlgorithms/Java/blob/master/src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/others/Huffman.java) | `compression/` |
| `others/CRC16.java`, `others/CRC32.java`, [`others/CRCAlgorithm.java`](https://github.com/TheAlgorithms/Java/blob/master/src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/others/CRCAlgorithm.java) | a dedicated `checksums/` package |
| [`misc/TwoSumProblem.java`](https://github.com/TheAlgorithms/Java/blob/master/src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/misc/TwoSumProblem.java), [`misc/ThreeSumProblem.java`](https://github.com/TheAlgorithms/Java/blob/master/src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/misc/ThreeSumProblem.java), [`others/TwoPointers.java`](https://github.com/TheAlgorithms/Java/blob/master/src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/others/TwoPointers.java) | a shared two-pointer/array-problems package |

### Proposed change

Move the files into the packages they belong to (updating package declarations, imports and test locations) and, ideally, retire `others/` and `misc/` entirely so there is no longer an "everything else" bucket.

This is purely a reorganization — no algorithm behavior changes.

issue_title: Google Sheets node evaluates Document and Sheet for the first input item only
issue_description:
### Bug Description

In the Google Sheets node (v2, node versions 4.x), the **Document** and **Sheet** resource locators are evaluated **once, against the first input item only**. Every other parameter of the operation (options, filters, range, columns) is evaluated per item.

So when the Sheet field is an expression like `{{ $json.sheet }}` and the node receives several items, the node silently uses item 0's sheet for all of them. For *Get Row(s)* on node versions > 4.1, the node loops over the input items (one read per item) but every iteration reads the same tab. There is no error and no execution hint, so the wrong data goes downstream unnoticed. The expression editor preview shows the per-item values correctly, which makes this harder to spot.

Root cause (same code on `master` and on the 2.39.10 tag):

- `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Sheet/v2/actions/router.ts` reads `documentId` and `sheetName` with item index `0` and resolves the sheet a single time before dispatching the operation:
  https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/4a01756ea453bc7cbdbc869968315934f76e800b/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Sheet/v2/actions/router.ts#L23-L49
- `sheet/read.operation.ts` then loops over all input items (for node version > 4.1) with that one `sheetName`:
  https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/4a01756ea453bc7cbdbc869968315934f76e800b/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Sheet/v2/actions/sheet/read.operation.ts#L179-L195
- while `utils/readOperation.ts` reads `options`, `filtersUI.values` and `combineFilters` per `itemIndex`:
  https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/4a01756ea453bc7cbdbc869968315934f76e800b/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Sheet/v2/actions/utils/readOperation.ts#L23-L89

This keeps coming up on the forum, where it is answered with workarounds (Split Out, Loop Over Items with batch size 1, Switch per sheet) rather than reported:
- https://community.n8n.io/t/google-sheets-get-rows-only-uses-first-dynamic-sheet-name/295060
- https://community.n8n.io/t/dynamic-expressions-wont-work-in-google-sheet-node/201479

### To Reproduce

1. Take a spreadsheet with two tabs that have different columns, e.g. `Channels Data` (16 rows) and `Posts Log` (188 rows).
2. Build: Manual Trigger → Code node returning two items `{ sheet: 'Channels Data' }` and `{ sheet: 'Posts Log' }` → Google Sheets **Get Row(s)**, Document by ID, Sheet **By Name** = `{{ $json.sheet }}`.
3. Execute.

Result on n8n 2.39.10, tested with node versions 4.5 and 4.6:

| Input items (in order) | Output items | Rows came from |
|---|---|---|
| `Channels Data`, `Posts Log` | 32 | `Channels Data` only (16 rows, read twice) |
| `Posts Log`, `Channels Data` | 376 | `Posts Log` only (188 rows, read twice) |

Swapping the order of the two input items changes which tab is read, and the second item's tab is never read in either case.

Workflow (replace the document ID and credential):

```json
{
  "nodes": [
    { "parameters": {}, "name": "When clicking ‘Execute workflow’", "type": "n8n-nodes-base.manualTrigger", "typeVersion": 1, "position": [0, 0] },
    { "parameters": { "jsCode": "return [{ json: { sheet: 'Channels Data' } }, { json: { sheet: 'Posts Log' } }];" }, "name": "Emit sheet names", "type": "n8n-nodes-base.code", "typeVersion": 2, "position": [220, 0] },
    { "parameters": { "documentId": { "__rl": true, "mode": "id", "value": "YOUR_SPREADSHEET_ID" }, "sheetName": { "__rl": true, "mode": "name", "value": "={{ $json.sheet }}" }, "options": {} }, "name": "Get rows", "type": "n8n-nodes-base.googleSheets", "typeVersion": 4.6, "position": [440, 0], "credentials": { "googleSheetsOAuth2Api": { "id": "YOUR_CREDENTIAL_ID", "name": "Google Sheets account" } } }
  ],
  "connections": {
    "When clicking ‘Execute workflow’": { "main": [[{ "node": "Emit sheet names", "type": "main", "index": 0 }]] },
    "Emit sheet names": { "main": [[{ "node": "Get rows", "type": "main", "index": 0 }]] }
  }
}
```

### Expected behavior

Document and Sheet should be resolved per input item like the other parameters, so the run above returns 16 rows from `Channels Data` followed by 188 rows from `Posts Log` (204 items), with paired items pointing at the right source. Same for Append, Update, Append or Update, Delete and Clear, which all go through the same router.

If per-item resolution is considered a breaking change that needs a new node version, a fallback would be to at least fail or add an execution hint when the Document or Sheet expression evaluates to different values across the input items, instead of silently using the first one.

Happy to open a PR for this if the approach is agreed.

### Debug Info

Copied from a self-hosted instance (Help > About n8n is not reachable from the API, so the relevant fields are listed here):

- n8n version: 2.39.10, self hosted
- Google Sheets node versions tested: 4.5 and 4.6; the code path is unchanged on `master` (4.7)
- Credential type: Google Sheets OAuth2
- Execution triggered via webhook (production mode); the manual-trigger version behaves the same

### Operating System

Linux (AWS EC2)

### n8n Version

2.39.10

### Node.js Version

Not checked (release build of 2.39.10); the behaviour is in the node code and does not depend on it

### Database

Not checked; does not affect this node's behaviour

### Execution mode

Not checked; does not affect this node's behaviour

### Hosting

self hosted

issue_title: Request for a statement on future development and ESLint 9 support
issue_description:
First of all, thank you for the enormous amount of work that has gone into this repository over the years. This project has a huge impact on the JavaScript ecosystem, and many teams (including ours) have relied on it for a long time.

This issue is not meant to pressure anyone for timelines. Rather, it is a request for clarity about the current status and future direction of the project.

ESLint 9 was released in April 2024,  and the main tracking issue for support is #2961.

Understandably, many users have been waiting for progress there. As time passes, more projects are trying to decide whether to:

- continue waiting
- maintain internal forks
- migrate to alternative configs
- or contribute to the migration effort

Because of this uncertainty, it might be very helpful for the community if maintainers could share a short statement about the project's current status and expectations. For example:

- Is the project still actively maintained with plans to support ESLint 9?
- Is support for the new flat config format planned?
- Are maintainers currently able to review and merge community contributions?
- If maintenance capacity is limited, would additional maintainers be welcome?

Even a short note would help many teams make better decisions. We have this on our board for almost two years and we need to make a decision now. 

It might also help if such a statement could be added near the beginning of the README so new users can quickly understand the current status of the project.

Again, thank you for maintaining this project and for the work that has gone into it over the years. Many of us would be happy to help if there is a clear direction or roadmap.

issue_title: update: same-version drifted editable finder survives the guard — uv audits an already-satisfied editable install as no-op, so the guard-triggered reinstall never rewrites it
issue_description:
## Context
The Sep-22 guards (`_editable_finder_mapping_current` / `_editable_install_is_current`, update_cmd_deps.py) correctly *detect* a drifted static finder MAPPING and correctly *force* the dependency-sync branch. But that branch runs `uv pip install -e .`, and uv audits an already-satisfied editable install as a no-op (your own comment documents this at _install_repair.py:750) — so when the drift is MAPPING-only (version string unchanged, top-level modules added; e.g. partial checkout, interrupted install, or a hand-patched finder), the reinstall silently no-ops and the drifted finder survives. Detection: reliable. Cure: conditional on the version string changing.

## Repro sketch (venv + uv)
1. venv has hermes-agent==X installed editable; tree is X.
2. Age the finder's MAPPING by hand (delete one top-level entry — simulates the interrupted-install state).
3. Run the dependency sync the updater triggers (`uv pip install -e .`) → uv reports satisfied, `Uninstalled 0`, finder mtime unchanged; cold imports of the dropped module still fail from a foreign cwd.

## Expected
When the trigger was a *finder-mapping mismatch*, the reinstall must be unconditional at the package level: `uv pip install --reinstall-package hermes-agent -e .` (the same-skip optimization is exactly what the guard is trying to defeat — a skip is always wrong once the guard fired). Cost is one rebuild.

## Observed (our fleet, 2026-10-05, 0.21.5, uv 0.9.x)
Version-bump drift (0.21.2 finder vs 0.21.5 tree) self-cured because the version change defeats the no-op audit. Same-version drift could not be cured without hand-running `uv pip install --reinstall`. Our board-level ask: make the guard's triggered reinstall `--reinstall-package`-scoped.

issue_title: MemoryQoS: container memory.high is not reset when an in-place resize makes the memory request equal the limit
issue_description:
### What happened?

With MemoryQoS on and a `memoryThrottlingFactor` set, I resized a Burstable container's memory request up to its limit in place. The container kept the `memory.high` computed for its previous request, so it stays throttled below its limit. It doesn't recover on later syncs.

Measured on v1.37.0 (kind, containerd, cgroup v2, `memoryThrottlingFactor: 0.9`), container with limit 512Mi:

| memory request | container memory.high |
|---|---|
| 256Mi (created) | 510025728 |
| 400Mi (resize) | 525123584 (recomputed, correct) |
| 512Mi = limit (resize) | 525123584 (stale, should be `max`) |
| 90s later | 525123584 |

I saw the same on v1.36.1.

### What did you expect to happen?

When request equals limit the kubelet deliberately doesn't set `memory.high`, so after the resize the container should end up with `memory.high=max`, the same as a container created with request == limit.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
# kind node, KubeletConfiguration
featureGates: {MemoryQoS: true}
memoryThrottlingFactor: 0.9
```

```sh
kubectl run a --image=registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10 \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"a","image":"registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10","resources":{"requests":{"memory":"256Mi","cpu":"100m"},"limits":{"memory":"512Mi"}}}]}}'
kubectl patch pod a --subresource resize -p '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"a","resources":{"requests":{"memory":"512Mi","cpu":"100m"},"limits":{"memory":"512Mi"}}}]}}'
# then read memory.high in the container's cgroup on the node
```

### Anything else we need to know?

I think the cause is in `generateLinuxContainerResources`. With MemoryQoS enforced, `memory.high` is added to `Unified` only when `memoryRequest != memoryLimitSpec` (and `memoryHigh > memoryRequest`). Otherwise the key is simply absent, and the runtime leaves an absent key untouched on `UpdateContainerResources`; CRI-O copies only the keys it's given. The MemoryQoS-off branch already writes `memory.high=max` for exactly this stale-after-resize reason, but the MemoryQoS-on branch has no equivalent.

This matters for VPA-driven resizes: a VPA `RequestsOnly` policy produces request == limit whenever the target is above the limit (kubernetes/autoscaler#9926).

issue_title: [Feature]: filter tailed records by minimum severity
issue_description:
## Problem

Operators using the root `openclaw logs` command cannot select a minimum severity for the bounded gateway log tail. During incident triage they must scan or externally filter debug and informational records, and ad-hoc text filtering does not preserve structured JSON output reliably.

This gap exists on current `main` in the root gateway/RPC/configured-file/systemd log flow. The existing `openclaw channels logs` feature proposal in #130187/#130202 owns channel log files and is not a substitute for the root command.

## Proposed bounded outcome

Add `openclaw logs --level <fatal|error|warn|info|debug|trace>` as a presentation-only minimum-severity filter.

- Reuse the existing canonical log parser and severity ordering.
- Apply the filter to both plain and JSON output.
- Preserve the current request, byte/line bounds, source selection, cursor advancement, follow/reconnect behavior, metadata, truncation notices, and errors.
- Exclude unclassified records only when `--level` is explicitly supplied.
- Keep output unchanged when the option is omitted.

## Existing alternatives

Shell filters such as `rg`, `grep`, or `jq` add platform-specific operator work and either lose structured records or require users to reproduce OpenClaw's parsing and level ordering. They do not provide a portable root CLI contract.

## Non-goals

- No server-side or historical log search.
- No attempt to fetch older records to fill the post-filter result count.
- No change to `openclaw channels logs`.
- No config, default, protocol, schema, persistence, migration, or security change.

## Acceptance and proof

- `--level warn --json` returns only warn, error, and fatal structured records.
- The same threshold works in plain output.
- Omitting `--level` preserves lower-level and unclassified records.
- An invalid level is rejected before log dispatch.
- A fully filtered `--limit 1` window remains empty rather than reading older records.
- Source cursor advancement and local-file/systemd fallback composition remain covered by focused tests.

I have an implementation ready and will open a closing PR with exact-head root CLI proof using isolated configuration and a controlled log file.

https://github.com/mcdado/next-route-cache-stale-repro

### To Reproduce

1. npm install
2. run ./repro.sh

### Current vs. Expected behavior

We deploy with DeployHQ in non-atomic mode. DeployHQ runs next build on its own build server, compares the output with the previous deployment, then uploads only the changed files over SSH into the existing application directory and deletes the files that are no longer part of the build. After the transfer it runs npm ci (for performance, instead of copying over the whole node_modules directory) and restarts `next start` with pm2 (to keep it alive).

The `.next` directory on the server is therefore never recreated: it is patched in place on every deploy. Files written by the server at runtime, such as .next/server/route-cache, are not part of the build output, so the deploy tool neither overwrites nor removes them.

After a new deployment `route-cache` will contain stale data, resulting in 404 for css and js files. Today an unrelated change that updated Next.js to the latest patch version went live and some pages were broken because of this.

We expect that after a new build these cached values are not used.

The linked reproduction was made by Claude Fable 5.1 and it highlights that `16.3.7` behaves correctly, while `16.3.8` and the `16.4.0-canary.60` do not. It suggests that https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/99482 is the key change that causes the problem because the key in `route-cache-key.ts` does not depend on the build.

We solved it by adding a step to the deployment that deletes `.next/server/route-cache` before restarting Next.

issue_title: Published image ships 17 fixable CVEs (1 critical) — base image rebuild + 4 dependency bumps
issue_description:
### Bug Description

The published `n8nio/n8n:2.39.4` image ships OS and npm packages at versions that have **already-published fixes**, so every self-hosted operator running a CVE scanner sees a red report they cannot act on themselves.

**To be explicit about what this is and isn't:** this is not a novel vulnerability in n8n's own code, so it is not a Vulnerability Disclosure Program submission. It is a supply-chain / release-pipeline report — the image needs rebuilding (and two direct dependencies bumping). Everything below is already public in the CVE database and in Alpine's advisories.

Scanned with `trivy image --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed`. **`--ignore-unfixed` matters: every CVE listed has a fix available today.**

#### CRITICAL

| CVE | Package | Installed | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-60002 | openssh | 10.3_p1-r0 | 10.3_p1-r1 |

#### HIGH — base image (rebuild fixes these)

| CVE | Package | Installed | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-59999, CVE-2026-60000 | openssh | 10.3_p1-r0 | 10.3_p1-r1 |
| CVE-2026-14456 | libcrypto3 | 3.5.7-r1 | 3.5.8-r0 |
| CVE-2026-76956, CVE-2026-76957 | libexpat | 2.8.3-r1 | 2.8.4-r0 |

#### HIGH — bundled npm dependencies (need a version bump, not a rebuild)

| CVE | Package | Installed | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-83608, -83613, -83614, -83615, -83616, -83619 | @xmldom/xmldom | 0.8.14 | 0.8.15 / 0.9.12 |
| CVE-2026-82659, GHSA-2x7j-588g-ccc2 | nodemailer | 8.0.10 | 9.0.1 / 9.1.0 |
| CVE-2026-63376, CVE-2026-77465 | toml | 3.0.0 | 4.1.2 / 4.2.0 |
| GHSA-j95f-988m-3j2f | @tiptap/core | 3.27.0 | 3.30.5 |

That is **17 distinct CVEs**, 1 critical.

### To Reproduce

```bash
docker run --rm aquasec/trivy:latest image \
  --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed \
  docker.io/n8nio/n8n:2.39.4
```

No n8n configuration is involved — the findings come from the image contents alone.

### Expected behavior

A freshly published image contains base packages and bundled dependencies with no CVEs that already have published fixes at build time.

Two things would help beyond a one-off rebuild:

1. **Rebuild published tags on a schedule**, independent of releases, so long-lived tags don't drift away from Alpine's security updates.
2. **`openssh` accounts for the only critical and 2 of the highs.** If the ssh *client* isn't needed at runtime (it may be there for git-based operations), dropping it would remove the entire critical finding.

The npm ones — `@xmldom/xmldom`, `nodemailer`, `toml`, `@tiptap/core` — need dependency bumps rather than a rebuild. `nodemailer` in particular has been outstanding for a while: it was the sole remaining finding on 2.37.1 back in August.

### Debug Info

Not applicable — this is an image-content report rather than a runtime defect. Reproduced purely by scanning the published image, independent of any deployment.

For context, the scan was run against an unmodified upstream image pulled from Docker Hub, not a locally built or customised one.

### Operating System

Linux (Kubernetes, Alpine-based official image — the finding is in the image, not the host)

### n8n Version

2.39.4 (also reproduced on 2.37.1)

### Node.js Version

As bundled in the official image

### Database

Postgres

### n8n EXECUTIONS_PROCESS setting

main

### Deployment method

Docker (Kubernetes)

issue_title: [Bug]: Failed to fetch server configuration: Load failed (desktop app on linux)
issue_description:
### Installation Method

Local Installation

### The Problem

I am reporting this bug after searching for solutions online and trying to resolve the issue with Claude (which led to this report).

---

The desktop app cannot connect to my self-hosted server, even though the exact same URL works perfectly in a browser and via `curl`. The error shown is:

> Failed to fetch server configuration: Load failed

This error appears **instantly** (no delay) when entering the correct, working server URL. A genuinely wrong/typo'd address also fails instantly, but with a *different* message: `Cannot connect to server. Internet works but this specific server is unreachable.`

Interestingly, if I take the correct, working URL and manually append `:8080` to it, I get that same "unreachable" message again — but this time only **after a long delay**, consistent with a real TCP connection attempt timing out (my reverse proxy, Cosmos-Cloud, only exposes 443 externally; nothing listens on 8080 from the outside). This confirms that the "reachability check" code path does perform a genuine network attempt when given a URL it treats as needing one.

So the behavior only diverges for the correct URL *without* a port: it hits "Failed to fetch server configuration: Load failed" instantly, with zero corresponding network activity (see trace below) — unlike every other case tested, which either times out for real (port appended) or fails a fast client-side format check (typo'd address). This suggests the app treats a bare domain (no explicit port) as passing initial validation, then moves to a distinct "fetch server configuration" step that fails immediately, client-side, before any socket is opened.

I've done extensive diagnostics to rule out environment causes:

- `curl -v https://<domain>/api/v1/info/status` → succeeds, returns `{"status":"UP"}` JSON.
- `gnutls-cli <domain> -p 443` → TLS handshake completes successfully, full cert chain (Let's Encrypt → ISRG Root X1) validated as trusted, TLS1.3.
- Ran `sudo trust extract-compat` (regenerates the GnuTLS/p11-kit trust bundle used by WebKitGTK on Arch-based systems) — no change.
- `WEBKIT_DEBUG=Network` while launching the extracted AppImage and retrying the connection — no relevant network log lines appear.
- `strace -f -e trace=network` on the extracted AppImage (`./squashfs-root/AppRun`) while retrying the connection to the self-hosted server — **zero syscalls reference the server's address at all**. The only external-looking `connect()` in the entire trace is a UDP `connect()` to `8.8.8.8:53` (the standard glibc trick for local-IP detection, not a real DNS query) and one TCP `connect()` to `127.0.0.1` (the app's own bundled local backend, unrelated to the self-hosted server). No DNS resolution, no TCP handshake, no TLS handshake toward the configured server is ever attempted at the OS level.

This matches the pattern reported independently on macOS in #5056 (zero outgoing traffic visible in Wireshark) and the self-hosted connection failures in #5264 and #5485, across different platforms (Windows/macOS/Linux) and different reverse proxy setups (NGINX, Cloudflare Tunnel, Cosmos-Cloud). In my case the reverse proxy is Cosmos-Cloud; I disabled all of its bot/security protections (SmartShield, auth, common-bot blocking) with no change, ruling out the proxy as the cause.

issue_description:
### What would you like to Propose?

I would like to add an educational implementation of **Learning With Errors (LWE) public-key encryption** (Regev, 2005) to the `ciphers` package.

LWE is the foundation of lattice-based cryptography and the mathematical basis of ML-KEM (Kyber), standardized by NIST as FIPS 203. The repository currently has no lattice-based algorithms, so this would be the first one and a natural complement to the existing hash-based signatures (Lamport, Winternitz).

### Issue details

**Algorithm:** LWE encryption (Regev, 2005)

**Problem statement:** Given many noisy linear equations `b = A·s + e (mod q)` with a small random error `e`, recovering the secret `s` is believed to be hard, even for quantum computers. Regev's scheme uses this hardness to encrypt single bits.

**How it works:**
- **Key generation:** sample a secret `s ∈ Z_q^n`, a random matrix `A ∈ Z_q^{m×n}` and a small error vector `e`. The public key is `(A, b = A·s + e)`, and the private key is `s`.
- **Encryption of a bit:** pick a random binary vector `r ∈ {0,1}^m`, then compute `u = rᵀ·A` and `v = r·b + bit·⌊q/2⌋ (mod q)`. The ciphertext is `(u, v)`.
- **Decryption:** compute `d = v − u·s (mod q)`. If `d` is closer to `q/2` than to `0`, the bit is 1; otherwise it is 0.
- **Messages:** a `byte[]` is encrypted bit by bit (MSB first).

**Parameters (toy):** `n = 32`, `q = 3329` (the ML-KEM modulus), `m = 128`, errors uniform in `[-3, 3]`. The accumulated noise is at most `m·3 = 384 < q/4`, so decryption is always correct.

**Proposed API** (`com.thealgorithms.ciphers.LWEEncryption`):
- `LWEEncryption()`, which performs key generation
- `Ciphertext encryptBit(int bit)` / `int decryptBit(Ciphertext ciphertext)`
- `Ciphertext[] encrypt(byte[] message)` / `byte[] decrypt(Ciphertext[] ciphertexts)`

**Scope:**
- No external dependencies; only `java.security.SecureRandom`
- JUnit 5 tests: bit and byte roundtrips, randomized encryption, wrong-key decryption, bit ordering, input validation and immutability
- Only two new files (implementation + test)

### Additional Information

This is intended for educational purposes only. The parameters are far too small to be secure, and real schemes use discrete Gaussian noise and much larger dimensions. This will be clearly stated in the Javadoc.

A possible follow-up would be a simplified Ring-LWE implementation over `Z_q[x]/(x^n + 1)`, which is closer to the actual structure of ML-KEM.

References:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Learning_with_errors
- O. Regev, "On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography", STOC 2005
- FIPS 203 (ML-KEM): https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/203/final

issue_description:
### Version

v18.14.2

### Platform

Linux qubit 5.15.108-0-lts #1-Alpine SMP Fri, 21 Apr 2023 05:55:14 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Subsystem

perf_hooks

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

In an interactive node session run:

```js
function timeDelta() {
    // The delta should be approximately the same on each invocation (assuming the system time is unchanged).
    return Date.now() - performance.now();
};
const ref = timeDelta();
const before = timeDelta();
```

Now suspend and resume the machine / VM through whatever means. Then continue in the same node session:

```js
const after = timeDelta();
console.log('BEFORE:', ref - before, 'AFTER:', ref - after);
```

Observe that the `after` value is incorrectly missing a number of seconds that matches the time the system was suspended. Eg. from my run:

```
BEFORE: -0.410888671875
AFTER: -7346.271728515625
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

100% (on Linux)

### What is the expected behavior? Why is that the expected behavior?

`performance.now()` is expected to jump with the realtime passed time while suspended according to [the spec](https://www.w3.org/TR/2023/WD-hr-time-3-20230425/#dfn-monotonic-clock) and https://github.com/w3c/hr-time/issues/115.

The https://github.com/mdn/content/issues/4713 issue also goes into detail on how the "Ticking During Sleep" applies to various platforms.

### What do you see instead?

No jump during sleep. Eg. by using more suitable clock reference, as proposed implemented in https://github.com/libuv/libuv/issues/1674.

### Additional information

The current `performance.now()` implementation is based on `process.hrtime()`:

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/2ac5e9889aba461f5a54d320973d2574980d206b/lib/internal/perf/utils.js#L13-L16

This issue also seems to contain a lot of relevant context around a concrete problem: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/issues/852.

issue_title: OpenAI-compatible endpoint: response ids have only 999 possible values (chatcmpl-rand.Intn(999))
issue_description:
### What is the issue?

The OpenAI-compatible endpoints mint response ids from a very small random space:

- `middleware/openai.go`: `id: fmt.Sprintf("chatcmpl-%d", rand.Intn(999))` for chat completions
- `middleware/openai.go`: `id: fmt.Sprintf("cmpl-%d", rand.Intn(999))` for completions

So every `/v1/chat/completions` response, Ollama Cloud included, carries one of only **999 ids**. Different requests routinely get the same id.

OpenAI clients and proxies treat `id` as a per-response identifier. Tools that key storage on it therefore collide. For example, LiteLLM's proxy uses the response id as the primary key of its spend-log table. After about 999 logged responses, almost every new successful call through Ollama's OpenAI endpoint is silently discarded from its logs. We measured this on a production proxy: 975 surviving rows, all `chatcmpl-NNN`, and successes stopped recording entirely. Details: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/39749

The native `/api/chat` path does not have this problem, because it returns no id and clients generate their own.

### Suggested fix

Generate a unique id per response, for example a UUID or a 96+ bit random value (`chatcmpl-<uuid>`), matching what OpenAI-compatible clients assume.

### OS / GPU / CPU / Ollama version

Observed against Ollama Cloud (`https://ollama.com/v1`). The code path is in `middleware/openai.go` on `main` as of 2026-09-25.

I'm seeing that generally WebGLRenderer is _significantly faster_ than WebGPURenderer for this initial render. As a result I'm having to use a WebGL context to perform the visibility culling while using a WebGPU context to do the actual edge projection.

I'm trying two different methods to render the Ids:

### Method 1

Add every mesh to a scene with a dedicated material with "id" uniform and render everything together. I've created sample fiddles showing a basic representation with 10,000 meshes:

|---|---|---|

|---|---|---|

issue_title: Type parameter escapes its constraint in a recursive call resolution
issue_description:
### 🔎 Search Terms

recursive, constraint, satisfies, return type inference, 64311

### 🕗 Version & Regression Information

- Introduced by #64311 (`7.1.0-dev.20260918.1`), still present in `7.1.0-dev.20260929.1`. Before #64311 the declaration was a circularity error.

### ⏯ Playground Link

_No response_

### 💻 Code

```ts
interface Schema<O> { readonly out: O }
type Shape = Record<string, Schema<any>>;
type Lookup = { x: 1; dflt: 2 };
declare function object<S extends Shape, P extends keyof Lookup>(shape: S): Schema<{ [K in keyof S]: S[K]["out"] }> & { p: P; f: (x: P) => void };
declare const str: Schema<string>;

const u = object({ name: str }) satisfies { p: number | "x" };
u.f(42); // error, P is "x"

const t = object({ name: str, get rec() { return object({ inner: t }); } }) satisfies { p: number | "x" };
t.f(42); // no error
const tp: "x" = t.p; // error: Type 'number | "x"' is not assignable to type '"x"'
```

### 🙁 Actual behavior

`P` on `t` is `number | "x"`, outside `keyof Lookup`, with no diagnostic. `P` only has a return-type inference from `satisfies`. The outer resolution filters it by the constraint, the re-entrant one doesn't, and `typeof t` ends up with the re-entrant result. With two mutually recursive consts only the one that resolves first gets the leaked type, so swapping the declaration order moves the error. Wes raised this in review: https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/64311#pullrequestreview-5239678270

### 🙂 Expected behavior

`P` is `"x"` on `t` as it is on `u`, and `t.f(42)` is an error.

# **PUBG/BGMI Sensitivity & Control Settings Guide**

Welcome to this guide on **PUBG/BGMI Sensitivity and Control Settings**! Whether you're a beginner or looking to level up your gameplay, this page will help you understand and customize the settings to suit your playstyle.

---

## **1. What Are Sensitivity Settings?**

**Sensitivity settings** control how fast your screen and crosshair move when you swipe your finger or move your device (gyroscope).

### **Types of Sensitivity:**

1. **Camera Sensitivity (Free Look)**  
   - Controls how fast the camera moves when looking around without aiming.
   - Best for scanning surroundings quickly.

2. **ADS Sensitivity (Aim Down Sight)**  
   - Affects how fast you move your aim while shooting.
   - Crucial for controlling recoil with your thumb.

3. **Gyroscope Sensitivity**  
   - Uses your device’s gyroscope to aim by tilting.
   - Very helpful for fine-tuned aim and recoil control.

### **Example:**
- A **high ADS sensitivity** = fast aim movement (good for close combat).
- A **low ADS sensitivity** = slow, steady movement (good for sniping).

---

## **2. What Are Control Settings?**

Control settings determine **how your buttons are placed** and **how you interact** with the game interface (jump, crouch, shoot, aim, etc.).

### **Popular Control Types:**

1. **Two-finger control** – Ideal for beginners. Limited flexibility.
2. **Three-finger control** – Better control while moving and shooting.
3. **Four-finger claw** – Advanced layout. Offers the best multitasking (aiming + movement + shooting).

---

## **3. How to Customize Your Settings**

### **Step-by-Step Guide:**

#### A. Sensitivity Settings

1. Go to **Settings > Sensitivity**.
2. Adjust the following:
   - **Camera** (for looking around)
   - **ADS** (for aiming while shooting)
   - **Gyroscope** (if enabled)

#### Suggested Sensitivity Example (for beginners):  
> (Can be adjusted based on device and preference)

- **Camera:**
  - 3rd Person No Scope – 120%
  - 1st Person No Scope – 130%
- **ADS:**
  - Red Dot/Holographic – 35%
  - 6x Scope – 10%
- **Gyroscope:**
  - Red Dot – 300%
  - 6x Scope – 100%

#### B. Control Settings

1. Go to **Settings > Controls > Customize**.
2. Move buttons like **shoot, aim, jump, crouch** to comfortable positions.
3. Save your layout or copy from a pro (PUBG offers layout codes).

---

## **4. Tips for Better Performance**

- **Use Training Mode** to test and tweak your settings.
- **Gradually increase sensitivity** to improve reflexes.
- **Enable Gyroscope** if you're comfortable tilting your device.
- **Save layout in the cloud** to avoid losing it.

---

## **Key Points for Revision:**

- **Camera Sensitivity** = Look Around  
- **ADS Sensitivity** = Recoil Control  
- **Gyroscope** = Device Tilt Aim  
- **Control Layout** = Button Placement for Comfort  
- **Customize Gradually** – Don’t rush to pro-level settings  
- **Practice** is key – Use training room regularly  

---

## **Final Note**

There’s **no “one-size-fits-all”** sensitivity or control layout. The best settings are the ones that **match your reflexes and comfort**. Keep experimenting and refining them!

issue_description:
### Details

Pluralization warnings were eliminated during the implementation of https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/pull/8497.

i18n/pl.toml

```toml
[day]
other = "miesiąca"
```

Statement|Result|Current Warning|Desired Warning
:--|:--|:--|:--
`{{ i18n "day" }}`|miesiąca||
`{{ i18n "day" 0 }}`|miesiąca||WARN ... "day" has no plural form "many"
`{{ i18n "day" 1 }}`|miesiąca||WARN ... "day" has no plural form "one"
`{{ i18n "day" 2 }}`|miesiąca||WARN ... "day" has no plural form "few"
`{{ i18n "day" "1.5" }}`|miesiąca||

Ref: <https://unicode-org.github.io/cldr-staging/charts/37/supplemental/language_plural_rules.html>

### Background

The motivation behind https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/pull/8497 was to suppress warnings when site authors translate words or phrases that do not require pluralization, using this construct:

i18n/es.toml

```toml
[contact]
other = "contacto"
```

and then invoke the translation without specifying a quantity: `{{ i18n "contact" }}`

Ideally, all i18n files should have this structure:

```toml
# Items without pluralization rules.

contact = "contacto"
help = "ayuda"

# Items with pluralization rules.

[day]
one = "día"
other = "días"
```

### Approach

Detect when the `i18n` function has been passed a quantity (including zero). If there's a quantity (including zero), perform the i18n lookup and emit warnings as needed. If there's not a quantity, do what we're doing now.

`/caveman ultra` compresses exactly one response. Every following turn drifts back to `full`-level output, even though `.caveman-active` correctly holds `ultra`.

## Cause

`src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` writes the mode correctly, but the per-turn reinforcement it injects is the same string for every level:

```js
additionalContext: "CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (" + activeMode + "). " +
  "Drop articles/filler/pleasantries/hedging. Fragments OK. " +
  "Code/commits/security: write normal."
```

That is the **full**-level ruleset with the active level's *name* interpolated into it. The rules that actually distinguish `ultra` (`SKILL.md`: "Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once.") never appear.

The only place that emits level-specific rules is `caveman-activate.js`, which filters `SKILL.md` to the active level — but it runs once, at `SessionStart`, for whatever level was active *then*. So after `/caveman ultra`:

- Turn 1 compresses, because the `Skill` tool loaded `SKILL.md` (ultra row included) for that turn.
- Turn 2+ sees only the generic reminder plus a stale `level: full` ruleset still sitting in context, and reverts.

The comment above the reinforcement block states its own intent — "keeps caveman visible in the model's attention on every user message" — which holds for on/off but not for intensity.

## Repro

```
$ echo full > ~/.claude/.caveman-active
$ /caveman ultra          # one terse response
$ <any next prompt>       # back to full-level verbosity
$ cat ~/.claude/.caveman-active
ultra
```

Hook output before the fix, at `ultra`:

```
CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (ultra). Drop articles/filler/pleasantries/hedging. Fragments OK. Code/commits/security: write normal.
```

Identical to the `lite` and `full` output apart from the parenthesised name.

## Fix

Branch `fix/per-turn-reinforcement-level-aware`, 3 files, 55 tests pass (`python3 -m pytest tests/ -q`).

- `src/hooks/caveman-config.js` — new `readSkillMd(hookDir)` (the 3-candidate resolution already used by `caveman-activate.js`) and `getLevelRules(modeLabel, hookDir)`, which returns the intensity-table description cell for one level, or `null` when `SKILL.md` is unreadable / the level has no row.
- `src/hooks/caveman-mode-tracker.js` — append `Level <level>: <rules>` to `additionalContext`, resolving the `wenyan` → `wenyan-full` alias the same way `caveman-activate.js` does. Falls back to the current generic text when `getLevelRules` returns `null`, so a standalone hook install without a skills dir is unaffected.
- `tests/test_mode_tracker.py` — three regression tests: reinforcement carries the active level's rules, two levels produce different reinforcement, `wenyan` resolves to the `wenyan-full` row.

After:

```
CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE (ultra). Drop articles/filler/pleasantries/hedging. Fragments OK. Code/commits/security: write normal. Level ultra: Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once. NO prose abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X → Y) — measured zero token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never touch
```

Happy to open this as a PR.

## Related: `SessionStart` clobbers a mid-session level change

Separate but compounding. `src/hooks/caveman-activate.js` unconditionally does:

```js
const mode = getDefaultMode();
...
safeWriteFlag(flagPath, mode);
```

The hook matches `startup|resume`, so a resume overwrites a mid-session `/caveman ultra` with the configured default. From `~/.claude/.caveman-mode-log.jsonl`:

```json
{"ts":1789926403616,"mode":"ultra","prev":"full"}
{"ts":1789935644569,"mode":"full","prev":"ultra"}
```

Nobody ran `/caveman full` in between. `SKILL.md` promises "Level persist until changed or session end", and a resume is neither. On `resume`, reading the existing flag and preferring it over `getDefaultMode()` would match the documented behavior — filed here rather than patched, since it may be intentional.

## Environment

- caveman `main` @ `0d95a81`, marketplace plugin install
- Claude Code 2.1.278, macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0), node via plugin runtime

issue_title: [Bug]: App Store iOS 2026.9.2 connects but never publishes APNs relay registration
issue_description:
## Summary

The App Store OpenClaw iOS app pairs successfully and establishes both node and operator connections, but never publishes `push.apns.register` to the paired Gateway. The Gateway therefore cannot send a push test or wake the app after iOS suspends the foreground connection.

This reproduces the symptom previously reported in #116088, but now with the currently available App Store build, a current Gateway, and a clean reinstall/re-pair.

## Versions

- OpenClaw Gateway: `2026.9.3` (`1391f7c`)
- OpenClaw iOS App Store app: `2026.9.2` (build 1; node surface reports `2026.9.20`)
- iOS: `26.6.2`
- Device model: `iPhone16,1`
- Gateway host: Linux x64
- Connection: secure Tailscale/WSS endpoint
- Push transport shown by the app: OpenClaw hosted relay at `ios-push-relay.openclaw.ai`

## Reproduction

1. Install OpenClaw `2026.9.2` from the Apple App Store.
2. Pair it with an OpenClaw `2026.9.3` Gateway using a fresh short-lived setup code.
3. Approve both the device pairing request and the node capability request.
4. Confirm that both the node and operator tokens are used and that the iPhone node is connected.
5. In the app, enable **Privacy → Notifications** and accept the hosted push relay disclosure.
6. In iOS Settings, confirm **Allow Notifications** is enabled.
7. Run **Settings → Diagnostics → Run Diagnostics**.
8. Observe that Diagnostics reports **Gateway Link: online** and **Notifications: Enabled**.
9. Attempt a Gateway push test for the newly paired iPhone.

## Expected result

After authorization and connection, the app should obtain an APNs token, register with the hosted relay, fetch the Gateway identity, and publish `push.apns.register`. The Gateway push test should then succeed.

## Actual result

- Foreground node connection succeeds.
- Both node and operator credentials are used successfully.
- App Diagnostics reports notifications as enabled.
- No `push.apns.register` event reaches the Gateway.
- A Gateway push test fails with:

```text
has no APNs registration (connect iOS node first)
```

## Recovery attempts already tested

- Force-quit and reopen the app.
- Toggle the app's Notifications setting off and on.
- Toggle iOS **Allow Notifications** off and on.
- Run app Diagnostics again.
- Remove the app completely, reinstall it from the App Store, create a new device identity, and re-pair/approve from scratch.

The clean reinstall and new pairing produce the same result, ruling out stale app preferences, stale pairing credentials, and the previous device identity as the cause.

## Diagnostic limitation

The app's Diagnostics screen reports notification authorization/presentation state but does not expose which push-registration stage failed. The remaining possibilities appear to be:

- APNs token acquisition / entitlement failure;
- hosted relay attestation or registration failure;
- Gateway identity fetch failure; or
- failure before the final `push.apns.register` publication.

A sanitized per-stage push registration status in the iOS Diagnostics screen would make this boundary observable without requiring Xcode or access to relay-side logs.

## Privacy

This report intentionally omits names, phone numbers, Gateway credentials, setup codes, Tailscale hostnames, IP addresses, and full device/node identifiers.

issue_title: WebGLRenderer: `sampler2DArrayShadow` uniform without a texture fails the draw call.
issue_description:
### Description

#34687 gave `sampler2DShadow` and `samplerCubeShadow` uniforms a depth fallback for when no texture is assigned. `sampler2DArrayShadow` doesn't have one yet: `setValueT2DArray1()` and `setValueT2DArrayArray()` fall back to `emptyArrayTexture`, an RGBA `DataArrayTexture`. A shadow sampler reading a non-depth texture is invalid, so the draw call fails with `INVALID_OPERATION` and the object isn't drawn.

No built-in shader declares `sampler2DArrayShadow`, so this only affects custom shaders. `WebGLProgram` declares its precision and `WebGLUniforms` sorts it with the other shadow samplers, so it does look intended to be supported.

The #34687 approach may not carry over directly: `WebGLTextures.uploadTexture()` only uses `TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY` for `DataArrayTexture` and `CompressedArrayTexture`, so a `DepthTexture` with `depth > 1` would be uploaded as a 2D texture.

### Reproduction steps

1. Create a `ShaderMaterial` that declares `uniform sampler2DArrayShadow map;` and leave `map.value` as `null`.
2. Render a mesh with it.
3. `gl.getError()` returns `1282` (`INVALID_OPERATION`) and the mesh is not drawn. The same material with `sampler2DShadow` or `samplerCubeShadow` renders without errors on `dev`.

### Code

```js
const material = new THREE.ShaderMaterial( {
	uniforms: { map: { value: null } },
	vertexShader: 'void main() { gl_Position = vec4( position.xy, 0.0, 1.0 ); }',
	fragmentShader: `
		uniform sampler2DArrayShadow map;
		void main() { gl_FragColor = vec4( vec3( texture( map, vec4( 0.5, 0.5, 0.0, 0.5 ) ) ), 1.0 ); }
	`
} );

scene.add( new THREE.Mesh( new THREE.PlaneGeometry( 2, 2 ), material ) );
renderer.render( scene, new THREE.Camera() );

console.log( renderer.getContext().getError() ); // 1282
```

### Live example

https://cdn.statically.io/gist/antialias/1c5270faadb9d6d0990fee04b5b6537b/raw/80ff24123f6a4c5c642559e897bc9ad27e6b6e8a/null-shadow-sampler.html ([source](https://gist.github.com/antialias/1c5270faadb9d6d0990fee04b5b6537b))

issue_title: Python Basics Review: correct wording and cover missing concepts
issue_description:
### Describe the Issue

1. **Repeated use cases**

   > `- **Introduction**: Python is a general-purpose programming language known for its simplicity and ease of use. Python is used in many fields like data science and machine learning, web development, scripting and automation, embedded systems and IoT, and much more.`

   > `- **Common Use Cases**: Python is used in data science, machine learning, web development, cybersecurity, automation and microcomputers like the Raspberry Pi and MicroPython-compatible boards.`

   Both bullets list use cases. The introduction ends with the vague phrase `and much more`, and the second list is missing an Oxford comma.

2. **Inconsistent heading capitalization**

   > `## What is Python?`

   > ``## Working with the `in` operator``

   > `## Common Operations used with Integers and Floats`

   > `## Boolean Operators and Short-circuiting`

   These headings do not consistently use title case.

3. **Variable-naming formatting and grammar**

   > `- Variable names can only start with a letter or an underscore (_), not a number.`

   > `- Variable names can only contain alphanumeric characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9) and underscores (_).`

   > ``- Variable names cannot be one of Python’s reserved keywords such as `if`, `class`, or `def`.``

   > ``- Variables names with multiple words are separated by underscores. Ex. `snake_case`.``

   The underscores and character ranges lack code formatting. The list also contains an em dash in the case-sensitivity item, a curly apostrophe, the phrase `Variables names`, and the fragment `Ex.`.

4. **Missing naming conventions**

   > `- **Naming Conventions for Variables**: Here are the naming conventions you should use for variables:`

   [How Do You Declare Variables and What Are Naming Conventions to Name Variables?](https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/lecture-understanding-variables-and-data-types/how-do-you-declare-variables-and-what-are-naming-conventions-to-name-variables) teaches descriptive variable names and avoiding single-letter names that do not communicate meaning. These conventions are missing from the review.

5. **Comment label and wording**

   > `- **Single Line Comments**: These types of comments should be used for short notes you wish to leave in your code.`

   The compound modifier `Single line` needs a hyphen. The plural phrase `These types` refers to a single comment type.

### Affected Pages

https://www.freecodecamp.org/learn/python-v9/review-python-basics/review-python-basics

### Expected behavior

1. The opening bullets should define Python once and collect its use cases in the second bullet:

   ```md
   - **Introduction**: Python is a general-purpose programming language known for its simplicity and ease of use.
   - **Common Use Cases**: Python is used in data science, machine learning, web development, cybersecurity, embedded systems and IoT, scripting, automation, and microcomputers such as the Raspberry Pi and MicroPython-compatible boards.
   ```

2. The four headings should read:

   ```md
   ## What Is Python?
   ## Working with the `in` Operator
   ## Common Operations Used with Integers and Floats
   ## Boolean Operators and Short-Circuiting
   ```

3. The existing naming rules should use code formatting and corrected punctuation and grammar:

   ```md
     - Variable names can only start with a letter or an underscore (`_`), not a number.
     - Variable names can only contain alphanumeric characters (`a-z`, `A-Z`, `0-9`) and underscores (`_`).
     - Variable names are case-sensitive: `age`, `Age`, and `AGE` are all considered unique.
     - Variable names cannot be one of Python's reserved keywords such as `if`, `class`, or `def`.
     - Variable names with multiple words use underscores, as in `snake_case`.
   ```

4. The naming-conventions list should also include these two items:

   ```md
     - Variable names should describe their purpose, as in `user_age`.
     - Single-letter variable names should be avoided when they do not communicate meaning.
   ```

5. The comment entry should read:

   ```md
   - **Single-Line Comments**: This type of comment should be used for short notes in your code.
   ```

issue_title: compact silently lands reasoning-only (empty-body) summaries, causing irrecoverable context loss
issue_description:
## Summary
When the model used for `/compact` returns a response containing **only reasoning parts and no text part**, opencode lands that empty-body message as the session summary and reports compact as successful. The epoch replacement then permanently destroys the original conversation history — yet everything reports success, so the agent continues with an essentially empty (corrupted) context and no warning.

## Reproduction — 100% reproducible (2/2 triggers)
- opencode **v1.18.21** (latest)
- Model: **`opencode-go/glm-5.3`** (reasoning model)
- Triggered compaction twice on this model; **both times** compact reported success while the summary message had only a `reasoning` part and no `text` part, and the original history was lost.

Steps:
1. Use `opencode-go/glm-5.3` in a session.
2. Trigger `/compact`.
3. Compact reports success; the resulting summary message has no text body; the original history is gone and cannot be recovered.

## Relationship to #41571
Shares the **same core failure** as #41571 (Kimi K3-256k): a reasoning model produces a reasoning-only summary (no `text` part), opencode marks it `summary: true`, lands it, and swaps in an empty summary — silently dropping history. #41571 traces this to the v1.18.15 `serialize()` flattening change in `compaction.ts` (history flattened to a wall of plain text → reasoning model analyzes instead of summarizing). `opencode-go/glm-5.3` on v1.18.21 exhibits the identical symptom at a 100% rate, suggesting the serialize-format issue affects reasoning models broadly, not just k3-256k. (I have not yet read `compaction.ts` to confirm glm-5.3's exact trigger mechanism, but the symptom + 100% rate + reasoning-model + same serialize code path make a shared root cause highly likely.)

## Additional proposals
- **L0 (stream layer):** detect/reject reasoning-only (no-text-part) responses as incomplete at stream end — upstream defense before compaction even runs.
- **Structural detection basis:** per the `@opencode-ai/sdk` Part union, `TextPart` (`type:"text"`) and `ReasoningPart` (`type:"reasoning"`) are **independent union members** — a reasoning-only response has no text part at all and is structurally detectable, not a length-threshold heuristic (negligible false-positive risk).
- **Irrecoverability:** once the epoch is replaced, the source material is destroyed, so any retry afterward is useless — the failure is silent and permanent. The failure must be caught **before** epoch replacement.

## Expected behavior
- Compact should **fail and retry the LLM while source material still exists** when the produced summary has no non-empty `TextPart` — not land it and replace the epoch.
- The success/"compacted" marker must not be set until the summary passes body validation.

## Suggested fix
Add a `hasNonEmptyTextBody(message)` check (iterate `message.parts`; require at least one `type === "text"` with non-whitespace content) at:
- **L0 (stream layer):** at stream end, reject reasoning-only responses as incomplete.
- **L1 (compact landing):** before epoch replacement, validate the summary body; on failure, retry the LLM (source still intact) instead of landing.

The same detection function can live in the SDK so plugins/tools share one definition. This is the "at minimum detect empty summaries and fail" bottom-line from #41571, plus an upstream L0 defense.

## Impact
- **Severity: high** — irrecoverable, silent context loss; the agent continues on a broken session with no warning because the compacted flag is set despite no real content.

## Environment
- opencode **v1.18.21** (latest)
- Model: `opencode-go/glm-5.3` (reasoning model)
- Repro rate: 2/2 (100%)

issue_title: r186: `GTAONode` fails to compile when its depth node is a multisampled texture — `textureGather` has no `texture_depth_multisampled_2d` overload
issue_description:
> **Draft, not filed; filing is the owner's call (#694 row 9).** Evidence tier **A**, and it is now
> reduced to a **standalone page with a one-variable control** — see below. Measured across three
> releases in a real app, on two platforms, and reproduced from a clean page against an untouched
> r186 tarball.

## What happens

In r186, `GTAONode`'s `sampleCenterDepth` reads depth with `this.depthNode.gather().sample( uv )`. The
AO function picks that path with `this._resolutionScale.lessThan( 1 ).select( sampleCenterDepth( uvNode ), sampleDepth( uvNode ) )`.
A uniform `select` emits BOTH branches, so the `textureGather` is in the shader whatever
`resolutionScale` is.

When the depth node comes from a `pass()` rendered with MSAA, it's a `texture_depth_multisampled_2d`.
WGSL has no `textureGather` for it, so the fragment module is invalid:

```
error: no matching call to 'textureGather(texture_depth_multisampled_2d, sampler, vec2<f32>)'
THREE.WebGPURenderer: Async render pipeline creation failed (renderPipeline_GTAO_*): Fragment module is invalid
```

Safari (iOS 26.6.2, WebGPU) reports the same thing as `no matching overload for initializer textureGather(ref<handle, texture_depth_multisampled_2d, read>, …)`.

## Measured

- **Setup:** a `pass()` scene with `renderer.samples > 0`, and `ao( scenePass.getTextureNode( 'depth' ), normal, camera )`.
- **Runs:** desktop Chromium, 85 s runs, each reaching the AO pass.

| three | GTAO errors |
|---|---|
| 0.184.0 | 0 |
| 0.185.1 | 0 |
| 0.186.0 | 128 |

r184 and r185 have no `gather()` in `GTAONode`. Confirmed by grep against both trees: `gather()` and
`sampleCenterDepth` appear in `examples/jsm/tsl/display/GTAONode.js` in r186 (lines 420 and 416) and
nowhere in r185's copy of the same file.

## Where it came from — #33914 / PR #33919

This is a side effect of a correct fix, not a mistaken one. **#33914** ("GTAONode: banding appears
at low radius") reported banding that *"only happens at `resolutionScale = 0.5` and is caused by
naively sampling a full res depth buffer when the resolution is lower"*. **PR #33919** ("GTAONode:
Fix banding issue", merged 2026-07-01) fixed it by adding exactly the three lines quoted above —
`sampleCenterDepth`, the `gather().sample( uv )` inside it, and the `_resolutionScale.lessThan( 1 )`
branch that selects it.

The gather is the right tool for that job. The regression is only that the branch is a **uniform
`select`**, which emits both sides into the shader — so the `textureGather` is compiled even when
`resolutionScale` is 1 and the gather path can never be taken at runtime. An application that never
lowers `resolutionScale` still cannot compile the shader if its depth is multisampled.

That is why the second suggested direction below is the more robust one: building the branch in JS
means the gather is only *generated* when it will be *used*, which fixes this without touching the
banding fix at all.

## Standalone reproduction — one variable

`renderer.samples` is the only thing that changes between a pass and a failure. Note it is read-only
on the renderer in r186, so MSAA is a construction parameter.

```js
import * as THREE from 'three/webgpu';
import { pass, mrt, output, normalView } from 'three/tsl';
import { ao } from 'three/addons/tsl/display/GTAONode.js';

const MSAA = true;                                   // <-- flip this
const renderer = new THREE.WebGPURenderer({ samples: MSAA ? 4 : 0 });
renderer.setSize(192, 192);
await renderer.init();

const scene = new THREE.Scene();
const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(50, 1, 0.1, 100);
camera.position.set(0, 0, 4);
scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.TorusKnotGeometry(0.7, 0.25, 64, 16),
                         new THREE.MeshStandardNodeMaterial({ color: 0xcccccc })));
scene.add(new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 2));

// A real normal node is supplied because GTAO's depth-derived normal path is separately
// invalid on a multisampled depth texture (textureDimensions) — see the note at the end.
const scenePass = pass(scene, camera);
scenePass.setMRT(mrt({ output, normal: normalView }));

const aoPass = ao(scenePass.getTextureNode('depth'),
                  scenePass.getTextureNode('normal'), camera);

const post = new THREE.RenderPipeline(renderer);
post.outputNode = aoPass.getTextureNode().mul(scenePass.getTextureNode('output'));
post.render();
```

**`samples: 4`** — six console errors, beginning with the WGSL compile failure:

```
THREE.WebGPURenderer: Uncaptured WebGPU GPUValidationError: Error while parsing WGSL:
```
