issue_title: Responses API streaming: text followed by a function call shares output_index 0, message never closed, final output reordered
issue_description:
### What is the issue?

When a streamed `/v1/responses` turn emits assistant text and then a function call, the event stream reuses one `output_index` for both items, never closes the message, and the final `response.output` lists the items in a different order than they were announced. A strict Responses stream consumer rejects the stream with "duplicate output item" or "terminal response changed output order".

A user of our project hit this on Ollama 0.34.4 and 0.35.1 while running a local model with tools. The same code is still on `main` at 42e911b (`openai/responses.go`):

1. **Shared `output_index`.** [`processTextContent`](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/42e911bc3d05798cad729cb474bf62f378cb2e26/openai/responses.go#L1868-L1917) announces the message at `c.outputIndex` and does not advance it. A later chunk with tool calls goes through [`emitFunctionCallEvents`](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/42e911bc3d05798cad729cb474bf62f378cb2e26/openai/responses.go#L1659-L1747), which announces the first `function_call` at `c.outputIndex + 0`. Both `response.output_item.added` events carry the same index.
2. **Message never closed.** After the tool calls, [`toolCallsSent`](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/42e911bc3d05798cad729cb474bf62f378cb2e26/openai/responses.go#L1456-L1460) is set. [`processCompletion`](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/42e911bc3d05798cad729cb474bf62f378cb2e26/openai/responses.go#L1946-L1947) then skips `output_text.done`, `content_part.done` and `output_item.done` for the message that was already opened.
3. **Final order differs from the stream.** [`buildFinalOutput`](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/42e911bc3d05798cad729cb474bf62f378cb2e26/openai/responses.go#L1919-L1938) puts `completedItems` (the function calls) first and appends the message last. The message was announced first, so `response.completed.response.output[i]` no longer matches the item announced at `output_index` i.

Event sequence for one such turn (abridged):

```
response.output_item.added           output_index=0  item.id=msg_…  type=message
response.content_part.added          output_index=0  item_id=msg_…
response.output_text.delta           output_index=0  item_id=msg_…
response.output_item.added           output_index=0  item.id=fc_…   type=function_call   <- same index
response.function_call_arguments.delta / .done   output_index=0  item_id=fc_…
response.output_item.done            output_index=0  item.id=fc_…
response.completed                   output=[fc_…, msg_…]                                <- reversed; msg_… never got output_item.done
```

Expected, matching OpenAI's Responses streaming: each output item gets its own `output_index` equal to its position in `response.output`. An item that was opened is closed with `output_item.done` before the response completes. The final `output` array keeps the announcement order.

A possible fix is to close the open message (`output_text.done`, `content_part.done`, `output_item.done`) and advance `c.outputIndex` before emitting function calls, and to record the message in `completedItems` at that point so `buildFinalOutput` keeps stream order.

Downstream context: https://github.com/Pal-AI-Lab/Coopanion/pull/21

### Relevant log output

```shell
ResponseProtocolError: Duplicate output item
```


### Ollama version

0.34.4, 0.35.1 (reported); code unchanged on main 42e911b

issue_title: chunkTimeout and timeout are silently ignored on the v2 packages/llm provider path
issue_description:
### Description

`chunkTimeout` and `timeout` are accepted by the provider config schema and documented, but `packages/llm` never reads them. Providers routed through the v2 native path therefore have **no client-side stall bound at all**, and the settings fail silently.

Implemented in two places, neither on the v2 path:

- `packages/core/src/aisdk.ts:78` (AI SDK path)
- `packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:1789` (v1 path)

Declared and documented:

- `packages/core/src/v1/config/provider.ts` — schema: "If no chunk arrives within this window, the request is aborted."
- `packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx` — same promise
- `packages/opencode/test/provider/header-timeout.test.ts` — passing test: "chunkTimeout raises a response stream error when SSE body stalls"

Not implemented:

- `packages/llm/src/providers/azure.ts` routes via `OpenAIResponses.route.with({ id: "azure-openai-responses" })`
- `packages/llm/src` contains no timeout application. The only `Timeout` reference is classification, `packages/llm/src/route/executor.ts:319` (`Cause.isTimeoutError`).

Note the schema lives under `core/src/`**`v1`**`/config/provider.ts` — this looks like a v1-era option that was not carried into `packages/llm`.

**Impact.** A half-open or stalled SSE stream is bounded only by Bun's TCP keepalive (`src/http/lib.rs` `set_keep_alive(true, 60)` plus hardcoded `TCP_KEEPINTVL=1` / `TCP_KEEPCNT=10` in `packages/bun-usockets/src/bsd.c`), so ~70s. If the peer stays alive but stops sending, nothing bounds it at all.

Against a real Azure OpenAI endpoint whose upstream APIM gateway RSTs mid-stream on ~2% of requests, every occurrence costs ~70s of dead time before the retry fires, and the turn surfaces only as `Decode error (200 POST ...)` — see #42482, whose cited path `packages/ai/src/route/executor.ts` is now `packages/llm/src/route/executor.ts`.

**Secondary observation.** The documented config key appears to be `options`, but only `settings` took effect on this build: `providers.azure.settings.baseURL` redirected the provider, `providers.azure.options.baseURL` did not. Worth confirming whether the v2 schema and docs disagree.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a local server that returns 200 with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, sends two valid SSE frames, then holds the socket open and sends nothing further.

2. Point a `packages/llm`-routed provider at it and set a short chunk timeout:

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "azure": {
      "settings": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:8899/openai/v1",
        "chunkTimeout": 15000
      }
    }
  }
}
```

3. `opencode run --standalone --model azure/<model> "hi"`

Expected: request aborts at ~15s with a stream error.

Actual: no abort. I killed it externally at 100s. Same result with `"timeout": 20000` (killed at 80s). `baseURL` in the same settings block did take effect, so the block is parsed and applied.

### OpenCode version

0.0.0-beta-18743

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin arm64)

### Terminal

Ghostty

issue_title: Agent ingress HTML-escapes message bodies and silently truncates long bodies
issue_description:
## Description

Message bodies arriving at opencode agents via the Slack bridge are corrupted in two silent ways. Nothing errors; the text is just wrong when it lands in agent context, beads, PRs, and shell commands.

### Defect 1 — HTML entity escaping (silent, length-preserving)

Message bodies are HTML-escaped on ingress: `<` → `<`, `>` → `>`, `&` → `&`.

Evidence (2026-09-30):
- An agent sent a raw `<main>` inside a plain-text sentence; the receiving agent quoted it back still escaped — confirms escaping affects Slack messages themselves, not just downstream tooling.
- Inbound scope blocks reached agents with `<main>` and `&` already escaped.
- Ruled out: voltron slack-post delivery path, model output — this is a normalising transform on ingress in the harness/context-assembly layer.

Impact: any agent copying an HTML tag, shell metacharacter (`>`, `|`, `&`), or comparison operator out of a bridge message pastes corrupted text into code, beads, PRs, or shell commands. Silent wrong-state.

### Defect 2 — long-body truncation (lossy)

Long message bodies are cut off, usually mid-block. Observed three times in one session:
1. A task group (4 items) arrived entirely absent — heading survived, content did not.
2. Groups C, D, E of a 138-line source file arrived absent (lines 85–138).
3. A closing rationale cut mid-sentence.

## System details

- **OpenCode version:** 1.18.34
- **Operating system:** macOS 27.0
- **Slack bridge/client setup:** custom fleet bridge (`voltron/scripts/slack-post`) delivering agent messages into opencode agent sessions; corruption observed on ingress into the agent context layer, after bridge delivery (bridge itself verified clean — entity forms present in agent-received bodies, not in bridge output)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Send any message containing `<`, `>`, or `&` through the Slack bridge to an opencode agent; observe the entity form in the agent's received body.
2. Send a body above some length threshold; observe truncation mid-block.

## Expected behavior

Message bodies arrive byte-identical: raw `<`, `>`, `&` preserved; long multi-block bodies complete.

## Ask

1. Locate the ingress/context-assembly path where entities are escaped and where bodies are truncated.
2. Preserve raw text on ingress (or provide an explicit escape contract agents can rely on).
3. Fix or remove the truncation limit — silent mid-block loss destroys task scope.
4. Regression test: body with `<`, `>`, `&`, and a >2k multi-block message arrives byte-identical.

## Cross-reference

- Linear: MG-1550 (metrograph-ai)
- Folded bead: MG-1552 (closed, scope merged into MG-1550)
- Original investigation ruled out: voltron delivery path, model output

GOVERSION='go1.27.0'
GOWORK=''
PKG_CONFIG='pkg-config'
```

### What did you do?

Found while testing an internal HTTP service against Go 1.27.

A handler reads part of the request body and then calls `Close()` on it, without
reading far enough to observe `io.EOF`. This is what a decoder does when it knows
how long its message is: it consumes exactly the payload and stops.

The program below drives `net/http` over a net.Pipe so it is deterministic and
has no timers.

```go
package main

import (
      "fmt"
      "io"
      "net"
      "net/http"
      "os"
)

func main() {
      serverConn, clientConn := net.Pipe()

      closeErr := make(chan error, 1)
      handler := http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
              // Read part of the body and stop, leaving bytes unread.
              if _, err := io.ReadFull(r.Body, make([]byte, 2)); err != nil {
                      closeErr <- fmt.Errorf("unexpected read error: %w", err)
                      return
              }
              closeErr <- r.Body.Close()
      })

      go (&http.Server{Handler: handler}).Serve(&oneShotListener{conn: serverConn})
      go io.Copy(io.Discard, clientConn)
      go io.WriteString(clientConn, "POST / HTTP/1.1\r\n"+
              "Host: example.com\r\n"+
              "Content-Length: 4\r\n"+
              "\r\n"+
              "test")

      err := <-closeErr
      fmt.Printf("req.Body.Close() = %v\n", err)
      fmt.Printf("want               <nil>\n")
      if err != nil {
              os.Exit(1)
      }
}

type oneShotListener struct{ conn net.Conn }

func (l *oneShotListener) Accept() (net.Conn, error) {
      if c := l.conn; c != nil {
              l.conn = nil
              return c, nil
      }
      select {}
}
func (l *oneShotListener) Close() error   { return nil }
func (l *oneShotListener) Addr() net.Addr { return pipeAddr{} }

type pipeAddr struct{}

func (pipeAddr) Network() string { return "pipe" }
func (pipeAddr) String() string  { return "pipe" }
```
[Playground Link](https://go.dev/play/p/P6gM5GS84Vq)


### What did you see happen?

```console
req.Body.Close() = EOF
```

### What did you expect to see?

```console
req.Body.Close() = nil
```

The change came from CL [794640](https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/go/+/794640), "net/http: don't rely on server request body not
changing", which refactored server-side body draining in `(*body).Close`:

Before and after, in src/net/http/transfer.go:

  go1.26.7  https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.26.7/src/net/http/transfer.go#L991-L1000
  go1.27.0  https://github.com/golang/go/blob/go1.27.0/src/net/http/transfer.go#L1006-L1016

```diff
-                     n, err = io.CopyN(io.Discard, bodyLocked{b}, maxPostHandlerReadBytes)
-                     if err == io.EOF {
-                             err = nil
-                     }
-                     if n == maxPostHandlerReadBytes {
-                             b.earlyClose = true
+                     n, err = io.CopyN(io.Discard, bodyLocked{b}, maxPostHandlerReadBytes+1)
+                     b.earlyClose = true
+                     if err == io.EOF && n <= maxPostHandlerReadBytes {
+                             b.earlyClose = false
+                             b.sawEOF = true
                      }
```

The assignment that cleared `io.EOF` was dropped. The CL message describes only
the refactor and does not mention changing what Close returns, so this looks
unintended.

Adding `err = nil` inside the new EOF branch restores the previous behavior while leaving the CL's
`maxPostHandlerReadBytes+1` bound and the `earlyClose/sawEOF` bookkeeping intact.

   ```

The full-suite run is the confirmed reproduction. The smaller class-level test invocation was not rerun before the test campaign was stopped.

## Expected behavior

All fixtures referenced by a checked-in unit test should be present or generated by its task dependencies, so `testGetClassName` reaches its assertion that the imported JVM class is named `HelloWorld`.

A closure check is that the test passes from a fresh clone after the normal dependency and build steps, with no manually supplied ignored files.

The suite contained three tests, one skipped test, and one failure. The failing test stopped before loading a program:

```text
java.io.FileNotFoundException: file HelloWorld.class does not exist in module TestResources
```

The test directly calls:

```java
Application.getModuleDataFile("TestResources", "HelloWorld.class")
```

No `HelloWorld.class` or corresponding `HelloWorld.java` fixture exists in the checkout. The repository-wide `.gitignore` also ignores `*.class`, making an accidentally generated local copy easy to miss during development.

- `Ghidra/Test/DebuggerIntegrationTest`
- `Ghidra/Test/TestResources`
- Trace RMI launcher class-name detection tests

issue_title: WebGLRenderer: shadow pass ignores `light.shadow.camera.layers` (inconsistent with WebGPURenderer since #30877)
issue_description:
### Description

`WebGLRenderer` ignores `light.shadow.camera.layers`. The shadow pass picks shadow casters by the layers of the camera passed to `renderer.render()`, not by the layers of the light's shadow camera. So there is no way to limit a light's shadow map to a subset of objects, for example "only the characters near a camp fire cast into its point-light cube map".

In `WebGLShadowMap.render()`, the call `renderObject( scene, camera, shadowCamera, light, this.type )` passes the outer `camera`, which is the viewing camera. `renderObject()` then tests `object.layers.test( camera.layers )`. For point lights the loop declares `const camera = shadow.camera`, but only inside the `if ( light.isPointLight )` block, so the `renderObject()` call after it still receives the viewing camera. Directional and spot lights behave the same way.

This was reported for both renderers in #30156. That issue was closed after #30877 ("ShadowNode: Inherit camera.layers only if shadow.camera.layers is not set") fixed `WebGPURenderer`. A later comment in #30156 notes that WebGL still has the issue. `WebGLRenderer` and `WebGPURenderer` now behave differently for the same scene.

In our project, every shadow caster in the scene went into the six faces of a point light's cube map, although its shadow camera was set to a layer that only the characters near the light were on.

### Reproduction steps

1. Create a `PointLight` with `castShadow = true` and set `light.shadow.camera.layers.set( 2 )`.
2. Add a floor with `receiveShadow = true`, and a box with `castShadow = true` on the default layer 0 only.
3. Render with a camera on layer 0.
4. The box casts a shadow on the floor. Expected: no shadow, because the light's shadow camera does not see layer 0.

### Code

```js
const light = new THREE.PointLight( 0xffffff, 12, 0, 1 );
light.position.set( 0, 4, 0 );
light.castShadow = true;
light.shadow.camera.layers.set( 2 ); // the shadow camera sees layer 2 only
scene.add( light );

const floor = new THREE.Mesh( new THREE.PlaneGeometry( 10, 10 ), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial() );
floor.rotation.x = - Math.PI / 2;
floor.receiveShadow = true;

const box = new THREE.Mesh( new THREE.BoxGeometry( 1, 1, 1 ), new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial( { color: 0xff0000 } ) );
box.position.set( 1, 1.5, 0 );
box.castShadow = true; // on layer 0 only: expected to cast no shadow
scene.add( floor, box );

renderer.render( scene, camera ); // camera on layer 0 -> the box casts a shadow
```

### Live example

https://jsfiddle.net/gh/gist/library/pure/ce71821589af080f7fd7ae568d2f9dce/

The page prints the floor's brightness under the box's shadow and at the mirrored, lit spot. With r186: `under the shadow: 71, beside: 232`, so the layer-0 box casts a shadow. With `box.castShadow = false` both values are about 232.

### Suggested fix

Mirror #30877 in `WebGLShadowMap`: when `shadow.camera.layers` is not the default mask, test the objects against it instead of the viewing camera's layers. For example, pass `shadow.camera` (or its layers) to `renderObject()` for the layer test, and keep the current behaviour when `shadow.camera.layers.mask === 1`, so existing scenes that only set the viewing camera's layers are unaffected.

Workaround until then: call `renderer.shadowMap.render( [ light ], scene, layerCamera )` yourself, where `layerCamera` is a camera that carries only the wanted layers. It must be called inside a render, for example in a scene's `onAfterRender`, because it needs the current render state. Then leave `shadow.needsUpdate = false` for the renderer's own pass.

### Version

r186

### Device

Desktop

### Browser

Chrome

issue_title: TypeScript 7 VS Code extension: a workspace "typescript" 7.x package is not detected, only "@typescript/native-preview", which is no longer published
issue_description:
The TypeScript 7 extension finds a workspace's own TypeScript 7 only in `node_modules/@typescript/native-preview`. That package was last published on 2026-07-07 (`7.0.0-dev.20260707.2`). TypeScript 7 now ships as `typescript`: `typescript@7.0.2` came out the next day, and the 7.1 nightlies ship as `typescript@next` (`7.1.0-dev.20260930.4` today). So a project that installs TypeScript 7 the current way runs the extension's bundled compiler instead of its own. Nothing tells the user, and the only fix is to write a `tsdk` setting by hand.

**Versions:** TypeScript 7 extension 1.0.1, VS Code 1.140.0, macOS.

### Repro

issue_title: v2 control channel keys are publicly derivable when auth.method = oidc
issue_description:
### Bug Description

With `auth.method = "oidc"`, the v2 wire control channel derives its AEAD keys from
input keying material that is empty, and from a salt that is fully public. Any observer
of the handshake can therefore derive the session keys for both directions.

`pkg/util/net/conn.go` derives the control-channel keys with:

```go
hkdf.Key(sha256.New, key, transcriptHash, info, libcrypto.AEADKeySize)
```

- `key` is `auth.EncryptionKey()`, which returns `[]byte(resolved.Token)`.
- `resolved.Token` is only populated inside `if resolved.Method == v1.AuthMethodToken`
  (`pkg/auth/auth.go`, both `BuildClientAuth` and `BuildServerAuth`). With OIDC that
  branch never runs, so the IKM is empty on both sides.
- The salt is `HashCryptoTranscript(clientHelloPayload, serverHelloPayload)`, computed
  over two frames that are exchanged in cleartext before encryption begins.
- `info` is a constant string.

Every input to the KDF is then public, so the AEAD layer provides no confidentiality
against anyone who can see the handshake. This matters most when frp is deployed behind
TLS-terminating infrastructure (reverse proxies, API gateways, service meshes), since
those components see the hellos.

With `auth.method = "token"` the derivation is sound, because the pre-shared token is
mixed in. The problem is specific to auth methods that have no pre-shared secret.

### frpc Version

0.71.0 (`dev` @ 832df8df)

### frps Version

0.71.0 (`dev` @ 832df8df)

### System Architecture

All. This is in protocol code and is not platform specific.

### Configurations

Any OIDC configuration with `transport.wireProtocol = "v2"`, for example:

```toml
# frpc
transport.wireProtocol = "v2"
auth.method = "oidc"
auth.oidc.clientID = "..."
auth.oidc.clientSecret = "..."
auth.oidc.tokenEndpointURL = "https://issuer.example.com/token"
```

```toml
# frps
auth.method = "oidc"
auth.oidc.issuer = "https://issuer.example.com"
auth.oidc.audience = "..."
```

### Logs

Not applicable. The connection succeeds normally; nothing is logged, which is part of
why this is easy to miss.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Confirm the encryption key is empty under OIDC:

```go
cfg := &v1.AuthClientConfig{Method: v1.AuthMethodOIDC}
cfg.OIDC.ClientID = "cid"
cfg.OIDC.ClientSecret = "secret"
cfg.OIDC.TokenEndpointURL = "https://issuer.example.invalid/token"
ca, _ := auth.BuildClientAuth(cfg)
len(ca.EncryptionKey()) // 0
```

2. Note that `HashCryptoTranscript` takes only the two hello payloads, both of which are
   written to the wire before `NewAEADCryptoReadWriter` is installed.

3. Given a capture of the ClientHello and ServerHello frames, recompute the transcript
   hash and run the same HKDF with an empty IKM to obtain the client-to-server and
   server-to-client keys.

### Affected area

Security

### Proposed fix

Add an ephemeral X25519 key share to `ClientHello` / `ServerHello` and mix the ECDH
output into the HKDF input keying material. Token deployments keep contributing their
pre-shared secret and additionally gain forward secrecy.

I have opened #5527 with an implementation, but I am happy to change the approach.
Three points I would especially like your opinion on before it is reviewed:

1. **Fail-closed behaviour.** The PR makes both sides refuse to open a v2 channel when
   the resulting keying material is empty, so a stripped key share cannot silently fall
   back to a publicly derivable key. The cost is that, under an auth method with no
   pre-shared secret, a peer with this change will not talk to a v2 peer without it.
   Token deployments are unaffected. Is that trade-off acceptable to you, or would you
   prefer it stay compatible and log a warning instead?

2. **Authentication.** The exchange is unauthenticated on its own, so an active attacker
   who rewrites both hellos can still man-in-the-middle. Closing that needs a transcript
   confirmation after login. I left it out to keep the change small, but I can add it.

3. **Scope.** The v1 control channel and work connections using
   `transport.useEncryption` are also keyed by the raw auth token and have the same
   weakness under OIDC. I did not touch them. Should they be handled separately?

issue_title: HTTP Request node: array[object] variables are inserted as Python repr, corrupting the request body
issue_description:
### Self Checks

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Language Policy](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/issues/1542).
- [x] This is only for bug report, if you would like to ask a question, please head to [Discussions](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/discussions/categories/general).
- [x] I have searched for existing issues [search for existing issues](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/issues), including closed ones.
- [x] I confirm that I am using English to submit this report, otherwise it will be closed.
- [x] 【中文用户 & Non English User】请使用英语提交，否则会被关闭 ：）
- [x] Please do not modify this template :) and fill in all the required fields.

### Dify version

1.17.1 (main at 8222397)

### Cloud or Self Hosted

Self Hosted (Source)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a Code node with an output `items` of type `Array[Object]` that returns:
   ```json
   [{"sku": "A1", "gift": true, "note": null}, {"sku": "B2", "gift": false, "note": "Tom's"}]
   ```
2. Add an HTTP Request node after it, body type `JSON`, body:
   ```
   {"items": {{#code.items#}}}
   ```
3. Run the workflow and check the request body that was sent.

Same with a `raw-text` body, and with other `Array[Object]` values such as the Knowledge Retrieval `result`.

Repro without the UI (run from `api/`):

```python
import json

from graphon.nodes.http_request.entities import HttpRequestNodeConfig, HttpRequestNodeData, HttpRequestNodeTimeout
from graphon.nodes.http_request.executor import Executor
from graphon.runtime.variable_pool import VariablePool

items = [{"sku": "A1", "gift": True, "note": None}, {"sku": "B2", "gift": False, "note": "Tom's"}]
pool = VariablePool()
pool.add(["code", "items"], items)


def build(body_type):
    node_data = HttpRequestNodeData.model_validate(
        {
            "title": "HTTP Request",
            "type": "http-request",
            "method": "post",
            "url": "https://example.com/orders",
            "authorization": {"type": "no-auth"},
            "headers": "",
            "params": "",
            "body": {"type": body_type, "data": [{"type": "text", "key": "", "value": '{"items": {{#code.items#}}}'}]},
        }
    )
    return Executor(
        node_data=node_data,
        timeout=HttpRequestNodeTimeout(connect=10, read=60, write=60),
        variable_pool=pool,
        http_request_config=HttpRequestNodeConfig(10, 60, 60, 1 << 20, 1 << 20, True, 0),
        http_client=object(),
        file_manager=object(),
    )


print("json body:    ", json.dumps(build("json").json))
print("raw-text body:", build("raw-text").content)
```

Output:

```
json body:     {"items": [{"sku": "A1", "gift": true, "note": "None}, {'sku': 'B2', 'gift': False, 'note': \"Tom's\"}"}]}
raw-text body: {"items": [{'sku': 'A1', 'gift': True, 'note': None}, {'sku': 'B2', 'gift': False, 'note': "Tom's"}]}
```

`ArraySegment.text` is just `str(self.value)`, i.e. a Python repr with single quotes, `True` and `None`:

https://github.com/langgenius/graphon/blob/11e2dee8cbd6dc2e6bf1c2059d9bbf4d0437ebe5/src/graphon/variables/segments.py#L128-L134

Only `ArrayStringSegment` overrides it with `json.dumps` (that came from the #12809 fix):

https://github.com/langgenius/graphon/blob/11e2dee8cbd6dc2e6bf1c2059d9bbf4d0437ebe5/src/graphon/variables/segments.py#L168-L177

The executor pastes `.text` into the body template. A JSON body then goes through `repair_json`, and a raw-text body is sent as is:

https://github.com/langgenius/graphon/blob/11e2dee8cbd6dc2e6bf1c2059d9bbf4d0437ebe5/src/graphon/nodes/http_request/executor.py#L269-L287

#34185 made object and `Array[Object]` variables selectable in the HTTP body, but that was a frontend change only. langgenius/graphon#235 only covers string variables.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The array is inserted as JSON and the API receives the same two objects.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

With a JSON body, the second object ends up inside the first one's `note` as a string, and `null` becomes the string `"None"` (see the output above). With a raw-text body, the body isn't valid JSON at all. There's no error in either case, the request just goes out with the wrong data.

Even a single null with no apostrophes, e.g. `[{"a": null}]`, is sent as `[{"a": "None"}]`.

issue_title: Schedule triggers in Europe/Dublin (and Africa/Casablanca, Africa/El_Aaiun) crash next-run calculation at their clock change and block every other scheduled workflow
issue_description:
### Self Checks

- [x] This is only for bug report, if you would like to ask a question, please head to Discussions.
- [x] I have searched for existing issues, including closed ones.

- [x] Please do not modify this template :) and fill in all the required fields.

### Dify version

main (f4602cc1fe)

### Cloud or Self Hosted

Self Hosted (Source)

### Steps to reproduce

`calculate_next_run_at` (`api/libs/schedule_utils.py`) computes a schedule plan's next run; the poller (`poll_workflow_schedules` → `_process_schedules` in `api/schedule/workflow_schedule_task.py`) calls it for every due plan.

1. `calculate_next_run_at("*/10 * * * *", "Europe/Dublin", base_time=datetime(2026, 10, 24, 23, 50, 5, tzinfo=UTC))`
2. `calculate_next_run_at("30 1 * * *", "Europe/Dublin", base_time=datetime(2026, 10, 24, 0, 30, 5, tzinfo=UTC))` (a daily 01:30 plan, right after its 24 October run)
3. Let the poller pick up a due plan like either of these beside any other due plan (for example a `UTC` plan).

The same happens for `Africa/Casablanca` and `Africa/El_Aaiun` at their clock changes (next one 2027-02-07 in the bundled tz data).

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

1 returns `2026-10-25T00:00:00Z` and 2 returns `2026-10-25T00:30:00Z` — what `Europe/London` returns for the same inputs today.

3: a plan whose next run cannot be computed is logged and skipped, and every other due plan still runs.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

1 and 2 raise a bare `AssertionError` from `croniter/croniter.py:210` (croniter 6.2.2). `schedule_utils.py:41` builds a pytz zone, and croniter's pytz branch assumes a DST offset is positive; the tz database models Irish winter time (and Morocco's Ramadan time) as a *negative* DST offset.

3: in `_process_schedules` the error escapes the loop before the batch is dispatched or committed. The plan stays the most overdue (the fetch orders by `next_run_at`), so it heads the next batch and the next one-minute poll fails the same way. No scheduled workflow runs on the instance until the calculation succeeds again.

How long depends on the plan, not only on the clock change (measured on `calculate_next_run_at` with the locked croniter 6.2.2 / pytz 2025.2):

| Europe/Dublin plan | Next run cannot be computed |
|---|---|
| every 5 or 10 minutes, hourly | about 2 hours around 2026-10-25 01:00 UTC |
| daily at 01:00–01:59 | 25 hours, from its 24 October run |
| weekly, Sunday 01:xx | 7 days, from its 18 October run |
| monthly on the 25th, 01:xx | from its 25 September run |

Plans at other times (for example daily 02:00 or 09:00) are not affected, and nor is `Europe/London`. I reproduced the calculation and the poller with unit tests (the poller on the unit-test SQLite database); I have not run it on a deployment with PostgreSQL and Celery.

Found while investigating #41214 (it is not that report's cause) by FireFunc agents running Claude Code, and reproduced with a failing unit test in `api/tests/unit_tests/libs/test_schedule_utils_enhanced.py`. A fix with tests (zoneinfo for the calculation, and a per-plan guard in the poller) is in review and will follow as a PR linked to this issue.

issue_title: `PromptTemplateParser.format` raises `TypeError` when a template variable is a number input (opening statement, expert-mode prompts)
issue_description:
### Self Checks

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guide and Language Policy.
- [x] This is only for bug report, if you would like to ask a question, please head to Discussions.
- [x] I have searched for existing issues, including closed ones.
- [x] I confirm that I am using English to submit this report, otherwise it will be closed.
- [x] 【中文用户 & Non English User】请使用英语提交，否则会被关闭 ：）
- [x] Please do not modify this template :) and fill in all the required fields.

### Dify version

main at f3074ced5b

### Cloud or Self Hosted

Self Hosted (Source)

### Steps to reproduce

`PromptTemplateParser.format` hands a `replacer` callback to `re.sub`. When the input value is not a string the callback returns it unchanged, and `re.sub` only accepts strings from a replacement callback:

https://github.com/langgenius/dify/blob/f3074ced5bc936c15fec1957e581582f44878f2a/api/core/prompt/utils/prompt_template_parser.py#L32-L42

Number inputs are intentionally kept as `int` / `float` by `BaseAppGenerator._validate_inputs` (`api/core/app/apps/base_app_generator.py`, the `VariableEntityType.NUMBER` branch), so they reach the parser as numbers.

Run from `api/`:

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace

from core.app.apps.message_based_app_generator import MessageBasedAppGenerator
from core.prompt.advanced_prompt_transform import AdvancedPromptTransform
from core.prompt.entities.advanced_prompt_entities import ChatModelMessage
from core.prompt.utils.prompt_template_parser import PromptTemplateParser
from graphon.model_runtime.entities.message_entities import PromptMessageRole

# 1. the parser itself
for value in (30, 1.5):
    try:
        print(PromptTemplateParser("You are {{age}} years old").format({"age": value}))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"parser.format({value!r}): {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

# 2. opening statement of a chat app that has a `number` input variable
gen = MessageBasedAppGenerator.__new__(MessageBasedAppGenerator)
entity = SimpleNamespace(
    app_config=SimpleNamespace(
        additional_features=SimpleNamespace(opening_statement="Hi {{name}}, you are {{age}} years old")
    ),
    inputs={"name": "Bob", "age": 30},  # a number variable stays an int after input validation
)
try:
    print(gen._get_conversation_introduction(entity))
except Exception as e:
    print(f"_get_conversation_introduction: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

# 3. expert-mode (advanced) prompt of a chat app
try:
    print(
        AdvancedPromptTransform()._get_chat_model_prompt_messages(
            prompt_template=[
                ChatModelMessage(text="User age: {{age}}", role=PromptMessageRole.SYSTEM, edition_type="basic")
            ],
            inputs={"age": 30},
            query=None,
            files=[],
            context=None,
            memory_config=None,
            memory=None,
        )
    )
except Exception as e:
    print(f"AdvancedPromptTransform: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

In product terms: a chat or agent-chat app with a **Number** variable that is referenced in the conversation opener, or in an expert-mode (advanced) prompt.

Callers that pass un-stringified inputs:

- `MessageBasedAppGenerator._get_conversation_introduction` (`api/core/app/apps/message_based_app_generator.py` L258-L275) — it catches only `KeyError`, so the `TypeError` propagates out of `_init_generate_records` when the conversation is created.
- `AdvancedPromptTransform` (`api/core/prompt/advanced_prompt_transform.py` L126, L182, L209, L305).

`SimplePromptTransform` is not affected because it converts first: `inputs = {key: str(value) for key, value in inputs.items()}` (`simple_prompt_transform.py` L61). That looks like the intended behaviour for the other two callers as well.

### ✔️ Expected Behavior

The number is rendered into the text: `Hi Bob, you are 30 years old`.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

```
parser.format(30): TypeError: sequence item 1: expected str instance, int found
parser.format(1.5): TypeError: sequence item 1: expected str instance, float found
_get_conversation_introduction: TypeError: sequence item 3: expected str instance, int found
AdvancedPromptTransform: TypeError: sequence item 1: expected str instance, int found
```

Suggested fix: make `replacer` return `str(value)` for non-string values (it already handles the missing-key case by returning the original placeholder), and add parser tests for `int`, `float` and `bool` inputs. I can send a PR for this.

issue_title: Use page ordinals for collapse on columnar keyword fields
issue_description:
### Description

Collapse on a columnar keyword field currently reads a `BytesRef` for every matching document and hashes it to find the group.

ColumNAR can already deliver a page as ordinals rather than bytes: `StringColumnReader#readBlock` drives a `StringBlockSink`, and `StringBlockSink#appendOrdinals` hands over the page's values as ordinals into the page's distinct values, along with the dictionary they index. Collapse could use those ordinals to avoid hashing the same value for every document, resolving each distinct value only once per page.

The benefit should be largest for low-cardinality fields with many matching documents, where the same value is reused many times within a page. As cardinality increases, the benefit from resolving each distinct value only once decreases, although grouping on integer ordinals still avoids per-document `BytesRef` comparisons.

The main complication is that these ordinals are local to a page, while Lucene's `GroupSelector` API is document-oriented. We would need to map page ordinals to groups across pages and likely adapt the selector/collector path to consume values in batches.

The same shape in ES|QL is `LIMIT n BY`:

```
# DSL
{ "collapse": { "field": "host.name" }, "sort": [ { "@timestamp": "asc" } ] }

# ES|QL
FROM logs | SORT @timestamp ASC | LIMIT 1 BY host.name
```

ES|QL's columnar path already reads pages this way, so it is a useful reference: `BytesRefsFromBinaryMultiSeparateCountBlockLoader` has a `PageSink` implementing `appendOrdinals` that builds an ordinal block directly rather than materialising a `BytesRef` per document.

Ideally we should also extend one of our existing benchmarks to cover collapse on both low- and high-cardinality keyword fields. Nothing covers it today: no Rally track runs a collapse query, and `KeywordTopNBenchmark` runs over `logsdb`, `logsdb_columnar` and `columnar` but pins cardinality to a constant. This would give us a baseline for the current implementation, measure the benefit of using page ordinals, and keep this query shape covered going forward.

`GroupingDocValuesSelector.Keyword` has a TODO for this.

Follow-up from #160941.

issue_title: 5.3 claims double-ended queue requires doubly-linked list
issue_description:
Why does a double-ended queue require a doubly-linked list? This can be implemented with a singly-linked list

* push front - insert before the head node
* pop front - remove the head node, point to the following node
* push back - append to the tail
* pop back - remove the tail node

In all cases, you maintain a pointer to head and tail.

The only time a doubly-linked list would make sense is if you need to iterate through the entire list front-to-back and back-to-front.

issue_title: Implement Thread-Specific Storage Pattern
issue_description:
## Description

Thread-Specific Storage is a concurrency design pattern where each thread retains its own instance of a shared object, typically achieved using `ThreadLocal<T>` in Java. By isolating data to each thread, you avoid synchronization overhead and minimize concurrency issues. Common use cases include storing thread-specific contexts, caching stateful objects like `DateFormat`, or managing per-thread counters without risking data corruption or race conditions.

### Key Elements

- **Isolation of State:** Each thread has its own copy of the data, reducing shared mutable state.
- **ThreadLocal Utility:** Java’s `ThreadLocal<T>` class provides a straightforward way to store data private to each thread.
- **Initialization & Cleanup:** Properly initializing and cleaning up thread-local data is crucial to prevent memory leaks.
- **Practical Use Cases:** Storing per-thread data such as locale-specific formatters, current transaction context, or local caches.

## References

1. *Pattern-Oriented Software Architecture, Volume 2: Patterns for Concurrent and Networked Objects*
2. [Java Design Patterns - Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/iluwatar/java-design-patterns/wiki)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new module or package named `thread-specific-storage` (or similar) is added.
- [ ] Demonstrates a clear use case of storing and retrieving thread-local data (e.g., per-thread state).
- [ ] Includes a readme (or `.md` file) explaining how the pattern works, with code examples or diagrams.
- [ ] Adheres to the repository’s coding style and naming conventions.
- [ ] Includes unit tests verifying behavior in a multi-threaded scenario.
- [ ] Passes all CI checks and meets the project’s contribution guidelines.

issue_title: Microservice pattern: Transaction log tailing
issue_description:
**Description:**
The Microservices - Transaction Log Tailing design pattern focuses on maintaining a consistent and up-to-date data view across different microservices by tailing the transaction log of a database. This pattern is particularly useful in scenarios where multiple microservices need to respond to changes in a shared database in real-time. It ensures that all services are notified of changes and can react accordingly without direct coupling.

**Main Elements:**
1. **Transaction Log:** The database maintains a log of all transactions. This log is used as the source of truth for all changes.
2. **Log Tailing:** A component tails the transaction log and publishes changes to a message broker or event stream.
3. **Event Stream:** Microservices subscribe to the event stream to receive updates.
4. **Consistency:** Ensures eventual consistency across different microservices by propagating changes through the event stream.
5. **Decoupling:** Reduces direct dependencies between microservices by using the transaction log as an intermediary.

**References:**
- [Microservices Pattern: Transaction Log Tailing](https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transaction-log-tailing.html)
- [Martin Fowler - Event-Driven Architecture](https://martinfowler.com/articles/201701-event-driven.html)
- [Project Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/iluwatar/java-design-patterns/wiki)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. Implement a component that tails the transaction log of a database and publishes changes to an event stream.
2. Develop microservices that subscribe to the event stream and update their state based on the received events.
3. Ensure eventual consistency across all microservices by validating that updates are correctly propagated and handled.

issue_description:
Hey maintainers! 👋

I noticed that the Presubmit.ai workflow is failing on pull requests. I took a look at the workflow file and found a couple of issues that are causing the failures.

## The Problem

The workflow in `.github/workflows/presubmit.yml` is failing with two errors:

1. **Missing API Key**: The workflow checks for `LLM_API_KEY` but it's not configured in the repo secrets
2. **Invalid Model**: The model `gemini-1.5-flash` isn't supported for the API version being used

This is blocking the AI reviewer from running on PRs, though it doesn't prevent merging since it's a separate check.

## Current Workflow Code

```yaml
- name: Check required secrets
  run: |
    if [ -z "${{ secrets.LLM_API_KEY }}" ]; then
      echo "Error: LLM_API_KEY secret is not configured"
      exit 1
    fi

- name: Run AI Reviewer
  uses: presubmit/ai-reviewer@latest
  env:
    GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    LLM_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LLM_API_KEY }}
    LLM_MODEL: "gemini-1.5-flash"
```

## Possible Solutions

### Option 1: Fix the workflow (if you want to keep the AI reviewer)

1. Add the `LLM_API_KEY` secret:
   - Go to Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
   - Add a new secret named `LLM_API_KEY` with your Google AI API key

2. Update the model to a supported version:
   ```yaml
   LLM_MODEL: "gemini-1.5-flash-002"
   # or another model from the supported list
   ```

### Option 2: Make it optional (recommended for now)

If you're not ready to configure the API key, you could make the workflow optional so it doesn't block contributors:

```yaml
- name: Check required secrets
  id: check-secrets
  run: |
    if [ -z "${{ secrets.LLM_API_KEY }}" ]; then
      echo "LLM_API_KEY not configured, skipping AI review"
      echo "skip=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    fi

- name: Run AI Reviewer
  if: steps.check-secrets.outputs.skip != 'true'
  uses: presubmit/ai-reviewer@latest
  # ... rest of the config
```

### Option 3: Disable the workflow temporarily

If the AI reviewer isn't critical right now, you could disable it:
- Go to Actions tab
- Select "Presubmit.ai" workflow
- Click the "..." menu
- Select "Disable workflow"

## Impact

Right now this doesn't block PRs from being merged, but contributors might see a red X on their PRs which can be confusing. Making it optional or fixing it would improve the contributor experience.

Let me know if you'd like me to submit a PR for any of these solutions!

issue_title: proposal: net/netip: add netip.Addr.To6()
issue_description:
### Proposal Details

This proposal was already pushed 4 years ago in #54365. I am pushing it again with additional new elements.

`netip.Addr` has `Unmap()` but no `Map()` or `To6()` method.

`Unmap()` is implemented like this:

```go
func (ip Addr) Unmap() Addr {
    if ip.Is4In6() {
        ip.z = z4
    }
    return ip
}
```

`To6()` could be implemented like this:

```go
func (ip Addr) To6() Addr {
    if ip.Is4() {
        ip.z = z6noz
    }
    return ip
}
```

In #54365, it was proposed each project implements its own helper:

```go
func AddrTo6(ip netip.Addr) netip.Addr {
    if ip.Is4() {
        ip = netip.AddrFrom16(ip.As16())
    }
    return ip
}
```

In the last couple of months, I spent some time to investigate a bit more this issue. You can find more details of my musing in [Hacking the Go compiler to efficiently map IPv4 to IPv6](https://vincent.bernat.ch/en/blog/2026-go-netip-addrto6).

First, Go 1.27 introduces a performance regression for the above `AddrTo6()` function due to [CL 748200][] / [issue #77720][77720].

Second, I have a compiler modification that would make `AddrTo6()` optimal by adding [one rewriting rule](https://github.com/vincentbernat/go/commit/netipmap-fix3) and an [earlier memcombine pass](https://github.com/vincentbernat/go/commit/netipmap-fix4).

[CL 748200]: https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/go/+/748200 "cmd/compile: forward small Load through Move to avoid redundant copies"
[77720]: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/77720 "cmd/compile: field access on struct-returning method copies entire struct"

```text
goos: linux
goarch: amd64
pkg: github.com/vincentbernat/go-netip-addrto6
cpu: AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor
                   │   Go 1.26.8    │             Our branch              │
                   │     sec/op     │    sec/op     vs base               │
AddrTo6/safe          6.5470n ±  0%   0.8944n ± 4%  -86.34% (p=0.002 n=6)
AddrTo6/unsafe        0.9071n ±  3%   0.8682n ± 1%   -4.28% (p=0.002 n=6)
AddrTo6/builtin       0.8871n ±  2%   0.8785n ± 1%        ~ (p=0.310 n=6)
```

So, it's possible for the compiler to optimize but:

1. This is fragile, as shown by the regression in Go 1.27 (which adds 9% of time to the benchmark).
2. My patches require running the memcombine pass twice. Would it be accepted?

So, I still think this is better to add a `To6()` or `Map()` method to `netip.Addr`.

cc @database64128 (for issue #54365) and @favonia (for issue #51833).

issue_title: install.ps1 uses $Args parameter, causing irm | iex failure in PowerShell 7
issue_description:
**What happen**
The Windows PowerShell installer fails when run using the documented one-line install command:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

PowerShell throws this error:

```text
iex : Cannot overwrite variable Args because the variable has been optimized. Try using the New-Variable or
Set-Variable cmdlet (without any aliases), or dot-source the command that you are using to set the variable.
At line:1 char:80
+ ... aw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 | iex
+                                                                       ~~~
    + CategoryInfo          : WriteError: (Args:String) [Invoke-Expression], SessionStateUnauthorizedAccessException
    + FullyQualifiedErrorId : VariableNotWritableRare,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.InvokeExpressionCommand
```

The issue appears to come from `install.ps1` declaring a parameter named `$Args`:

```powershell
param(
  [Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments = $true)]
  [string[]]$Args
)
```

PowerShell has an automatic variable named `$args`, and variable names are case-insensitive, so `$Args` conflicts with `$args` when the script is executed through `iex`.

**Expected**
The documented Windows one-line install command should run successfully in PowerShell without failing on the `$Args` parameter.

A possible fix is to rename the parameter to something like `$InstallArgs` and update the argument forwarding references:

```powershell
param(
  [Parameter(ValueFromRemainingArguments = $true)]
  [string[]]$InstallArgs
)

# ...

& node $local @InstallArgs

# ...

& npx -y "github:$Repo" @InstallArgs
```

**Before/after example**
```text
Input: irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman/main/install.ps1 | iex

Got:   Cannot overwrite variable Args because the variable has been optimized.

Want:  The installer should continue normally, check for Node.js >=18, and run the Node installer via npx or the local bin/install.js.
```

issue_title: redis 长时间不使用再使用会报 command timeout 错误的问题
issue_description:
mall项目使用缓存过程中，redis连接超时会报错，返回500，造成获取数据失败，需要再次请求才能获得数据
```
io.lettuce.core.RedisCommandTimeoutException: Command timed out after 300 millisecond(s)
	at io.lettuce.core.ExceptionFactory.createTimeoutException(ExceptionFactory.java:51)
	at io.lettuce.core.protocol.CommandExpiryWriter.lambda$potentiallyExpire$0(CommandExpiryWriter.java:167)
	at io.netty.util.concurrent.PromiseTask.runTask(PromiseTask.java:98)
	at io.netty.util.concurrent.ScheduledFutureTask.run(ScheduledFutureTask.java:170)
	at io.netty.util.concurrent.DefaultEventExecutor.run(DefaultEventExecutor.java:66)
	at io.netty.util.concurrent.SingleThreadEventExecutor$4.run(SingleThreadEventExecutor.java:989)
	at io.netty.util.internal.ThreadExecutorMap$2.run(ThreadExecutorMap.java:74)
	at io.netty.util.concurrent.FastThreadLocalRunnable.run(FastThreadLocalRunnable.java:30)
	at java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:748)
```
### 问题描述
> 在springboot项目里使用redis做队列的，使用过程中会遇到短时间不操作（五分钟左右），redis连接就断开了，再使用redis时会报连接超时，此次操作会失败，然后几秒内会重连，重新连上之后又可以正常往redis写东西了

### 解决方案

1 、亲测有效：Redis 服务端 通过 tcp-keepalive 发送 ack 达到超活检测效果 官方建议设置 60s 时间
redis客户端执行：`CONFIG SET tcp-keepalive 60`，重启redis客户端。
2、心跳检测，如下
```
@Scheduled(cron = "0/10 * * * * *")
public void timer() {
    redisTemplate.opsForValue().get("heartbeat");
}
```
### 以下亲测无效
3、亲测无效：~~[改为jedis依赖](https://my.oschina.net/u/3740959/blog/4560638)。（我采用该方案，注意Jedis对象线程不安全(Lettuce对象是线程安全的）~~
```
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.data</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-data-commons</artifactId>
    <version>${spring-data-commons.version}</version>
    <exclusions>
        <exclusion>
            <groupId>redis.clients</groupId>
            <artifactId>jedis</artifactId>
        </exclusion>
        <exclusion>
            <artifactId>lettuce-core</artifactId>
            <groupId>io.lettuce</groupId>
        </exclusion>
    </exclusions>
</dependency>
<!-- 解决redis超时io.lettuce.core.RedisCommandTimeoutException -->
<dependency>
    <groupId>redis.clients</groupId>
    <artifactId>jedis</artifactId>
</dependency>
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.apache.commons</groupId>
    <artifactId>commons-pool2</artifactId>
</dependency>
```
4、亲测无效：~~升级 lettuce-core 至 5.3.0+，
（具体看此 [Fix infinite command timeout #1260](https://github.com/lettuce-io/lettuce-core/issues/1269) ）~~

### 参考
> 1、[请教一个 redis 长时间不使用再使用会报 command timeout 错误的问题](https://v2ex.com/t/693771)、
2、[springboot2.0.3 redis一会不操作会自动断开连接 队列channel监听器失效](https://www.jianshu.com/p/36be264926b0)

issue_title: go/types: types.Error.go116end end position derived from placeholder Ident.Name is garbage
issue_description:
Type-checking the code below results in a types.Error whose hidden go116end field (which gopls accesses via reflection) is invalid:

```go
package p

type I interface{ M() }

var m map[int]int

func _() {
	var a int
	var b I
	a, b = m[0] // error: cannot use ok value of (comma, ok) expression ... as I value
	_, _ = a, b
}
```

Standalone repro:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"go/ast"
	"go/parser"
	"go/token"
	"go/types"
	"reflect"
)

func main() {
	for _, src := range []string{
		`package p; type I interface{ M() }; var m map[int]int; func _() { var a int; var b I; a, b = m[0]; _, _ = a, b }`,
		`package p; type I interface{ M() }; func f() (int, int); func _() { var a I; var b int; a, b = f(); _, _ = a, b }`,
	} {
		fset := token.NewFileSet()
		f, _ := parser.ParseFile(fset, "a.go", src, 0)
		conf := types.Config{Error: func(err error) {
			e := err.(types.Error)
			v := reflect.ValueOf(e)
			start, end := v.FieldByName("go116start").Int(), v.FieldByName("go116end").Int()
			fmt.Printf("%s\n\tspan [%d,%d) len=%d; file size %d\n", e.Msg, start, end, end-start, len(src))
		}}
		conf.Check("p", fset, []*ast.File{f}, nil)
	}
}
```
It prints:
```
cannot use ok value of (comma, ok) expression (value of type bool) as I value in multiple assignment: bool does not implement I (missing method M)
	span [94,128) len=34; file size 112
cannot use 1st function result (value of type int) as I value in multiple assignment: int does not implement I (missing method M)
	span [96,115) len=19; file size 113
```

The start position is accurate but the end is not, as it is derived from the length of the error description crammed by `(*Checker).multiExpr` into the Ident.Name field.So `len("ok value of (comma, ok) expression") == 34` and `len("1st function result") == 19`. Both values fall past EOF and land in an unrelated file. A similar pattern appears in genericExprList. These bogus end positions are the root cause of the crash in gopls described in #81814.

A fix would be to use the real extent for the error span and carry the description separately.

issue_title: [FEATURE REQUEST] Add Lamport One-Time Signature Scheme (Hash-Based Post-Quantum Signature)
issue_description:
### What would you like to Propose?

I propose adding a **Lamport One-Time Signature** implementation to the ciphers package.

The ciphers package currently contains classical public-key algorithms such as RSA,
ECC, and Diffie-Hellman, but no post-quantum algorithms. The Lamport signature
(Lamport, 1979) is a hash-based one-time signature scheme whose security relies only
on the one-wayness of a cryptographic hash function rather than on integer
factorization or discrete logarithms, which makes it resistant to quantum computer
attacks. It is the foundational building block of modern post-quantum signature
standards such as SPHINCS+ and XMSS.

Lamport signatures are a good fit for this repository because:

- It would be the first post-quantum algorithm in the repository, filling a gap that
  is increasingly relevant now that NIST has standardized post-quantum schemes and
  the JDK itself has started adopting them.
- It can be implemented entirely using standard Java (`java.security.MessageDigest`
  and `java.security.SecureRandom`) without any external dependencies, matching the
  educational and dependency-free style of this repository.
- The algorithm is straightforward to understand and demonstrates important
  cryptographic concepts such as one-way functions, hash-based commitments, and the
  trade-offs of one-time key usage.
- It complements the existing RSA, ECC, and DiffieHellman implementations by showing
  a fundamentally different (hash-based) approach to digital signatures.

### Issue details

**Algorithm / problem statement:** Generate a key pair where the private key
consists of 256 pairs of random 32-byte secrets (one pair per bit of a SHA-256
message digest) and the public key consists of the SHA-256 hashes of those secrets.
To sign a message, hash it and, for each bit of the digest, reveal the secret
corresponding to that bit value (0 or 1); the signature is the sequence of 256
revealed secrets. To verify, hash the message, hash each revealed secret, and
compare against the corresponding public key entries.

- src/main/java/com/thealgorithms/ciphers/LamportSignature.java

- Key pair generation using SecureRandom (256 pairs of 32-byte secrets; public key
  as SHA-256 hashes of the secrets).
- sign() method producing a signature for a given message.
- verify() method validating a message/signature pair against a public key.
- Constant structure with no external dependencies (java.security only).
- Input validation for:
  - null message, signature, or keys
  - malformed signature length (must contain exactly 256 secrets)
  - attempting to sign a second message with the same key pair (one-time property
    enforced with a usage flag)

- src/test/java/com/thealgorithms/ciphers/LamportSignatureTest.java

- A valid signature verifies successfully.
- A tampered message is rejected.
- A tampered signature is rejected.
- A signature does not verify under a different key pair.
- Signing a second message with the same key pair throws an exception.
- Tests for null/invalid inputs and exception handling.

- The implementation will include Javadocs describing the algorithm, why it is
  considered quantum-resistant, the one-time usage limitation (each signature
  reveals half of the private key, so a key pair must never sign two different
  messages), a note that the implementation is for educational purposes only, and
  a reference to the Wikipedia article
  (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamport_signature).

### Additional Information

I searched the repository and existing pull requests and could not find any Lamport
signature or other post-quantum algorithm implementation in the Java repository.

If this proposal is accepted, I'd be happy to implement the algorithm along with
comprehensive JUnit 5 tests and documentation following the repository's coding
standards. This could also serve as the starting point for a small series of
hash-based post-quantum algorithms (Winternitz OTS, Merkle Signature Scheme),
which I would propose in separate issues if maintainers are interested.

issue_title: Claude shrink hook: `allow` decision, changed command text and lost input fields
issue_description:
**What happen**

In `compress` mode, the Claude Code `PreToolUse` shrink hook rewrites a Bash command to `<caveman> shrink -- <command>`. The source shows three defects:

1. **Approval.** The hook returns `permissionDecision: "allow"` for each command that its filter accepts. The filter accepts commands that change state, for example `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, `kubectl delete`, `aws` and `gh`.
2. **Changed command text.** Permission rules evaluate the rewritten input. A rule such as `Bash(git push:*)` can then stop matching the command. Removing `allow` does not fix this defect.
3. **Lost input fields.** `updatedInput` contains only `command`. The hook reference states that `updatedInput` replaces the whole input. Thus the input loses `timeout`, `run_in_background` and `description`.

I verified the source part of this report. I did not verify the host behavior yet. Each host statement below is a prediction from the Claude Code documentation until the host tests run.

#### 1. The hook returns `allow`

The Claude Code output of `shrinkHook` is:

```ts
{ hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision: "allow", updatedInput: { command: rewritten } } }
```

`shouldShrink` accepts a command whose first word is in `SHRINK_ALLOW`:

```
git cargo go npm pnpm yarn pip pip3 pytest make jest vitest tsc eslint mypy ruff pylint mvn gradle
dotnet rspec bundle grep rg ag egrep fgrep find ls tree du df ps docker kubectl terraform helm
aws gcloud az gh
```

The filter rejects shell operators and some streaming flags. It excludes a few first-two-token pairs, for example `git commit`, `docker exec` and `terraform apply`. The pair check reads only the first two tokens, so a global option before the subcommand passes the filter:

- `git -C . commit` passes, although the filter excludes `git commit`.
- `docker --context example exec example id` passes, although the filter excludes `docker exec`.

The streaming pattern rejects `-f`, so `git push -f` does not pass. `git push --force` passes.

The hook reference states that deny and ask rules still apply after a hook returns `allow`. Thus the predicted effect is narrower than "every accepted command runs without a prompt". Where no rule covers the command and the permission mode asks, the `allow` decision can remove that prompt.

The code comment above `shrinkHook` describes the same risk for Codex (#1037). The fix for #1037 removed Codex from the hook. The Claude Code branch still returns `allow`.

#### 2. The rewrite changes the text that rules match

The rewritten command is:

```
'<path to caveman>' shrink -- git push --dry-run origin main
```

The hook reference states that permission rules evaluate the rewritten input. A rule for `Bash(git push:*)` can then stop matching the command. This defect stays after the fix removes `allow`. This report makes no claim about other `PreToolUse` hooks. Matching hooks run in parallel, and the reference does not state that one hook receives the output of another.

I saw this problem in one Claude Code session. That session entered a git worktree through the `EnterWorktree` tool. In it, a plain `git status` was refused with this message:

> This session is isolated in the worktree ..., but this command runs caveman with a git command among its operands: what runs it, and from which directory or root, cannot be read here (name git right after the launcher and its options) ... Refusing to run it

Git worked again after I set `think.mode` to `record`. I did not record the Claude Code version. The component that produced the refusal is not known. The host tests below check if the refusal depends on the rewrite.

#### 3. The rewrite loses input fields

`updatedInput` is `{ command: rewritten }`. The hook reference states that `updatedInput` replaces the whole input. An input with `timeout`, `run_in_background` or `description` loses these fields. This changes how the command runs, not only how rules match it.

**Expected**

- The shrink hook returns no permission decision. The normal permission flow of Claude Code decides.
- Permission rules match the original command. If the host cannot match rules against the original command, the hook does not rewrite it.
- The rewrite copies each input field and changes only `command`.
- Two decisions stay separate: which commands have output that the hook can compress, and which permission decision applies. The hook makes only the first decision.

#### Proposed fix

1. Remove `permissionDecision: "allow"` from the Claude Code output of `shrinkHook`. If the host requires a decision together with `updatedInput`, stop the rewrite for Claude Code, as #1037 did for Codex.
2. Copy the original `tool_input` into `updatedInput` and replace only `command`.
3. Keep rule matching on the rewritten text safe. If the hook cannot do this, do not rewrite commands that a permission rule can cover.
4. Make the filter read the subcommand after global options, or remove the exclusion pairs together with the `allow` decision.

Acceptance criteria, one for each defect:

- Approval: with the hook present, a command without a matching rule gives the same prompt as with the hook absent.
- Rule matching: an ask rule and a deny rule for the original command apply with the hook present.
- Input fields: each input field except `command` is equal before and after the rewrite.
- Filter: tests include global options before the subcommand, for example `git -C . commit`, and flags that write, for example `git diff --output=file`.

**Before/after example**

```
Input: git push --force origin main
Got:   {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse", "permissionDecision": "allow",
        "updatedInput": {"command": "'<path to caveman>' shrink -- git push --force origin main"}}}
Want:  {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
        "updatedInput": {<all original input fields>, "command": "<rewritten command>"}}}
       with no permission decision, and permission rules that still match the original command.
       If the host cannot match rules against the original command, no rewrite.
```

**Platform**
- [x] Claude Code
- [ ] Codex
- [ ] Other: ___

**Version / install method**

caveman v2.7.0: the global npm CLI `@caveman-ai/cli` with the native Claude Code integration, which writes the `caveman shrink-hook` `PreToolUse` entry into `~/.claude/settings.json`. Source details:

- caveman v2.7.0, plugin cache `caveman/caveman/2.7.0`
- `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, SHA-256 `83d332977a47d3bc281b3780819519ba779409fa41e04964d59c1f1d4a354d35`
- `SHRINK_ALLOW` at line 13864, `shouldShrink` at lines 13877–13893, and the `shrinkHook` output at line 13940
- `main` on 2026-09-28, with the same code (line numbers on `main` can change).

## Reproduction

### Source part (verified)

Run the extracted `shouldShrink` and `shrinkHook` functions of the pinned file above with simulated input, configuration, executable lookup and output. Do not run the command strings. The source part shows:

- the `allow` decision for `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, `kubectl delete`, `aws s3 rm` and `gh repo delete`
- the two filter bypasses above
- an `updatedInput` that contains only `command`

### Host part (not run yet)

Fixture:

- A source repository and a bare destination repository, both new, in a temporary directory.
- `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, so no user or system Git configuration applies.
- In the local configuration of both repositories: `core.hooksPath` set to an empty directory, `protocol.allow=never` and `protocol.file.allow=always`. Thus no Git hook, remote helper or external transport runs. A local `git push --dry-run` can run a `pre-push` hook, so this control is necessary.
- The command text is `git push --dry-run origin main`, with no `-c` option, because a `-c` option changes the tokens that `shouldShrink` reads.
- Before each case, the fixture makes sure that the remote references are unchanged and the hooks directory is empty.

Record for each run: the Claude Code version, the permission mode, the permission rules and the active hooks.

Conditions. Each condition runs in a new session with the same permission mode and the same rules:

- A: no shrink hook.
- B: the hook as released: `allow` and the rewritten `updatedInput`.
- C: the same rewritten `updatedInput` and no `permissionDecision`.
- D: `allow` and an `updatedInput` equal to the original input.

Comparisons. Each pair changes one thing only:

- Approval defect: B against C, and D against A.
- Rewrite defect: C against A, and B against D.
- Rule matching: the rewrite comparisons, in a case with an ask rule and a case with a deny rule. A case without a matching rule gives evidence only for the approval comparisons.
- Input fields: a separate case whose original input has `command`, `timeout`, `run_in_background` and `description`. It compares the input that the tool receives in C with the original input. The permission cases use an input with `command` only.
- Worktree refusal: the rewrite comparisons in a worktree session. A refusal in B and C, and none in A and D, connects the refusal to the rewrite. It does not name the component that refuses.

For each case and condition, record these items:

- The original command
- The rewritten command
- If a prompt appeared
- If the command ran
- The input fields that the tool received

## Workaround

```bash
caveman config set think.shrink false
caveman doctor claude --fix
```

After these commands, `~/.claude/settings.json` has no `shrink-hook` entry, and the other caveman hooks stay. You can also set `think.mode` to `record`, but that setting turns off all compression.

## Related

- #1037: Codex re-prompts for already-approved commands after the shrink rewrite. The fix removed Codex from the hook.
- #1049: the native install always added the shrink hook. The fix made `think.shrink=false` work. That issue notes that the `allow` decision widens the permission grant on Codex.

issue_title: syscall: update Windows SysProcAttr for recent process creation features
issue_description:
### Proposal Details

I propose to update syscall.SysProcAttr on Windows to let callers control the following process creation parameters:

 - The job object list for the new process.
 - The console for the new process.
 - The desktop for the new process.
 - The AppContainer configuration for the new process.
 - (**Added, July 28**) The [experimental sandbox](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/createprocessinsandbox) configuration for the new process.

In general package syscall is frozen. However, one exception is details that affect process creation through os/exec, because otherwise the only way to make such calls is to fork both syscall and os/exec.

The API change is these new fields in syscall.SysProcAttr on Windows:

```
	Jobs                       []Handle            // if non-nil, start the process with this job object list
	Console                    Handle              // if non-zero, start the process connected to this console
	Desktop                    string              // if non-empty, start the process on the named desktop
	AppContainer               *AppContainer       // if set, create AppContainer process with this metadata
	Sandbox                    *Sandbox            // if non-nil, start the process in the described sandbox
```

And a new type, AppContainer:

```
// An AppContainer defines parameters for creating a process in an AppContainer.
// It is a safe Go version of the Windows SECURITY_CAPABILITIES structure.
// See https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/ns-winnt-security_capabilities.
type AppContainer struct {
	SID          *SID
	Capabilities []SIDAndAttributes
 }
```

We could instead define SecurityCapabilities to be the literal Windows struct, but that Windows struct is unsafe and also may possibly change in the future. The #if in the documentation page definition look scary. It seemed cleaner to give it an appropriate name and use a Go slice. Then if the actual struct passed to the Windows call varies by OS version, that's an implementation detail and not an API detail.

And also a new type Sandbox (**added July 28**):

```
// A Sandbox defines parameters for creating a process in an experimental sandbox.
// See https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthz/createprocessinsandbox.
type Sandbox struct {
    Identity string  // sandbox name
    Spec     []byte  // FlatBuffer-encoded specification; see Microsoft docs
}
```

That is the entire API change. I have used the AppContainer part of this API successfully to implement basic sandboxing of Windows programs using AppContainer. I have not used the Sandbox part since Microsoft has not yet enabled the API on my Windows system (you can call it but it says not supported), but given the recent launch of https://github.com/microsoft/mxc, it seems likely they will enable it in the coming six months, so having it ready for the Feb 2027 Go release seems worthwhile.

There is no support in package syscall for constructing a sandbox spec. We could add that instead to golang.org/x/sys/windows, where it can be more easily updated. This proposal is concerned with the minimal amount necessary to enable use of the new functionality through os/exec.

The AppContainer details in this proposal are a safer version of the accepted proposal #65611. I suggest we do the API in this proposal _instead of_ #65611, because in general we keep syscall.SysProcAttr type-safe, even on Windows. 

The job object details in this proposal mostly match the undiscussed proposal #79927.

The desktop details in this proposal address the feature requested in #42836.

The implementation (except for Sandbox) is at [CL 801640](https://go-review.googlesource.com/c/go/+/801640).

issue_description:

we have fixed it.

🎁 Enhancement (please don't include this emoji/text, just add your details)
Please start by describing the problem that you are trying to solve. There may already
be a solution, or there may be a way to solve it that you hadn't considered.


TIP: You can always edit your issue if it isn't formatted correctly.
     See https://guides.github.com/features/mastering-markdown 
-->
### Problem
I currently find it quite difficult to manage composable configuration when using Kubernetes with Spring Boot.

a single kubernetes ConfigMap makes it easy to mount all contained configuration files (effectively behaving as a wildcard), but they can only be mounted into a single directory.

Spring Boot, on the other hand, mainly supports importing a wildcard of directories, with each directory containing a single application.yaml.

These two approaches are incompatible and you can't simply use wildcards end-to-end. There are several ways to workaround this (either mount the files in the "wildcard" format of kubernetes, but also pass the list of files to springboot; or mount the files in the "wildcard" format of springboot, but this requires explicitly listing all the file at the volumemount site) but in both cases you need to explicitely list all files. I find it rather cumbersome and error-prone.

I'm not sure where the better fix would be. Could Spring Boot make it easier to consume multiple configuration files from a single directory, in a way that matches how ConfigMaps are naturally mounted? Or do you think it should be Kubernetes job to provide a more convenient way to mount a ConfigMap in the layout expected by Spring Boot — one directory per file, with inside the right filename?

### Exemple 
as a concrete example, imagine 3 spring boot deployments, a shared configmap, each one its specific configmap.
you have multiple deployments variants, so you're configuration has to be composable. Maybe in some cases you want to add a new timeout config file to all, and maybe a database connection credentials for 2 of the 3 microservices that use the database

You have multiple possibilities:
- change the volumemounts:
  -  add the files to the corresponding existing configmap, and also at the volumemount level list all files to be mounted in subpaths (e.g. at  /config/timeouts/application.yaml, /config/database/application.yaml)
  - OR create new configmaps, modify the volumemounts of each microservice to mount to the correct folder /config/timeout and /config/database
- put the files in the existing configmap and wildcard mount them, and get spring boot to read them by listing them explicitely (many ways to do this, using files or env vars or command line flags, activating profiles, setting confignames, or spring.config.additional-location pointing to the files or import: directives in an existing files; or even run init containers just to move things around)

There are probably many more but arguably no simple solution ? What do you think ?

ps: I'm working on this in the context of a kustomize deployments using components, but that's kind of at a higher level than the configuration problem
ps2: as far as i understand, configtrees don't help with this, they only allow to work with configmaps that are "springkey": "value" instead of "filenamekey": "filenamecontent"

issue_title: Same-session tool-set churn (identical tool count, different membership) defeats prompt-cache reuse
issue_description:
**Summary.** On one Windows host (OpenClaw 2026.9.3, `tools.profile=coding`, no `tools.allow`/`tools.deny`, model `deepseek/deepseek-flash`), a single `agent:main:dashboard:*` session alternates **between runs** among several tool sets: 54, 50, 43A, 43B, 46, 42 and 39. Two of them have **exactly the same tool count (43) but different membership**:

- **43A only:** `message, progress_card, session_status, sessions_send`
- **43B only:** `intent, portal, sessions, terminal`
- **39 = exactly `43A ∩ 43B`** (observed once) → the two groups toggle independently on top of a 39-tool base.

Because the tool list is part of the cached prefix, each flip invalidates the prompt cache for the next request.

**Evidence.** 2,161 `cache:state` snapshots from `cache-trace.jsonl`:

- **0 of 260 runs** change the tool set *within* a run → the variation is **attempt-level**, not mid-run.
- **28 same-session cross-run changes in 49 h**, all in dashboard/main sessions.
- `cache:result.options.changes` reports `"tool set changed with same count"` **67 times** (usually paired with `"system prompt digest changed"`).
- Exact set identity is stable per attempt *kind* where the kind is explicit in the run id (`announce:requester-settle:*` → 50, `skill-workshop-review:*` → 54, `openclaw-turn-*` → 1), i.e. explicit kinds are deterministic while ordinary agent turns are not. Bucketing ordinary dashboard/main runs by request count still yields multiple sets inside one bucket (8 of 29 buckets are multi-set, ≈82 runs); the sharpest case is **all 17 single-request runs split across 4 different sets** (54×7, 43A×8, 50×1, 39×1).

**Source-level observation.** `resolveCodingToolConstructionPlanForAllowlist(toolsAllow)` (`dist/attempt-tool-construction-plan-*.mjs` L68-92) returns the full plan (`ALL_CODING_TOOL_CONSTRUCTION_PLAN`) only when `toolsAllow` is **absent**; otherwise `includeChannelTools` / `includeOpenClawTools` are derived from which core tool families the allowlist matches, and `includeChannelTools === includePluginTools`. The assembly then gates `listChannelAgentTools(...)` and `createOpenClawTools(...)` on those flags (`dist/agent-tools-*.mjs` L557-560). No `tools.*` config input reaches this function — the only input is the per-attempt `toolsAllow`.

**Requests**

1. **Trace the source of the per-attempt allowlist on non-cron (dashboard/webchat) sessions.** Which of `attempt.toolsAllow` / `inheritedToolAllowlist` / `cronCreatorToolAllowlist` / `scheduledToolPolicy` injects it, and under what condition? We can only account for cron jobs (whose `payload.toolsAllow` explains their sets) — cron jobs are *different sessions* and do not share the prefix cache, so they are not the cause here.
2. **Make tool construction deterministic per (agent, session, surface) within a session**, or surface the reason when it is not. Today the same session flips between set variants on ordinary turns.
3. **Record tool-policy provenance per run.** `cache:state.options.snapshot` carries `provider / modelId / modelApi / streamStrategy / transport / systemPromptDigest / toolDigest / toolCount / toolNames` but **no policy provenance**. One field naming the source of the effective allowlist (e.g. `payload | agent | profile | inherited | cronCreator | scheduledToolPolicy | none`) plus the resolved construction-plan flags would make this root-causable from local data. Right now `resolveCodingToolConstructionPlanForAllowlist()` cannot be traced back to its input.
4. **Redaction gate in the cache trace.** The gate drops the prompt when it looks like JSON and exceeds ~16 KB by shape. In the same 2,161-snapshot window only **8 runs** kept a usable `system` prompt (the rest are a 36-char `[Oversized diagnostic JSON redacted]` placeholder), which blocks section-level diffing — e.g. **no 43A run has a readable prompt at all**. Prefer gating on actual secret content rather than on shape/size.

**Environment note.** Reproduced with a stock `coding` profile and no allow/deny lists, so this is not caused by local policy configuration. Local diagnostics only; no configuration change produced the variation (no config edits in the window).

*(Filed from local, read-only diagnostics. Happy to attach the analysis scripts or run any instrumented build you point us at.)*
